title: Energy-Resolved Polarization Catalog of High-Count BH-XRBs
description: This project creates a systematic energy-resolved polarization catalog of high-exposure BH-XRB observations (>150 ks each), using standard IXPE PCUBE analysis with merged DU event files to measure PD, PA, and MDP99 in two energy bands (2-5 keV, 5-8 keV). We test for energy-dependent polarization using chi-squared comparisons in the (q,u) plane for all observations with secure broadband detections, applying the test to the Gaussian-distributed Stokes parameters irrespective of sub-band detection status. Novel publishable results include: (1) the first systematic catalog of energy-resolved normalized Stokes parameters in high-count BH-XRB observations with proper statistical treatment, (2) quantification of energy-dependent polarization evolution in the (q,u) plane with rigorous significance assessment, and (3) population-level comparison of low-energy vs high-energy polarization signatures across multiple epochs for LMC X-3.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND FEASIBILITY CHECK
For each source and obs_id listed, locate Level-2 event files for all three DUs from the local archive. Verify file existence. Selected observations have exposures >150 ks:
- 4U 1630-47: 01250401 (459 ks)
- LMC X-1: 02001901 (563 ks)
- LMC X-3: 02006599 (457 ks), 03004899 (385 ks), 03004901 (382 ks), 03005001 (389 ks)
- Swift J1727.8-1613: 03005801 (202 ks), 03006001 (151 ks)
Abort if any dataset is missing.

STEP 2 - PER-DU DATA QUALITY VERIFICATION
For each observation, before merging, perform a per-DU quality check:
(a) Use xselect to extract the count rate from each DU event file in the 2-8 keV band within a 60 arcsec source region.
(b) Compute the mean count rate across the three DUs and the fractional deviation of each DU from the mean.
(c) Flag any DU with fractional deviation > 20% as potentially anomalous.
(d) Record a quality flag for each DU. If all three DUs are consistent, proceed. If one DU is anomalous, exclude it from the merge and document the exclusion. If two or more DUs are anomalous, flag the observation for cautious interpretation but proceed with available data.
Output: DU quality summary table with count rates and flags per observation.

STEP 3 - EVENT FILE MERGING
For each observation, merge the Level-2 event files from all quality-verified DUs into a single combined event file using ftmerge (HEASoft FTOOL). Exclude any DUs flagged as anomalous in STEP 2. Output: one merged event file per observation with a log indicating which DUs were included.

STEP 4 - SOURCE AND BACKGROUND REGION DEFINITION
For each observation, define a circular source region of radius 60 arcsec centered on the source coordinates (following BH-XRB consensus). Define an annular background region with inner radius 180 arcsec and outer radius 240 arcsec. Save region files in DS9 format for use with xpbin.

STEP 5 - BROADBAND PCUBE EXTRACTION (2-8 keV)
For each merged event file, run xpbin with algorithm=PCUBE in the full 2-8 keV band. Apply NEFF weighting. Use the source region from STEP 4. Extract PD, PA, MDP99, and normalized Stokes parameters (q=Q/I, u=U/I) with uncertainties (sigma_q, sigma_u). This establishes the broadband polarization detection status for each observation.

STEP 6 - BROADBAND DETECTION CRITERION CHECK
For each observation, verify whether a secure broadband polarization detection exists: PD > MDP99 (equivalent to >99% confidence). Record detection status. Only observations meeting this broadband criterion will be used for energy-resolved chi-squared testing in STEP 9. Report the number of observations passing this threshold. Observations without broadband detection will have energy-resolved results reported but excluded from chi-squared testing.

STEP 7 - ENERGY-RESOLVED PCUBE EXTRACTION
For each merged event file, run xpbin with algorithm=PCUBE in two energy bands: 2-5 keV and 5-8 keV. Apply NEFF weighting. Use the source region from STEP 4. For each band, extract: PD, PA, MDP99, q, u, sigma_q, sigma_u. Store results in a pandas DataFrame indexed by source, obs_id, energy_band. Note: these measurements are valid regardless of whether PD > MDP99 in each sub-band because q and u are Gaussian-distributed.

STEP 8 - ENERGY-BAND SUMMARY TABLE
For each observation and energy band, record the MDP99 value and the measured PD. Create a summary table indicating the detection status per band (PD > MDP99 or not). This is for informational purposes; it does NOT gate the chi-squared test.

STEP 9 - ENERGY-DEPENDENCE CHI-SQUARED TEST
For observations with secure BROADBAND detections (from STEP 6), regardless of sub-band detection status, perform the energy-dependence test on the Gaussian Stokes parameters:
(a) Compute the inverse-variance weighted mean (q_mean, u_mean) across the two energy bands:
    q_mean = sum(q_j/sigma_qj^2) / sum(1/sigma_qj^2), and similarly for u_mean.
(b) Compute chi-squared = sum_j [(q_j - q_mean)^2/sigma_qj^2 + (u_j - u_mean)^2/sigma_uj^2] with dof = 2*(N_bands - 1) = 2.
(c) Compute p-value from scipy.stats.chi2.sf(chi2, dof).
A p-value < 0.05 indicates significant energy-dependent polarization at 95% confidence. Record chi2, dof, p-value per observation. This test is valid because q and u are Gaussian-distributed with known uncertainties.

STEP 10 - ENERGY GRADIENT QUANTIFICATION (SIGNIFICANT DETECTIONS ONLY)
Only for observations where the chi-squared test in STEP 9 yields p-value < 0.05 (indicating statistically significant energy dependence):
(a) Compute the vector difference in normalized Stokes parameters: Delta_q = q(5-8) - q(2-5), Delta_u = u(5-8) - u(2-5).
(b) Compute uncertainties via error propagation: sigma_Delta_q = sqrt(sigma_q1^2 + sigma_q2^2), and similarly for u.
(c) Compute the magnitude |Delta| = sqrt(Delta_q^2 + Delta_u^2) and its uncertainty using standard error propagation.
(d) Compute the direction of change in the (q,u) plane: theta_Delta = 0.5 * arctan2(Delta_u, Delta_q).
For observations NOT showing significant energy dependence, do NOT compute or report these gradient metrics; instead note 'consistent with no energy dependence' in the output.

STEP 11 - INTRA-SOURCE CONSISTENCY TEST (LMC X-3 MULTI-EPOCH)
For LMC X-3 (4 observations), test inter-epoch consistency in each energy band:
(a) For each energy band (2-5 keV and 5-8 keV), compute the inverse-variance weighted mean (q_mean, u_mean) across all four epochs.
(b) Compute chi-squared = sum_i [(q_i - q_mean)^2/sigma_qi^2 + (u_i - u_mean)^2/sigma_ui^2] where i indexes the 4 observations, with dof = 2*(N_obs - 1) = 6.
(c) Compute p-value from scipy.stats.chi2.sf(chi2, dof).
Output: intra-source consistency table with chi2, dof, p-value per energy band. This tests whether the polarization properties of LMC X-3 vary across epochs.

STEP 12 - VISUALIZATION
(a) For each observation with broadband detection, create (q, u) plane plots showing the two energy bands with error ellipses (1-sigma from sigma_q, sigma_u), color-coded (blue for 2-5 keV, red for 5-8 keV). Include broadband result (black) for reference. Mark observations with significant energy dependence.
(b) For LMC X-3, create a multi-panel (q, u) plot showing all four epochs in each energy band to visualize temporal consistency.
(c) For observations with significant energy dependence only, generate a bar chart of energy gradient magnitudes |Delta| with error bars.
(d) Create a summary figure showing PD vs energy band for each source (with MDP99 indicated as a dashed line for reference).
Save all figures as PNG files with descriptive names.

STEP 13 - RESULTS COMPILATION
(a) Write primary catalog CSV: source, obs_id, energy_band, exposure_ks, DUs_included, q, q_err, u, u_err, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99.
(b) Write broadband detection summary CSV: source, obs_id, broadband_PD, broadband_MDP99, broadband_detected (True/False).
(c) Write energy-dependence test results CSV (for broadband-detected observations only): source, obs_id, chi2_energy_test, dof, p_value, significant_energy_dependence (True if p<0.05). For significant cases only: Delta_q, Delta_q_err, Delta_u, Delta_u_err, gradient_magnitude, gradient_err.
(d) Write LMC X-3 intra-source consistency results CSV: energy_band, chi2, dof, p_value, consistent (True if p>0.05).
(e) Write DU quality verification summary CSV from STEP 2.

conclusions: Processed all 8 high-exposure BH-XRB observations with real NEFF-weighted PCUBE analysis. 5/8 yield secure broadband (2-8 keV) detections (4U 1630-47 PD=8.1%, three LMC X-3 epochs PD=2.4-4.0%, Swift J1727.8-1613/03005801 PD=3.4%); LMC X-1, LMC X-3/03004901, and Swift 03006001 are non-detections. LMC X-3 is consistent across its four epochs in both energy bands (p=0.36 at 2-5 keV, p=0.22 at 5-8 keV). All 24 DUs passed the <20% fractional-deviation quality check; all 3 DUs included for every observation.

title: Intra-Observation Polarization Angle and Degree Stability in Bright BH-XRBs
description: This project quantifies the intra-observation stability of both polarization angle (PA) and polarization degree (PD) in long-exposure BH-XRB observations using time-resolved PCUBE analysis. For each observation, we divide the exposure into orbital-timescale segments (~5 ks), measure PA and PD in each segment, and apply chi-squared constancy tests to identify statistically significant variability in either quantity. Because PD is positively biased in the low-significance regime, the model-independent normalized Stokes parameters (Q/I, U/I) provide the statistically robust joint test, while the direct PA and PD constancy tests give the physically interpretable per-quantity assessment. Novel publishable results include: (1) a systematic catalog of PA and PD stability metrics for 6 high-exposure BH-XRB observations spanning 110-563 ks, (2) identification of any observations showing significant PA wander or PD variability beyond statistical noise, and (3) upper limits on PA and PD variability amplitude for sources consistent with constant polarization, constraining the geometric and physical stability of the polarization-producing regions.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL: Verify availability of Level-2 event files for all 6 observations: Cyg X-1 (01002901, 03002599), Swift J1727.8-1613 (03005801, 03006001), 4U 1630-47 (01250401), LMC X-1 (02001901). Confirm presence of ixpe_*_det1_evt2.fits, ixpe_*_det2_evt2.fits, ixpe_*_det3_evt2.fits for each obs_id. These observations range from 110 to 563 ks exposure, providing sufficient statistics for time-resolved polarimetry.

STEP 2 - SOURCE REGION DEFINITION AND EVENT EXTRACTION: For each observation:
  (a) Use xselect to define a circular source region of 60 arcsec radius centered on source coordinates.
  (b) Merge DU1, DU2, DU3 event files using xselect into a single combined event list.
  (c) Filter events to 2-8 keV energy range using xselect.
  Output: One filtered, merged event file per observation.

STEP 3 - TIME-RESOLVED POLARIZATION ANALYSIS: For each observation:
  (a) Determine total Good Time Interval (GTI) exposure and divide into N segments of approximately 5 ks each.
  (b) For each time segment, run xpbin with algorithm=PCUBE to generate a polarization cube using NEFF weighting.
  (c) Extract from each PCUBE: PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, and normalized Stokes parameters Q/I, U/I with errors.
  (d) Record segment start time (MJD), stop time, and effective exposure.
  Output per observation: N PCUBE files and a time-series table with columns [segment_id, t_start_mjd, t_stop_mjd, exposure_s, PD_pct, PD_err, PA_deg, PA_err, QI, QI_err, UI, UI_err, MDP99].

STEP 4 - OBSERVATION-INTEGRATED POLARIZATION: For each observation:
  (a) Run xpbin with algorithm=PCUBE on the full merged event file to obtain observation-averaged PD, PA, Q/I, U/I with errors.
  (b) Compute MDP99 for the full observation.
  (c) Record detection significance as PD/sigma_PD.
  Output: Integrated polarization parameters for each observation.

STEP 5 - PA AND PD CONSTANCY TESTS: For each observation:
  (a) Compile the time-series of PA and PD measurements from Step 3.
  (b) PA constancy: perform weighted chi-squared test chi2_PA = sum[(PA_i - PA_mean)^2 / PA_err_i^2], where PA_mean is the weighted mean PA.
  (c) PD constancy: perform weighted chi-squared test chi2_PD = sum[(PD_i - PD_mean)^2 / PD_err_i^2], where PD_mean is the weighted mean PD.
  (d) Compute degrees of freedom dof = N_segments - 1 for each test.
  (e) Calculate p-values from chi2 and dof using scipy.stats.chi2.sf for both PA and PD.
  (f) Flag observation as showing significant PA variability if p_value_PA < 0.01, and significant PD variability if p_value_PD < 0.01 (99% confidence).
  (g) CAVEAT: PD is a positively-biased quantity in the low-significance regime (PD/PD_err < ~3) and its distribution departs from Gaussian, so the chi2_PD test is only approximate when segment significances are low. Interpret chi2_PD alongside the model-independent Q/I, U/I constancy test of Step 6, which is unbiased and is the statistically robust joint reference.
  Output per observation: chi2_PA, chi2_PD, dof, p_value_PA, p_value_PD, pa_variability_flag, pd_variability_flag.

STEP 6 - STOKES PARAMETER CONSTANCY TEST (UNBIASED JOINT REFERENCE): For each observation:
  (a) Perform weighted chi-squared test for constancy of Q/I time series: chi2_QI = sum[(QI_i - QI_mean)^2 / QI_err_i^2].
  (b) Perform weighted chi-squared test for constancy of U/I time series: chi2_UI = sum[(UI_i - UI_mean)^2 / UI_err_i^2].
  (c) Compute combined 2D chi-squared: chi2_2D = chi2_QI + chi2_UI with dof_2D = 2*(N_segments - 1).
  (d) Calculate p-values for each test. Because Q/I and U/I are approximately Gaussian and unbiased, the 2D test is the primary, model-independent verdict on whether the polarization vector (PA and PD jointly) is constant.
  Output per observation: chi2_QI, chi2_UI, chi2_2D, p_value_QI, p_value_UI, p_value_2D.

STEP 7 - PA AND PD VARIABILITY AMPLITUDE QUANTIFICATION: For each observation:
  (a) Compute standard deviation of measured PA values (sigma_PA_measured) and of measured PD values (sigma_PD_measured).
  (b) Compute expected statistical scatter: sigma_PA_expected = sqrt(mean(PA_err_i^2)) and sigma_PD_expected = sqrt(mean(PD_err_i^2)).
  (c) If sigma_measured > sigma_expected for a quantity, compute intrinsic scatter sigma_intrinsic = sqrt(sigma_measured^2 - sigma_expected^2), separately for PA and PD.
  (d) Otherwise, report sigma_intrinsic as an upper limit (sigma_intrinsic < sigma_expected), separately for PA and PD.
  (e) Compute peak-to-peak ranges: PA_range = PA_max - PA_min and PD_range = PD_max - PD_min.
  Output: sigma_PA_intrinsic (or upper limit), sigma_PD_intrinsic (or upper limit), PA_range, PD_range.

STEP 8 - STRUCTURE FUNCTION ANALYSIS: For each observation with N >= 10 segments:
  (a) Compute first-order structure function of PA: SF_PA(tau) = <(PA(t+tau) - PA(t))^2>, and of PD: SF_PD(tau) = <(PD(t+tau) - PD(t))^2>.
  (b) Compute each SF at lag tau = 5 ks, 10 ks, 20 ks (if exposure permits).
  (c) Test for any trend in SF with lag that would indicate correlated PA or PD wandering.
  Output: PA and PD structure function values at each lag.

STEP 9 - CROSS-SOURCE COMPARISON: Compile results from all 6 observations into summary table.
  (a) Rank observations by PA constancy p-value and, separately, by PD constancy p-value to identify the most/least stable sources in each quantity.
  (b) Compute correlation between integrated MDP99 and chi2_PA/dof, and between MDP99 and chi2_PD/dof, using Spearman rank to check whether apparent variability is driven by measurement precision.
  (c) Compare mean intrinsic PA scatter and mean intrinsic PD scatter (or upper limits) between sources.
  (d) Identify whether any source shows variability in one quantity but not the other (e.g., stable PA with variable PD, or vice versa), which would help distinguish purely geometric reorientation from changes in scattering optical depth / emission-region physics.

STEP 10 - VISUALIZATION: Generate diagnostic and publication-quality figures using matplotlib:
  (a) Time-series plots for each observation with stacked panels sharing a common time axis: PA vs time and PD vs time, with error bars, overplotting the weighted mean as a horizontal line in each panel.
  (b) Q/I vs U/I Stokes plane plots for each observation showing all time segments as points with error ellipses, color-coded by time (this jointly visualizes PA and PD evolution).
  (c) Histograms of reduced chi-squared values (chi2_PA/dof and chi2_PD/dof) across all observations.
  (d) Summary figures: PA scatter vs observation duration and PD scatter vs observation duration for all sources.
  (e) Structure function plots SF_PA(tau) and SF_PD(tau) for observations with sufficient segments.

STEP 11 - OUTPUT PRODUCTS:
  (a) Master results table: pa_pd_stability_catalog.csv with columns [source, obs_id, exposure_ks, n_segments, PD_integrated, PD_integrated_err, PA_integrated, PA_integrated_err, chi2_PA, p_value_PA, chi2_PD, p_value_PD, dof, chi2_2D, p_value_2D, sigma_PA_intrinsic, sigma_PD_intrinsic, PA_range_deg, PD_range_pct, pa_variability_flag, pd_variability_flag].
  (b) Time-series data files per observation: {obs_id}_polarization_timeseries.csv with per-segment PA and PD measurements.
  (c) Summary statistics: pa_pd_variability_summary.txt reporting which observations pass/fail the PA and PD constancy tests at 99% confidence.
  (d) Publication-quality figures: pa_pd_timeseries_all.pdf, stokes_plane_evolution.pdf, chi2_histograms.pdf, structure_function.pdf.

conclusions: All 6 BH-XRB observations processed with real per-segment PCUBEs (independent time-sliced extractions via red_ixpe.pcube tmin/tmax). PD is intra-observation constant in every observation (upper limits only). The robust, unbiased 2D q,u constancy test flags genuine intra-observation Stokes-vector variability in exactly one observation: Swift J1727.8-1613 ObsID 03006001 (p_2D=0.004). PA-only tests also flag 03005801 and LMC X-1 02001901, but those are non-detection / low-significance cases where PA is near the q-u coordinate singularity and the unbiased 2D test confirms constancy. Cyg X-1 (both epochs) and 4U 1630-47 are securely stable.

title: Flux-Hardness-Polarization Correlations in Multi-Epoch BH-XRB Observations
description: This project systematically quantifies correlations between model-independent polarization (PD, PA from PCUBE) and spectral properties (count rate, hardness ratio) across 30 multi-epoch BH-XRB observations spanning five sources. Unlike existing energy-resolved or intra-observation studies, we compute Spearman correlations between epoch-averaged PCUBE-derived PD and contemporaneous hardness ratios (4-8 keV / 2-4 keV) and total count rates extracted using xselect from the same observations. The novelty is the first systematic cross-epoch correlation analysis between polarization and spectral hardness for multiple BH-XRBs using purely model-independent measurements, testing whether harder spectral states exhibit systematically different polarization. Sources span both persistent (Cyg X-1, LMC X-3) and transient (Swift J1727.8-1613, Cyg X-3) systems with sufficient epochs (2-12) for correlation analysis, plus GX 339-4 for additional sampling.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL
Locate Level-2 event files (*evt2*) from the local IXPE archive for all observations listed: Cyg X-1 (12 obs: 01002901, 01250101, 02008201, 02008301, 02008401, 02008501, 02008601, 03002201, 03003101, 03010001, 03010101, 03002599), Swift J1727.8-1613 (8 obs: 02250901, 02251001, 02251101, 02251201, 02251301, 03005701, 03006001, 03005801), LMC X-3 (4 obs: 02006599, 03004899, 03004901, 03005001), GX 339-4 (2 obs: 03005101, 03005301), Cyg X-3 (4 obs: 02001899, 02250301, 02009101, 03250301). Verify all 30 observations exist. Decompress gzipped files to working directory if needed.

STEP 2 - PER-DU PCUBE POLARIZATION EXTRACTION
For each observation and EACH DU separately (DU1, DU2, DU3), run ixpeobssim.core.pipeline.xpbin with algorithm='PCUBE' on the individual DU event files using energy range 2-8 keV (emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1). Use a 60 arcsec circular source region centered on the source. Do NOT specify irfname; let ixpeobssim auto-resolve from event headers. This produces 3 PCUBE files per observation.

STEP 3 - COMBINED STOKES PARAMETER EXTRACTION
For each observation, read the three per-DU PCUBE outputs using ixpeobssim.binning.polarization.xBinnedPolarizationCube class. Extract the normalized Stokes parameters (q=Q/I, u=U/I), their errors, and effective counts (NEFF) from each DU using the class accessors. Combine the three DUs using error-weighted averaging of q and u: q_combined = sum(q_i/sigma_i^2) / sum(1/sigma_i^2), with sigma_combined = 1/sqrt(sum(1/sigma_i^2)). Compute combined PD = sqrt(q_combined^2 + u_combined^2), PA = 0.5*arctan2(u_combined, q_combined), and propagate errors. Also extract and sum MDP99 across DUs following standard combination.

STEP 4 - DETECTION SIGNIFICANCE
For each observation, compute the statistical significance of the polarization detection as S = PD / PD_ERR. Flag observations with S > 3.0 as secure detections (corresponding to >99.7% confidence for a 2D Gaussian). Record detection status (True/False), significance S, and MDP99 for reference.

STEP 5 - COUNT RATE AND HARDNESS RATIO EXTRACTION WITH XSELECT
For each observation and each DU, use HEASoft xselect to extract source spectra from the Level-2 event files. Define a 60 arcsec circular source region. In xselect: (a) read the event file, (b) filter on region, (c) extract counts in 2-4 keV (soft) and 4-8 keV (hard) bands, (d) record exposure time from the output. Alternatively, use ixpeobssim xpselect with appropriate region and energy filtering. Sum counts across all three DUs. Compute total 2-8 keV count rate = (soft_counts + hard_counts) / total_exposure. Compute hardness ratio HR = hard_counts / soft_counts. Propagate Poisson errors: sigma_counts = sqrt(N), sigma_rate = sqrt(N)/T, sigma_HR via standard error propagation of ratio. Record MJD midpoint from DATE-OBS/DATE-END keywords.

STEP 6 - FEASIBILITY CHECK
Before correlation analysis, report per-source: N_epochs, N_detections (S > 3), median PD, median PD_err. Flag sources where N_epochs < 3 as having insufficient epochs for robust correlation analysis. Continue analysis for all sources but note caveats for GX 339-4 (2 epochs).

STEP 7 - SPEARMAN CORRELATION: PD vs HARDNESS RATIO
For each source with N >= 3 epochs (Cyg X-1, Swift J1727.8-1613, LMC X-3, Cyg X-3), compute Spearman rank correlation coefficient between PD and HR using scipy.stats.spearmanr. Use ALL epochs regardless of detection status to avoid selection bias. Report rho and two-sided p-value. For GX 339-4 (N=2), report only descriptive statistics (values, difference).

STEP 8 - SPEARMAN CORRELATION: PD vs COUNT RATE
For each source with N >= 3 epochs, compute Spearman rank correlation between PD and total 2-8 keV count rate using scipy.stats.spearmanr on ALL epochs. Report rho and p-value. This tests whether brighter states show different polarization independent of spectral shape.

STEP 9 - PA PREFERRED DIRECTION TEST
For each source with N >= 3 epochs, test whether PA clusters around a preferred direction across epochs (indicating a persistent geometry) or is scattered. Convert PA to unit vectors on the circle: x_i = cos(2*PA_i), y_i = sin(2*PA_i). Compute the Rayleigh test statistic R = (1/N)*sqrt((sum(x_i))^2 + (sum(y_i))^2) and its p-value using scipy.stats or astropy.stats. A small p-value indicates PA is NOT uniformly distributed but clusters around a preferred direction. Report mean PA direction and concentration parameter.

STEP 10 - MULTI-PARAMETER SUMMARY TABLE
Create summary table per source with columns: source, N_epochs, N_detections, median_PD, median_PD_err, HR_range (min-max), rate_range (min-max), rho_PD_HR, p_PD_HR, rho_PD_rate, p_PD_rate, Rayleigh_R, Rayleigh_pvalue, mean_PA. Flag correlations with p < 0.05 as nominally significant (noting multiple comparison caveat).

STEP 11 - VISUALIZATION
Generate per source: (a) PD vs HR scatter plot with error bars and Spearman rho annotation, points color-coded by detection significance S; (b) PD vs count rate scatter plot with error bars; (c) PA vs MJD time series with error bars; (d) polar plot showing PA distribution across epochs with error wedges. Create summary figure comparing Spearman rho_PD_HR values across all five sources with 95% confidence intervals.

STEP 12 - OUTPUT
Save to CSV: (1) per_observation_table.csv with columns: source, obs_id, mjd, exposure_ks, count_rate, count_rate_err, HR, HR_err, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, significance_S, detection_flag; (2) per_source_summary.csv with correlation statistics and Rayleigh test results. Save all figures as PNG files with descriptive filenames.

title: Structure Function Analysis of Stokes Q/U Variability in BH-XRBs
description: This project characterizes Stokes Q and U variability timescales in BH-XRBs by computing structure functions (SFs) on the un-normalized, Gaussian-distributed Stokes parameters Q and U extracted from time-segmented PCUBE outputs. All BH-XRBs with exposure >150 ks are included for intra-observation SF analysis: 4U 1630-47 (458 ks), 4U 1957+115 (571+692 ks), Cyg X-1 (241 ks), Cyg X-3 (275 ks), LMC X-1 (563 ks), LMC X-3 (457-389 ks each), Swift J1727.8-1613 (150-202 ks), SS 433 (387 ks), SS 433 WEST (247+745 ks), IGR J17091-3624 (163 ks), and GS 1354-64 (150+452 ks). Long observations are segmented into 15-30 ks bins; final MDP99 per segment is determined by xpbin output rather than approximation. Multi-epoch Discrete Correlation Function analysis is restricted to sources with ≥6 observations (Cyg X-1: 12 obs; Swift J1727.8-1613: 8 obs); sources with 4 epochs use chi-squared tests only. Observations are classified by spectral hardness into hard, intermediate, and soft states for cross-state comparison. This systematic SF analysis of Stokes Q/U variability timescales across spectral states in BH-XRBs is novel and publishable.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT: Verify availability of all specified obs_ids in the local Level-2 archive. For each observation, locate DU1/DU2/DU3 event files (*_det1_evt2.fits.gz, *_det2_evt2.fits.gz, *_det3_evt2.fits.gz). Decompress to a working directory. Using astropy.io.fits, read GTI extension and compute total good time T_exp. Compute total 2-8 keV source counts N_tot within r=60 arcsec of source coordinates (RA_OBJ, DEC_OBJ from header). For T_exp > 150 ks, set T_seg = max(15 ks, T_exp/15) to target at least 10 segments; for 100 < T_exp < 150 ks, set T_seg = T_exp/8. Record feasibility table: obs_id, source_name, T_exp_ks, N_segments, T_seg_ks, N_counts_total. Observations with T_exp < 100 ks are retained only for multi-epoch variability analysis (chi-squared test), not intra-observation SF analysis.

STEP 2 - STATISTICAL POWER VALIDATION VIA MONTE CARLO SIMULATION: Before proceeding, validate that SF slope β can be constrained for representative observation. Select Cyg X-1 01002901 (~240 ks). Using the planned N_segments (e.g., 15) and expected per-segment statistical uncertainty σ_Q (estimated as 1/sqrt(N_counts_per_segment * 0.09), where 0.09 approximates μ²), generate 1000 Monte Carlo realizations: Q_i = Q_0 + cumsum(randn * σ_intrinsic) where σ_intrinsic = σ_Q (i.e., intrinsic variance equals 100% of statistical variance). For each realization, compute SF(τ) = mean[(Q(t+τ) - Q(t))²] for lags τ = 1, 2, ..., floor(N/3). Fit power-law SF(τ) = A * τ^β using scipy.optimize.curve_fit. Compute distribution of recovered β values and report standard deviation σ(β_recovered). If σ(β) > 0.5, increase T_seg (reducing N_segments) until σ(β) < 0.5. Record optimal segmentation parameters.

STEP 3 - TIME-RESOLVED PCUBE GENERATION: For observations with T_exp > 100 ks (qualifying for intra-observation analysis), generate PCUBE for each time segment using ixpeobssim.core.pipeline.xpbin. First, read event file headers to obtain TSTART. Compute segment boundaries: tmin_i = TSTART + i*T_seg, tmax_i = TSTART + (i+1)*T_seg (MET). Call: pipeline.xpbin(*evt_files, algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1, tmin=tmin_i, tmax=tmax_i). Do NOT specify irfname; allow auto-resolution from headers. Store output paths. Also generate one full-observation PCUBE for reference. For observations < 100 ks used only in multi-epoch analysis, generate only the full-observation PCUBE.

STEP 4 - STOKES Q AND U EXTRACTION FROM PCUBE: Read each PCUBE output using ixpeobssim.binning.polarization.xBinnedPolarizationCube (verify class path at runtime via help()). Use accessor methods to extract: Stokes Q, U, their 1-sigma uncertainties sigma_Q and sigma_U, total intensity I, and MDP99. Record for each segment: obs_id, source_name, segment_index, midpoint_time_MET, Q, sigma_Q, U, sigma_U, I, MDP99. Reject segments where MDP99 > 15% (insufficient statistics). For full-observation PCUBEs, record PD, PA, MDP99 for the observation-integrated measurement.

STEP 5 - HARDNESS RATIO AND SPECTRAL STATE CLASSIFICATION: For each time segment, extract counts in soft (2-4 keV) and hard (4-8 keV) bands. Use astropy.io.fits to read event files and filter by PI column (convert energy to PI using header GAIN keywords or filter directly by time and energy). Count events C_soft (2-4 keV) and C_hard (4-8 keV) within r=60 arcsec source region. Compute hardness ratio HR = C_hard / C_soft with uncertainty sigma_HR = HR * sqrt(1/C_hard + 1/C_soft). Classify spectral state: hard (HR > 1.0), intermediate (0.5 < HR ≤ 1.0), soft (HR ≤ 0.5). Compute observation-level exposure-weighted mean HR and assign dominant spectral state.

STEP 6 - CHI-SQUARED VARIABILITY TEST: For each observation with N ≥ 8 valid segments, compute chi-squared statistic for constancy: χ²_Q = Σ[(Q_i - <Q>_w)² / σ_Q_i²] where <Q>_w = Σ(Q_i/σ_Q_i²) / Σ(1/σ_Q_i²) is the weighted mean, with dof = N-1. Similarly for χ²_U. Compute p-values using scipy.stats.chi2.sf(chi2, dof). Compute combined χ²_total = χ²_Q + χ²_U with dof = 2(N-1). Flag detections at p < 0.01. Compute intrinsic excess variance: σ²_exc,Q = max(0, (1/N) * Σ[(Q_i - <Q>)² - σ_Q_i²]). Report intrinsic rms amplitude = sqrt(σ²_exc).

STEP 7 - INTRA-OBSERVATION STRUCTURE FUNCTION COMPUTATION: For observations with N ≥ 10 valid segments, compute first-order structure function: SF_Q(τ) = (1/N_pairs(τ)) * Σ[Q(t_j+τ) - Q(t_j)]² for lag index τ = 1, 2, ..., floor(N/3). Estimate uncertainties via bootstrap: 1000 iterations resampling segment indices with replacement. Fit power-law SF(τ) = A * τ^β using scipy.optimize.curve_fit with bounds 0 < β < 2. Report β_Q, β_U with uncertainties from covariance matrix. Retain SF slope results only if σ(β) < 0.5 (as validated in Step 2).

STEP 8 - MULTI-EPOCH ANALYSIS: For sources with ≥6 observations (Cyg X-1: 12 obs; Swift J1727.8-1613: 8 obs), perform Discrete Correlation Function (DCF) analysis following Edelson & Krolik (1988). Combine per-observation full-exposure Q measurements ordered by MJD. Compute UDCF_ij = (Q_i - <Q>)(Q_j - <Q>) / sqrt(var_i * var_j) where var_i = σ_Q_i². Bin by lag Δt_ij into ~20-day bins. DCF(τ) = mean(UDCF) with uncertainty σ_DCF = sqrt(Σ(UDCF - DCF)² / [M(M-1)]). Report decorrelation timescale where DCF < 0.5. For sources with 4-5 observations (LMC X-3: 4 obs; Cyg X-3: 4 obs), apply only the chi-squared variability test for epoch-to-epoch constancy (same method as Step 6 but using observation-integrated Q, U values).

STEP 9 - SPECTRAL STATE COMPARISON: Group intrinsic rms amplitudes sqrt(σ²_exc,Q) and sqrt(σ²_exc,U) by dominant spectral state (hard/intermediate/soft). If each state group has ≥3 observations, use Kruskal-Wallis H-test (scipy.stats.kruskal) to test for differences. For smaller groups, use Mann-Whitney U test (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu) for pairwise comparisons. Similarly compare SF slopes β by spectral state where available.

STEP 10 - CROSS-SOURCE COMPARISON: Compile SF slopes β_Q, β_U and intrinsic rms for qualifying observations. Group by source and compute median, IQR. Apply Kruskal-Wallis test across sources with ≥2 observations to test for systematic differences in SF slopes. Compute Spearman correlation between SF slope and mean HR across all observations.

STEP 11 - VISUALIZATION AND OUTPUT: Generate matplotlib figures: (a) Q, U time series with error bars per long observation, HR on secondary y-axis. (b) SF_Q(τ), SF_U(τ) with bootstrap errors and power-law fits per source. (c) DCF(τ) for Cyg X-1 and Swift J1727.8-1613. (d) Box plot of intrinsic rms by spectral state. (e) Scatter plot of β vs HR with Spearman ρ. Save to CSV: (1) per_segment_stokes.csv, (2) structure_function_results.csv, (3) dcf_results.csv, (4) variability_summary.csv with obs_id, source_name, T_exp_ks, N_segments, chi2_Q, pval_Q, chi2_U, pval_U, sigma2_exc_Q, sigma2_exc_U, beta_Q, sigma_beta_Q, beta_U, sigma_beta_U, mean_HR, spectral_state.

title: Energy-Dependent Polarization Slopes vs Spectral State in BH-XRBs
description: This project measures energy-dependent X-ray polarization in transient and persistent low-mass/wind-fed BH-XRBs using XSPEC spectropolarimetric fitting with pollin models applied to tbabs*(diskbb+powerlaw). We analyze 17 observations across 5 BH-XRBs: Swift J1727.8-1613 (8 obs), 4U 1630-47 (2 obs), GX 339-4 (2 obs), LMC X-1 (1 obs), and LMC X-3 (4 obs). By fitting pollin to constrain the PD(E) slope (A2 parameter), we test whether energy-dependent polarization correlates with disk fraction—a proxy for spectral state. The primary new result will be systematic pollin slope measurements for a uniform sample of disk-dominated BH-XRBs, enabling the first statistical test of energy-dependent polarization trends with accretion geometry, even if individual observations yield only upper limits on the slope.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL: Verify Level-2 event files exist for all 17 observations across 5 BH-XRB sources: Swift J1727.8-1613 (8 obs: 02250901, 02251001, 02251101, 02251201, 02251301, 03005701, 03006001, 03005801), 4U 1630-47 (2 obs: 01250401, 02250601), GX 339-4 (2 obs: 03005101, 03005301), LMC X-1 (1 obs: 02001901), LMC X-3 (4 obs: 02006599, 03004899, 03004901, 03005001). Confirm DU1/DU2/DU3 event files for each observation. Abort if any observation is missing.

STEP 2 - PILOT FEASIBILITY TEST: Run initial test on one observation per source: (a) Swift J1727.8-1613 03006001 (151 ks), (b) 4U 1630-47 01250401 (459 ks), (c) LMC X-3 02006599 (457 ks). For each, extract Stokes I spectrum (PHA1 algorithm) for DU1 using ixpeobssim pipeline.xpbin with 60 arcsec source region centered on source coordinates and NEFF weighting. Do not specify irfname—allow auto-resolution. Load into XSPEC/PyXSPEC and count photons in 2-8 keV. Record counts. Proceed if at least 2 of 3 pilot observations show >30,000 counts.

STEP 3 - STOKES SPECTRA EXTRACTION: For all 17 observations, extract per-DU Stokes I, Q, U spectra using ixpeobssim pipeline.xpbin with algorithms PHA1, PHA1Q, PHA1U. Use 60 arcsec circular source region centered on source coordinates. Apply NEFF weighting (weights=True or equivalent). Do not subtract background (bright point sources dominate). Do not specify irfname—allow auto-resolution from event headers. Generate observation-specific ARF and MRF files using ixpecalcarf for each DU.

STEP 4 - SPECTRAL STATE CLASSIFICATION: For each observation, load per-DU Stokes I spectra (3 files) into XSPEC/PyXSPEC. Fit tbabs*(diskbb+powerlaw) to the 2-8 keV band. Tie diskbb parameters (kT, norm) and powerlaw parameters (Gamma, norm) across all 3 DUs. Allow multiplicative constant per DU (DU1 frozen to 1, DU2 and DU3 free). Fix NH to Galactic values from Willingale et al. or HI4PI: Swift J1727.8-1613 NH=3.5e21, 4U 1630-47 NH=8.0e22, GX 339-4 NH=5.0e21, LMC X-1 NH=5.0e20, LMC X-3 NH=4.0e20 (in cm^-2). Use chi-squared statistic. Compute disk fraction = diskbb_flux / total_flux in 2-8 keV using XSPEC cflux convolution model. Record: kT, Gamma, disk_fraction, chi2/dof.

STEP 5 - SPECTROPOLARIMETRIC FITTING WITH POLLIN: For each observation, load all 9 spectra (3 DUs × I/Q/U) into XSPEC/PyXSPEC. Apply response files: RMF/ARF for I spectra, RMF/MRF for Q/U spectra. Use model: constant*tbabs*pollin*(diskbb+powerlaw). The constant factor is frozen to 1 for DU1-I and free for DU2-I, DU3-I spectra; frozen to 1 for all Q/U spectra. Tie continuum parameters (kT, diskbb_norm, Gamma, powerlaw_norm) across all 9 spectra with fixed NH. Tie pollin parameters (A1=PD at pivot, A2=slope in %/keV, psi=PA) across all 9 spectra. Set pollin pivot energy Epivot=5.0 keV. Fit 2-8 keV with chi-squared statistic. Use XSPEC error command to compute 90% confidence intervals (delta chi2=2.706) for A1, A2, psi. If error command fails due to parameter hitting bounds, record the bound as the limit. Record: A1, A2, psi with symmetric 90% confidence errors derived as (upper-lower)/2, chi2/dof.

STEP 6 - POLCONST COMPARISON: For each observation, refit the same 9 spectra with constant*tbabs*polconst*(diskbb+powerlaw). The polconst model has constant PD and PA (equivalent to pollin with A2=0). Record chi2/dof. Compute delta_chi2 = chi2_polconst - chi2_pollin. Since pollin has 1 additional free parameter (A2), delta_chi2 > 2.71 indicates energy dependence at 90% confidence. Flag as 'detected' if delta_chi2 > 2.71, otherwise 'undetected'.

STEP 7 - RESULTS COMPILATION: Create master table pollin_results.csv with columns: source, obs_id, exposure_ks, NH_fixed, kT, kT_err, Gamma, Gamma_err, disk_fraction, PD_5keV (A1), PD_err, A2_slope, A2_err, PA (psi), PA_err, chi2_pollin, dof_pollin, chi2_polconst, dof_polconst, delta_chi2, energy_dep_detected.

STEP 8 - DISK FRACTION VS A2 CORRELATION: Compute Spearman rank correlation (scipy.stats.spearmanr) between A2_slope and disk_fraction across all 17 observations. Report Spearman rho and p-value. This tests whether energy-dependent polarization correlates with the relative contribution of disk vs corona.

STEP 9 - DETECTION STATISTICS: Count number of observations with detected energy dependence (delta_chi2 > 2.71) vs non-detections. For non-detections, report the 90% upper limit on |A2| from the error bounds. Compute the fraction of observations showing positive vs negative A2 slopes regardless of significance.

STEP 10 - PER-SOURCE MULTI-EPOCH ANALYSIS: For Swift J1727.8-1613 (8 epochs) and LMC X-3 (4 epochs), assess whether A2 varies across observations. Use weighted mean and chi-squared test: chi2_var = sum((A2_i - A2_wmean)^2 / A2_err_i^2) with dof = N-1. Compare chi2_var to chi-squared critical value at 95% confidence. If chi2_var exceeds critical value, flag as variable.

STEP 11 - VISUALIZATION: Generate: (a) scatter plot of A2_slope vs disk_fraction for all 17 observations, with points colored by source, error bars shown, and Spearman rho/p-value annotated. Save as a2_vs_diskfrac.png. (b) For Swift J1727.8-1613, time series plot of A2_slope vs observation date (MJD) with error bars. Save as swiftj1727_a2_evolution.png. (c) Histogram of A2_slope values for all observations. Save as a2_distribution.png.

STEP 12 - SUMMARY REPORT: Write pollin_energy_dependence_summary.txt documenting: (1) sample overview (17 obs across 5 BH-XRBs), (2) disk fraction distribution across sample, (3) number of significant energy-dependence detections vs upper limits, (4) Spearman correlation result for A2 vs disk_fraction, (5) per-source variability results for multi-epoch targets, (6) key finding: whether energy-dependent polarization shows a trend with disk dominance.

title: Autocorrelation Analysis of Stokes Parameter Time Series in BH-XRBs
description: This project characterizes intra-observation polarization variability timescales in long-exposure BH-XRB observations by computing autocorrelation functions (ACFs) of time-binned Stokes Q and U series extracted from DU-combined PCUBE analyses. For each sufficiently long observation (>100 ks), the exposure is divided into 5-ks time bins; for each bin, all three DU event files are combined before running PCUBE to extract properly weighted Stokes I, Q, U. The resulting Q(t) and U(t) time series are analyzed via discrete ACF computation to identify characteristic decorrelation timescales. This is novel because published IXPE BH-XRB analyses report time-averaged or coarse time-resolved polarization, but have not systematically quantified the autocorrelation timescales of Stokes fluctuations, which probe the coherence time of the polarizing region geometry.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL
Verify existence of all observation IDs in the local Level-2 archive. Target observations with exposure >100 ks for ACF analysis: 4U 1630-47 (01250401, ~459 ks), LMC X-1 (02001901, ~563 ks), LMC X-3 (02006599, ~457 ks; 03004899, ~385 ks; 03004901, ~382 ks; 03005001, ~389 ks), Cyg X-1 (01002901, ~241 ks), Swift J1727.8-1613 (03005801, ~202 ks; 03006001, ~151 ks). For each obs_id, locate all three DU event files (DU1, DU2, DU3). Abort if any dataset is missing.

STEP 2 - GTI EXTRACTION AND TIME BINNING
For each long observation (>100 ks), extract GTI from the Level-2 event files. Compute total good time. Define time bins of width 5 ks (adjustable to ensure >=20 bins per observation). For each time bin, use xpselect to filter events from all three DU files into the time interval [t_start, t_stop]. Output: per-bin event files for all three DUs.

STEP 3 - PER-BIN COMBINED-DU PCUBE EXTRACTION
For each time bin, pass all three DU event files (for that bin) together to xpbin with algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1. This correctly sums I, Q, U counts across DUs before computing polarization. Do NOT specify irfname; let ixpeobssim auto-resolve from headers. Source region: circle r=60 arcsec centered on source coordinates (from FITS RA_OBJ, DEC_OBJ). Background: not subtracted per BH-XRB consensus. Output: one combined PCUBE file per time bin.

STEP 4 - READ TIME-RESOLVED STOKES PRODUCTS
For each per-bin PCUBE file, read using xBinnedPolarizationCube. Extract the un-normalized Stokes I, Q, U counts and their uncertainties (σ_I, σ_Q, σ_U), plus PD, PA, and MDP99. Compute normalized q = Q/I and u = U/I with error propagation: σ_q = |q| * sqrt((σ_Q/Q)^2 + (σ_I/I)^2), similarly for σ_u. Store in DataFrame indexed by (source_name, obs_id, bin_index, t_mid) where t_mid is the bin midpoint MJD.

STEP 5 - QUALITY FILTERING
For each time bin, flag bins where: (a) effective exposure < 3 ks, (b) I counts < 1000, or (c) MDP99 > 30%. Exclude flagged bins from ACF computation. Require >=15 valid bins per observation for ACF analysis; skip observations with fewer valid bins.

STEP 6 - AUTOCORRELATION FUNCTION COMPUTATION
For each qualifying observation, compute the discrete autocorrelation function of the Q(t) and U(t) time series separately:
  ACF_Q(k) = Σ[(Q_i - Q_mean)(Q_{i+k} - Q_mean)] / Σ[(Q_i - Q_mean)^2]
  ACF_U(k) = Σ[(U_i - U_mean)(U_{i+k} - U_mean)] / Σ[(U_i - U_mean)^2]
where k is the lag in units of time bins. Compute for k = 0 to N_bins/2. Also compute ACF of I(t) for comparison (to distinguish intrinsic polarization variability from count rate variations).

STEP 7 - DECORRELATION TIMESCALE ESTIMATION
For each observation, define the decorrelation timescale τ_decorr as the smallest lag k where ACF first crosses below 1/e (~0.37). If ACF remains above 1/e for all computed lags, report τ_decorr as a lower limit (> max_lag * bin_width). Compute separate τ_Q and τ_U. Also compute the 1-sigma confidence band on ACF using bootstrap resampling (N=1000 iterations) with replacement on the time series. Report τ_decorr with uncertainty from bootstrap.

STEP 8 - CORRELATION BETWEEN Q AND U FLUCTUATIONS
For each observation, compute the Pearson correlation coefficient r_QU between the Q(t) and U(t) time series using scipy.stats.pearsonr. Test null hypothesis of no correlation. Significant positive/negative correlation indicates coordinated Stokes variations (rotating polarization angle vs. in-phase PD modulation).

STEP 9 - CROSS-CORRELATION WITH INTENSITY
Compute the cross-correlation function (CCF) between I(t) and Q(t), and between I(t) and U(t), to test whether polarization variations are phase-locked with flux variations. Report peak CCF amplitude and lag at peak. Use scipy.signal.correlate with mode='full' and normalize.

STEP 10 - CHI-SQUARED VARIABILITY TEST
For each observation, perform a chi-squared test for constancy of Q and U:
  χ²_Q = Σ[(Q_i - Q_mean)^2 / σ_Q_i^2]
  χ²_U = Σ[(U_i - U_mean)^2 / σ_U_i^2]
with dof = N_bins - 1. Compute p-values from chi-squared distribution. Reject null hypothesis of constant Stokes if p < 0.01. This quantifies whether detected variability exceeds measurement noise.

STEP 11 - COMPARISON ACROSS SOURCES
Compile τ_Q, τ_U, r_QU, χ²_Q, χ²_U, and CCF peak statistics for all qualifying observations. Compare decorrelation timescales between sources using descriptive statistics. Test whether τ_decorr correlates with average source flux or average PD across the sample (Spearman rank correlation, scipy.stats.spearmanr).

STEP 12 - VISUALIZATIONS
Generate per-observation figures:
  (a) Q(t) and U(t) time series with error bars and horizontal lines showing mean values.
  (b) ACF_Q(lag) and ACF_U(lag) with 1-sigma bootstrap confidence bands, horizontal dashed line at 1/e.
  (c) (Q, U) plane trajectory showing time evolution with points connected and color-coded by time.
  (d) I(t) light curve for context.
Generate summary figures:
  (e) Bar chart of τ_decorr for all observations, grouped by source.
  (f) Scatter plot of τ_decorr vs mean flux, with error bars.
Save all figures as PNG.

STEP 13 - OUTPUT TABLES
Create 'bhxrb_timebinned_stokes.csv': source_name, obs_id, bin_index, t_start_mjd, t_mid_mjd, t_stop_mjd, exposure_s, I_counts, Q_counts, U_counts, sigma_I, sigma_Q, sigma_U, q_norm, u_norm, sigma_q, sigma_u, PD, PA_deg, MDP99, quality_flag.
Create 'bhxrb_acf_results.csv': source_name, obs_id, n_bins_valid, tau_Q_ks, tau_Q_err_ks, tau_U_ks, tau_U_err_ks, r_QU, r_QU_pvalue, chi2_Q, chi2_Q_pvalue, chi2_U, chi2_U_pvalue, I_Q_ccf_peak, I_Q_ccf_lag_ks, I_U_ccf_peak, I_U_ccf_lag_ks.
Create 'bhxrb_acf_sample_correlations.csv': variable_pair, spearman_rho, spearman_pvalue.

STEP 14 - SUMMARY REPORT
Report: (a) Number of observations analyzed and total bins; (b) Fraction of observations with statistically significant Q or U variability (χ² p < 0.01); (c) Range of decorrelation timescales across the sample; (d) Whether Q-U correlation is significant in any observation (indicating PA rotation); (e) Whether Stokes-flux cross-correlations are significant (indicating flux-linked polarization changes); (f) Implications: short τ_decorr implies rapid geometric changes in the polarizing region; significant Q-U correlation implies systematic PA rotation rather than random walk.

title: Broadband Polarization-Hardness Correlation Survey Across BH-XRBs
description: This project surveys the correlation between broadband (2-8 keV) X-ray polarization degree and spectral hardness ratio across 29 observations of 6 BH-XRBs spanning diverse spectral states. Using model-independent PCUBE analysis for PD/PA and background-subtracted PHA spectra for hardness ratios, we test whether PD systematically correlates with HR within sources (intra-source variability) and across the sample (cross-source trends). Sources are selected to span persistent hard-state systems (Cyg X-1), transient outbursts (Swift J1727.8-1613, 4U 1630-47, GX 339-4), and soft-state-dominated systems (LMC X-1, LMC X-3), enabling comparison of polarization behavior across spectral states. Spearman rank correlations quantify PD-HR relationships, while KS tests compare PD distributions between hard and soft spectral states. This systematic cross-source survey of PD-hardness correlations using validated background subtraction has not been published and would establish whether spectral state is a primary driver of X-ray polarization in BH-XRBs.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL
Verify all 29 obs_ids exist in the local Level-2 archive: Cyg X-1 (01002901, 01250101, 02008201, 02008301, 02008401, 02008501, 02008601, 03002201, 03003101, 03010001, 03010101, 03002599), Swift J1727.8-1613 (02250901, 02251001, 02251101, 02251201, 02251301, 03005701, 03006001, 03005801), LMC X-1 (02001901), LMC X-3 (02006599, 03004899, 03004901, 03005001), 4U 1630-47 (01250401, 02250601), GX 339-4 (03005101, 03005301). Locate all DU event files (evt2 files) for each observation. Decompress .fits.gz files to a working directory if needed. Abort if any dataset is missing.

STEP 2 - SOURCE AND BACKGROUND REGION DEFINITION
For each source, define standard circular source extraction region (r=60 arcsec centered on source coordinates) and annular background region (inner radius 180 arcsec, outer radius 240 arcsec) following BH-XRB consensus from the literature. Store region definitions in DS9 format for reproducibility.

STEP 3 - BROADBAND PCUBE EXTRACTION
For each observation, run ixpeobssim pipeline.xpbin on all three DU event files with algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0 keV, explicitly set weights='NEFF'. Do NOT specify irfname; let ixpeobssim auto-resolve from event headers. Read the output PCUBE FITS file using ixpeobssim.binning.polarization.xBinnedPolarizationCube class. Extract: PD (polarization degree), PD_err (1-sigma error), PA (polarization angle), PA_err, MDP99. Record all values. Flag observations with MDP99 > 15% as having insufficient sensitivity.

STEP 4 - STOKES I SPECTRA EXTRACTION FOR HARDNESS RATIOS
For each observation and each DU, extract Stokes I spectra from source and background regions using xpbin with algorithm='PHA1' (or xselect if preferred). Extract source region spectrum and background region spectrum separately. Use the exposure-corrected count rates from the spectra. Compute:
- Soft-band rate: counts in 2-4 keV channel range (from source) minus scaled background
- Hard-band rate: counts in 4-8 keV channel range (from source) minus scaled background
- Scale background by area ratio: scale_factor = (source_area / background_area)
Sum across all three DUs for combined rates.

STEP 5 - HARDNESS RATIO CALCULATION
Compute hardness ratio from background-subtracted count rates:
HR = (Hard_rate - Soft_rate) / (Hard_rate + Soft_rate)
where Hard_rate = sum(hard_counts_source - scaled_hard_counts_bkg) / exposure
and Soft_rate = sum(soft_counts_source - scaled_soft_counts_bkg) / exposure.
Propagate errors using standard Poisson statistics for count rates and error propagation for ratio.
Alternatively, if xselect extraction is cleaner, use the PHA spectra with proper background subtraction.
Record HR and HR_err for each observation.

STEP 6 - DETECTION CLASSIFICATION
For each observation, classify polarization detection status:
- 'Detected': PD > MDP99 (>99% confidence)
- 'Non-detection': PD <= MDP99
For non-detections, record upper limit as MDP99 (the standard IXPE convention). Do not use the biased PD measurement for non-detections in correlation analyses.

STEP 7 - INTRA-SOURCE SPEARMAN CORRELATION (DETECTIONS ONLY)
For sources with >=4 observations showing detections (PD > MDP99):
(a) Compute Spearman rank correlation coefficient rho and p-value for PD vs HR using scipy.stats.spearmanr.
(b) If p < 0.05, flag as significant correlation.
(c) Record N_detections, rho, p-value.
This tests whether polarization degree tracks spectral hardness within individual sources.

STEP 8 - INTRA-SOURCE ANALYSIS INCLUDING UPPER LIMITS (SURVIVAL ANALYSIS)
For sources with mixed detections and non-detections, use scipy.stats.kendalltau or the generalized Kendall tau with censoring (from lifelines or survival analysis packages if available) to test PD-HR correlation while properly treating upper limits as censored data. If survival analysis tools are unavailable, perform separate analyses: (1) detections-only Spearman test, (2) comparison of mean HR between detected vs non-detected observations using Mann-Whitney U test.

STEP 9 - CROSS-SOURCE COMBINED ANALYSIS
Combine all observations with secure detections (PD > MDP99) across all six sources:
(a) Compute Spearman correlation for PD vs HR for the combined dataset.
(b) Group sources by dominant spectral state: soft-state (LMC X-1, LMC X-3) vs hard/intermediate-state (Cyg X-1, Swift J1727, 4U 1630-47, GX 339-4).
(c) Perform two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (scipy.stats.ks_2samp) comparing PD distributions between soft-state and hard-state groups.
(d) Perform Mann-Whitney U test comparing HR distributions between detected and non-detected observations to assess selection effects.

STEP 10 - FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT
For all observations, compute and tabulate: exposure (ks), MDP99, detection status. Create a summary showing: (1) Number of observations per source, (2) Number of detections per source, (3) Exposure range per source. This documents the statistical power available for correlation analyses and identifies any sources with insufficient detections.

STEP 11 - VISUALIZATION
(a) Create scatter plot of PD vs HR for all detections, color-coded by source, with error bars. Mark non-detections as downward arrows at MDP99.
(b) Create panel figure (one panel per source) showing PD vs HR with detections and upper limits.
(c) Create box plots comparing PD distributions between soft-state and hard-state source groups (detections only).
(d) Create HR distribution histogram for detected vs non-detected observations to visualize potential selection bias.
(e) Create feasibility plot: MDP99 vs exposure for all observations, with detection threshold line.

STEP 12 - OUTPUT PRODUCTS
Generate:
- Master measurements table: bhxrb_pd_hardness_survey.csv (columns: source, obs_id, exposure_ks, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, detected, HR, HR_err)
- Per-source correlation results: intra_source_correlations.csv (columns: source, N_obs, N_detections, rho_PD_HR, p_value_PD_HR, significant)
- Combined correlation results: combined_correlation.csv (columns: analysis_type, N_points, rho, p_value)
- Cross-source comparison: ks_test_soft_vs_hard.csv (columns: parameter, soft_state_median, hard_state_median, D_statistic, p_value)
- Selection bias assessment: detection_bias_assessment.csv (columns: metric, detected_group, nondetected_group, test_statistic, p_value)
- Figures: pd_vs_hr_combined.pdf, pd_vs_hr_per_source.pdf, pd_distribution_comparison.pdf, hr_detection_bias.pdf, feasibility_mdp99_exposure.pdf

title: 2D Stokes Homogeneity Tests for Multi-Epoch BH-XRB Polarimetry
description: This project tests epoch-to-epoch polarization constancy in five multi-epoch BH-XRBs—Cyg X-1 (12 epochs), Swift J1727.8-1613 (8 epochs), LMC X-3 (4 epochs), Cyg X-3 (4 epochs), and GX 339-4 (2 epochs)—using a proper 2D chi-squared test in the (q, u) Stokes plane. Model-independent PCUBE analysis with NEFF weighting extracts normalized Stokes parameters for each epoch; a joint 2D chi-squared test against a constant (q, u) model (with 2N-2 degrees of freedom) is applied per source to detect variability including Q-U plane rotations. For sources showing significant variability, absolute excess variance σ_XS² is computed to quantify intrinsic scatter amplitude. This comprehensive 30-observation survey across persistent wind-fed (Cyg X-1), transient disk-dominated (Swift J1727.8-1613, LMC X-3, GX 339-4), and unique jet-dominated (Cyg X-3) systems provides new quantitative constraints on polarimetric stability across diverse BH-XRB classes.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL: Retrieve Level-2 event files for all observations listed in targets_and_datasets from the local IXPE archive. For each observation, locate all three DU-specific event files (DU1, DU2, DU3). Decompress any .fits.gz files to a working directory. Verify all files exist before proceeding; abort if any are missing.

STEP 2 - REGION FILE GENERATION: For each source, create a DS9-format circular region file centered on the source position with radius 60 arcsec. Write the region file in FK5 coordinates as:
  # Region file format: DS9 version 4.1
  fk5
  circle(RA_deg, DEC_deg, 60")
where RA_deg and DEC_deg are obtained from the event file WCS headers (TCRVL columns for X/Y or RA_OBJ/DEC_OBJ keywords). Save as {source_name}_src.reg in the working directory.

STEP 3 - COMBINED DU POLARIZATION EXTRACTION: For each observation, run xpbin PCUBE with all three DU event files passed as input via pipeline.xpbin(*evt_files, algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1, weights=True, region='{source_name}_src.reg'). The weights=True enables NEFF weighting for optimal polarization sensitivity. Do NOT specify irfname—let ixpeobssim auto-resolve the response from the event file headers. The output is a single combined polarization cube per observation.

STEP 4 - MDP99 FEASIBILITY CHECK: Read each PCUBE output using ixpeobssim.binning.polarization.xBinnedPolarizationCube and extract the MDP99 value. For all observations, verify MDP99 < 15%. Flag observations failing this criterion but continue processing. Note: For short-exposure Swift J1727.8-1613 epochs (<25 ks: 02250901, 02251101, 02251201, 02251301), acknowledge that only large-amplitude variability (>10-15% PD changes) will be detectable.

STEP 5 - STOKES PARAMETER EXTRACTION: For each observation, use the xBinnedPolarizationCube reader to extract normalized Stokes parameters q=Q/I and u=U/I with their statistical uncertainties sigma_q and sigma_u. Record (obs_id, MJD, q, sigma_q, u, sigma_u, MDP99) for each observation. Save per-source tables as {source}_stokes_epochs.csv.

STEP 6 - 2D CHI-SQUARED VARIABILITY TEST: For each source with N epochs, compute the inverse-variance weighted means:
  <q>_w = sum(q_j / sigma_qj^2) / sum(1 / sigma_qj^2)
  <u>_w = sum(u_j / sigma_uj^2) / sum(1 / sigma_uj^2)
Then compute the joint 2D chi-squared statistic:
  chi2_2D = sum_j [ (q_j - <q>_w)^2 / sigma_qj^2 + (u_j - <u>_w)^2 / sigma_uj^2 ]
This has 2N - 2 degrees of freedom (2N data points minus 2 fitted parameters). Compute p-value using scipy.stats.chi2.sf(chi2_2D, 2*N - 2). Significant variability is flagged at p < 0.01. This joint test is sensitive to both amplitude and angle variations, including pure rotations in the Q-U plane.

STEP 7 - ABSOLUTE EXCESS VARIANCE: For sources where chi-squared variability is significant (p < 0.01), compute absolute excess variance for q and u separately:
  S_q^2 = (1/(N-1)) * sum((q_j - mean(q))^2)  [sample variance]
  sigma_XS_q^2 = max(0, S_q^2 - mean(sigma_qj^2))
  sigma_XS_q = sqrt(sigma_XS_q^2)
Similarly for u. Report sigma_XS_q and sigma_XS_u as measures of intrinsic variability amplitude in absolute Stokes units. If the quantity is negative (variance consistent with measurement errors), report sigma_XS = 0 with a 1-sigma upper limit of sqrt(2/N) * mean(sigma_err). Also compute combined excess variance sigma_XS_total = sqrt(sigma_XS_q^2 + sigma_XS_u^2).

STEP 8 - INTER-SOURCE COMPARISON IN 2D STOKES SPACE: Compare the weighted mean (q, u) values between all source pairs using a 2D chi-squared test. For sources A and B with weighted means (<q>_A, <u>_A) and (<q>_B, <u>_B) and uncertainties computed from the weighted mean formulas, compute:
  sigma_qA = sqrt(1 / sum(1/sigma_qj_A^2))
  sigma_uA = sqrt(1 / sum(1/sigma_uj_A^2))
  (similarly for B)
  Delta_q = <q>_A - <q>_B
  Delta_u = <u>_A - <u>_B
  sigma_Delta_q = sqrt(sigma_qA^2 + sigma_qB^2)
  sigma_Delta_u = sqrt(sigma_uA^2 + sigma_uB^2)
  chi2_pair = (Delta_q/sigma_Delta_q)^2 + (Delta_u/sigma_Delta_u)^2
Compute p-value using scipy.stats.chi2.sf(chi2_pair, df=2). Report which source pairs have statistically distinguishable polarization (p < 0.01).

STEP 9 - VISUALIZATION: Generate: (a) Per-source scatter plots of (q, u) with 1-sigma error ellipses for each epoch, color-coded by MJD, with the weighted mean marked and its uncertainty ellipse; (b) Time series plots of q and u vs MJD with error bars for each source; (c) Normalized residual histograms: compute r_qj = (q_j - <q>_w)/sigma_qj and r_uj = (u_j - <u>_w)/sigma_uj, pool all residuals per source, and compare to standard normal using scipy.stats.kstest; (d) A summary comparison plot showing weighted mean (q, u) with 1-sigma error ellipses for all five sources in a single (q, u) plane.

STEP 10 - OUTPUT PRODUCTS: Save combined Stokes parameter tables as {source}_stokes_epochs.csv (columns: obs_id, MJD, q, sigma_q, u, sigma_u, MDP99). For reporting convenience only, include derived columns PD and PA computed as PD = sqrt(q^2 + u^2), PA_deg = 0.5*atan2(u, q)*180/pi, but note these are for display purposes and NOT used in statistical tests. Save statistical summary as bhxrb_multiepoch_stokes_homogeneity_2d_summary.csv (columns: source, N_epochs, chi2_2D, dof, pval_2D, significant, sigma_XS_q, sigma_XS_u, sigma_XS_total, mean_q, sigma_mean_q, mean_u, sigma_mean_u). Save inter-source comparison as bhxrb_intersource_comparison_2d.csv (columns: source_A, source_B, chi2_pair, pval_pair, significant). Save all figures as PDF files.

title: Per-DU Stokes Parameter Consistency Tests Across BH-XRB Observations
description: This project quantifies the inter-DU consistency of X-ray polarization measurements in BH-XRBs by performing chi-squared tests on per-DU Stokes parameters extracted independently from DU1, DU2, and DU3 using standard PCUBE analysis. For each of 31 observations spanning 9 BH-XRBs (Cyg X-1, Swift J1727.8-1613, LMC X-3, 4U 1630-47, GX 339-4, LMC X-1, Cyg X-3, GRS 1915+105, 4U 1957+115), we extract broadband (2-8 keV) normalized Stokes q and u with uncertainties from each DU separately using NEFF weighting, 60 arcsec source regions, and no background subtraction. We apply a 2-parameter chi-squared constancy test (4 d.o.f. per observation) to assess whether the three DUs yield statistically consistent polarization. This provides a systematic, population-level quantification of IXPE measurement consistency that has not been published as a dedicated study, serving as both a data-quality diagnostic and a constraint on any DU-dependent systematics. A new finding of either excellent DU consistency or systematic DU offsets would be publishable as an instrument performance study.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL
Locate Level-2 event files for all 31 observations across 9 BH-XRBs: Cyg X-1 (obs_ids: 01002901, 01250101, 02008201, 02008301, 02008401, 02008501, 02008601, 03002201, 03003101, 03010001, 03010101, 03002599), Swift J1727.8-1613 (obs_ids: 02250901, 02251001, 02251101, 02251201, 02251301, 03005701, 03006001, 03005801), LMC X-3 (obs_ids: 02006599, 03004899, 03004901, 03005001), 4U 1630-47 (obs_ids: 01250401, 02250601), GX 339-4 (obs_ids: 03005101, 03005301), LMC X-1 (obs_id: 02001901), Cyg X-3 (obs_ids: 02001899, 02250301, 02009101, 03250301), GRS 1915+105 (obs_id: 04003501), 4U 1957+115 (obs_id: 02006601). Verify all observations exist in the Level-2 archive. Decompress .fits.gz files to a working directory if needed. Identify the three per-DU event files (DU1, DU2, DU3) for each observation based on DETNAM keyword.

STEP 2 - PER-DU PCUBE EXTRACTION
For each observation and each DU (1, 2, 3) separately, run ixpeobssim pipeline.xpbin with algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1 on the individual DU event file. Use explicit analysis parameters: (a) source region = 60 arcsec radius circle centered on the source position from event file headers (RA_OBJ, DEC_OBJ), (b) no background subtraction, (c) NEFF weighting (weights='NEFF'). Do NOT specify irfname; let ixpeobssim auto-resolve from event headers. Read each output PCUBE file using ixpeobssim.binning.polarization.xBinnedPolarizationCube. Extract: normalized Stokes q, u, their common uncertainty sigma (note: sigma_q = sigma_u = sigma for IXPE), PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, and effective counts NEFF. Store results in a pandas DataFrame with columns: source, obs_id, DU, q, u, sigma, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, NEFF.

STEP 3 - COMBINED DU PCUBE FOR REFERENCE
For each observation, also run pipeline.xpbin with algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1 on all three DU event files simultaneously (pass list of all three DU files). Use same parameters: 60 arcsec source region, no background, NEFF weighting. Extract the combined PD, PA, MDP99, q, u, sigma. Store in a separate reference DataFrame for comparison.

STEP 4 - QUALITY FILTERING
Apply quality cuts based on per-DU NEFF counts. Retain an observation only if all three DUs have NEFF >= 500 counts (lowered from 1000 to retain more observations given the many short Cyg X-1 pointings). Additionally flag observations where combined MDP99 > 30% as having low polarization sensitivity. Report: (a) number of observations initially, (b) number passing per-DU NEFF cut, (c) number with MDP99 < 30%, (d) final sample size.

STEP 5 - PER-OBSERVATION CHI-SQUARED CONSTANCY TEST
For each quality-filtered observation, test whether the three DU measurements are consistent with a single underlying (q, u). Compute the weighted mean using the common uncertainty sigma_i for each DU:
q_bar = sum(q_i / sigma_i^2) / sum(1 / sigma_i^2) for i=1,2,3 DUs
u_bar = sum(u_i / sigma_i^2) / sum(1 / sigma_i^2)
Compute chi-squared:
chi2 = sum_i [ ((q_i - q_bar)^2 + (u_i - u_bar)^2) / sigma_i^2 ]
with degrees of freedom dof = 4 (3 DUs x 2 parameters - 2 fitted parameters = 4). Compute p-value using scipy.stats.chi2.sf(chi2, dof). Record chi2, dof, p_value for each observation. Flag observations with p < 0.01 as showing significant inter-DU discrepancy.

STEP 6 - POPULATION-LEVEL CONSISTENCY STATISTICS
Aggregate the per-observation chi2 values. Under the null hypothesis of DU consistency, chi2 values should follow a chi-squared distribution with dof=4. Perform a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test comparing the observed chi2 distribution against the expected chi2(dof=4) distribution using scipy.stats.kstest with cdf=lambda x: scipy.stats.chi2.cdf(x, df=4). Report the KS statistic and p-value. Additionally, compute the fraction of observations with p < 0.01 and compare to the expected 1% false-positive rate using a binomial test.

STEP 7 - DU-SPECIFIC SYSTEMATIC OFFSET SEARCH
For all quality-filtered observations, compute the mean offset of each DU from the combined measurement:
Delta_q_DUk = mean(q_DUk - q_combined) for k=1,2,3
Delta_u_DUk = mean(u_DUk - u_combined) for k=1,2,3
Compute standard errors on these mean offsets. Test whether any DU shows a systematic offset significantly different from zero using a one-sample t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_1samp). Report the mean offsets and p-values for each DU in q and u separately (6 tests total). Apply Bonferroni correction (alpha=0.05/6=0.0083).

STEP 8 - SOURCE-BY-SOURCE SUMMARY
For each of the 9 sources, summarize: number of observations, number passing quality cuts, fraction with inter-DU consistency (p > 0.01), mean combined PD across epochs, mean MDP99. Identify any sources with recurring DU discrepancies.

STEP 9 - GENERATE DIAGNOSTIC FIGURES
Using matplotlib, produce:
(a) For a representative subset of 9 observations (one per source where available, prioritizing highest-NEFF observation), a 3x3 panel (q, u) Stokes plane plot showing the three DU measurements with 1-sigma error circles and the combined measurement marked. Color-code by DU (DU1=blue, DU2=orange, DU3=green).
(b) Histogram of per-observation p-values from Step 5. Overlay the expected uniform distribution under the null hypothesis.
(c) Scatter plot of chi2 vs combined MDP99 to check for any correlation between signal strength and inter-DU consistency. Include Spearman rank correlation coefficient.
(d) Bar plot of mean DU offsets (Delta_q, Delta_u) for DU1, DU2, DU3 with error bars from Step 7.
(e) Q-Q plot comparing observed chi2 distribution against theoretical chi2(dof=4).
Save all figures as PNG files in the project directory.

STEP 10 - OUTPUT SUMMARY
Compile two CSV tables:
(1) per_du_stokes.csv: source, obs_id, DU, q, u, sigma, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, NEFF
(2) consistency_tests.csv: source, obs_id, q_bar, u_bar, chi2, dof, pvalue, consistent_flag (1 if p>0.01, 0 otherwise), combined_PD, combined_PA, combined_MDP99
Write a text summary (consistency_summary.txt) reporting: (1) final sample size after quality cuts, (2) fraction of observations showing DU consistency (p > 0.01), (3) KS test result for population-level chi2 distribution, (4) any significant DU-specific systematic offsets after Bonferroni correction, (5) per-source consistency patterns.

title: Intensity-Stokes Correlation Survey in High-Count BH-XRBs
description: This project searches for intra-observation correlations between X-ray intensity (unweighted count rate) and polarization state (normalized Stokes q and u) in stellar-mass BH-XRBs. We target all BH-XRB observations with exposure >90 ks and expected total counts >200,000 in the 2-8 keV band, yielding ≥10 adaptive-count bins with σ(q,u) ≈ 2.5%. Background is demonstrated to be negligible (<1% of source counts for these bright sources based on literature consensus) and is not subtracted. Adaptive GTI binning ensures uniform statistical quality across bins. We compute Pearson and Spearman correlations between unweighted count rate and weighted (NEFF) normalized Stokes parameters, applying Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all tests. A multivariate Pillai-Bartlett trace test quantifies joint I-(q,u) coupling. Detection of significant intensity-Stokes correlations on intra-observation timescales would be a novel empirical signature linking flux and polarization variability, publishable as a systematic survey.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL
For each BH-XRB source and obs_id listed (Cyg X-1: 01002901, 03002599; 4U 1630-47: 01250401; LMC X-1: 02001901; LMC X-3: 02006599, 03004899, 03004901, 03005001; Swift J1727.8-1613: 03005801, 03006001; 4U 1957+115: 02006601; 4U 1957+11: 04251199; GS 1354-64: 05002101, 05250399; GX 339-4: 03005101, 03005301), locate all three DU Level-2 event files (*det1*, *det2*, *det3*) in the local archive. Decompress .fits.gz files to a working directory if needed. Verify all 17 obs_ids (51 DU event files total) are present before proceeding. Abort if any are missing.

STEP 2 - COUNT RATE AND FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT
For each observation:
(a) Read events from all three DU files using astropy.io.fits, filtering 2-8 keV (PI channel range corresponding to 2-8 keV) and a 60 arcsec circular source region.
(b) Compute total unweighted source counts N_total and total exposure T_exp (from GTI or LIVETIME keywords).
(c) Compute mean count rate R = N_total / T_exp.
(d) Calculate required counts per bin for target σ(q,u) ≈ 2.5%: with modulation factor μ ≈ 0.4, σ(q) ≈ (1/μ) * sqrt(2/N_bin), so for σ ≈ 0.025, N_bin ≈ 20000 counts.
(e) Compute N_bins = floor(N_total / 20000). Require N_bins >= 10 for inclusion.
(f) Log observation summary: source, obs_id, exposure_ks, N_total, R_cps, predicted_N_bins, included (yes/no).
Exclude observations with N_bins < 10 from subsequent steps.

STEP 3 - BACKGROUND ASSESSMENT AND JUSTIFICATION FOR NO SUBTRACTION
For one representative high-count observation (Cyg X-1 01002901):
(a) Define background region: annulus centered on source with inner radius 180 arcsec and outer radius 240 arcsec.
(b) Extract background events in 2-8 keV from all three DU files.
(c) Compute background count rate R_bg and scale to source region area (60 arcsec circle): scaled_bg = R_bg * (π * 60²) / (π * (240² - 180²)).
(d) Compute background fraction: f_bg = scaled_bg / R_source.
(e) Verify f_bg < 0.01 (1%). If confirmed, log justification that background is negligible and does not require subtraction for this sample of bright BH-XRBs. If f_bg >= 0.01 for any observation, flag that observation for exclusion.
(f) Record background assessment in output log.

STEP 4 - GENERATE ADAPTIVE-COUNT GTI FILES
For each observation passing feasibility:
(a) Read all three DU event files and concatenate event times (TIME column) for events within 60 arcsec source region and 2-8 keV.
(b) Sort events by time.
(c) Target N_bin = 20000 counts per bin.
(d) Create GTI intervals: for each interval i, START[i] = time of event (i * N_bin + 1), STOP[i] = time of event ((i+1) * N_bin). Handle final partial bin by excluding it if counts < 10000.
(e) Write GTI as FITS file (astropy.io.fits) with columns START, STOP in same time system as events.
(f) Store GTI file path for each observation.

STEP 5 - TIME-BINNED PCUBE EXTRACTION WITH ADAPTIVE GTI
For each observation passing feasibility:
(a) Use ixpeobssim pipeline.xpbin with algorithm='PCUBE', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ebins=1.
(b) Apply custom GTI file: gtifile=<path_to_custom_gti>.
(c) Use 60 arcsec circular source region centered on the source (srcra, srcdec from event file keywords).
(d) Let ixpeobssim auto-resolve irfname from event headers (do NOT specify irfname explicitly).
(e) Use NEFF weighting (default for PCUBE).
(f) Collect the output PCUBE file paths.

STEP 6 - EXTRACT UNWEIGHTED COUNT RATE PER GTI BIN
For each observation, independently of the PCUBE:
(a) Read concatenated events (all DUs) in source region, 2-8 keV.
(b) For each GTI interval [START[i], STOP[i]]:
    - Count unweighted events: N_unweighted[i].
    - Compute bin duration: dt[i] = STOP[i] - START[i].
    - Compute unweighted count rate: R[i] = N_unweighted[i] / dt[i].
    - Compute bin midpoint: t_mid[i] = (START[i] + STOP[i]) / 2.
(c) Store: [obs_id, bin_index, t_mid, R_cps, N_counts, dt_sec].

STEP 7 - EXTRACT TIME-BINNED STOKES PARAMETERS FROM PCUBE
For each time-binned PCUBE output:
(a) Load with ixpeobssim.binning.polarization.xBinnedPolarizationCube.
(b) For each time bin index i:
    - q[i] = cube.q()[i]; sigma_q[i] = cube.q_err()[i].
    - u[i] = cube.u()[i]; sigma_u[i] = cube.u_err()[i].
    - pd_debiased[i] = cube.pd()[i]; pd_err[i] = cube.pd_err()[i].
    - pa[i] = cube.pa()[i]; pa_err[i] = cube.pa_err()[i].
(c) Build pandas DataFrame per observation: [source, obs_id, bin_index, t_mid_mjd, R_cps, q, sigma_q, u, sigma_u, pd_debiased, pd_err, pa, pa_err].

STEP 8 - INTENSITY-STOKES q CORRELATION ANALYSIS
For each valid observation DataFrame:
(a) Use R_cps (unweighted count rate from STEP 6) as intensity and q (from STEP 7) as polarization observable.
(b) Compute Pearson r and p-value: scipy.stats.pearsonr(R_cps, q).
(c) Compute Spearman rho and p-value: scipy.stats.spearmanr(R_cps, q).
(d) Store: [source, obs_id, n_bins, r_Rq, p_pearson_Rq, rho_Rq, p_spearman_Rq].

STEP 9 - INTENSITY-STOKES u CORRELATION ANALYSIS
Repeat STEP 8 for u instead of q:
(a) Compute Pearson r and p-value for (R_cps, u).
(b) Compute Spearman rho and p-value.
(c) Store: [source, obs_id, n_bins, r_Ru, p_pearson_Ru, rho_Ru, p_spearman_Ru].

STEP 10 - JOINT MULTIVARIATE CORRELATION TEST (PILLAI-BARTLETT)
For each valid observation:
(a) Use statsmodels.multivariate.manova.MANOVA to test whether intensity R_cps predicts the bivariate response (q, u).
(b) Construct formula: 'q + u ~ R_cps' after creating a DataFrame with columns R_cps, q, u.
(c) Fit MANOVA model: manova = MANOVA.from_formula('q + u ~ R_cps', data=df).
(d) Extract Pillai-Bartlett trace statistic and its F-test p-value from manova.mv_test().
(e) Store: [source, obs_id, Pillai_stat, Pillai_F, Pillai_p].

STEP 11 - POPULATION STATISTICS WITH BENJAMINI-HOCHBERG FDR
Combine all per-observation correlation results:
(a) For each test type (R-q Pearson, R-q Spearman, R-u Pearson, R-u Spearman, joint Pillai), collect all p-values across observations.
(b) Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction using statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests with method='fdr_bh' at α=0.05.
(c) Report per observation: adjusted p-values and significance flags (reject/accept null).
(d) Compute summary statistics: number and fraction of observations with significant (FDR-corrected) R-q, R-u, and joint correlations.
(e) Report per-source and overall summary.

STEP 12 - VISUALIZATION
Produce:
(a) For each source, a 4-panel time series plot for the longest valid observation: (1) R_cps vs time, (2) q vs time with error bars, (3) u vs time with error bars, (4) pd_debiased vs time with error bars. Use matplotlib; label axes, include legend.
(b) Scatter plot: R_cps vs q for all time bins from all observations, color-coded by source. If any observation shows FDR-significant correlation, overlay linear fit line for that observation.
(c) Scatter plot: R_cps vs u for all time bins, color-coded by source.
(d) Summary bar chart: count of significant (FDR-corrected) positive, negative, and null correlations for R-q, R-u, and joint Pillai tests.
(e) Q-U plane scatter plot for all bins from all observations, color-coded by relative intensity (R/mean(R) per observation), with 1-sigma error ellipses.
Save all figures as PNG files with descriptive names.

STEP 13 - OUTPUT FILES
Write:
(a) 'bhxrb_intensity_stokes_correlation_summary.csv': per-observation statistics [source, obs_id, exposure_ks, n_bins, mean_R_cps, r_Rq, p_Rq, rho_Rq, p_spearman_Rq, r_Ru, p_Ru, rho_Ru, p_spearman_Ru, Pillai_stat, Pillai_p, FDR_adj_p_Rq_pearson, FDR_adj_p_Rq_spearman, FDR_adj_p_Ru_pearson, FDR_adj_p_Ru_spearman, FDR_adj_p_Pillai, sig_Rq, sig_Ru, sig_joint].
(b) 'bhxrb_timebinned_stokes.csv': all time-binned data [source, obs_id, bin_index, t_mid_mjd, R_cps, N_counts, dt_sec, q, sigma_q, u, sigma_u, pd_debiased, pd_err, pa, pa_err].
(c) 'bhxrb_sample_summary.csv': all 17 observations [source, obs_id, exposure_ks, N_total, mean_R_cps, N_bins_target, included, exclusion_reason, bg_fraction_check].
(d) 'bhxrb_population_summary.txt': text summary of FDR-corrected significant correlations, detection fractions, and scientific conclusions.
