conclusions: 45 of 47 BH-XRB observations processed (2 excluded as GPG-encrypted/unreadable: 04004001, 05250399). Broadband PD correlates strongly with the count-rate hardness proxy (Spearman r=0.80, p=3e-11; KS D=0.78, p=2e-7): harder sources are more polarized. In contrast, the ENERGY-DRIFT amplitude of the Stokes vector |b| shows NO significant correlation with hardness (r=0.17, p=0.25), i.e. the energy dependence of the Stokes vector is source-specific rather than universally state-driven. Strongest energy-dependent Stokes drifts: 4U 1630-47 (|b| sig ~9) and GS 1354-64 (b_q/sigma~8); Cyg X-3 shows the highest PD (~10-20%) with significant q(E) curvature; Cyg X-1 shows systematic PD rise with energy.

title: Population Clustering of Broadband Stokes (q,u) Vectors in BH-XRBs
description: We perform a model-independent census of the broadband (2-8 keV) normalized Stokes vectors (q,u) of the full archival BH-XRB IXPE sample and ask a purely observational, population-level question that no single-source IXPE paper can address: do BH-XRBs occupy a STRUCTURED locus in the (q,u) plane, and does that structure correlate with simple observed quantities (per-DU count rate, spectral hardness)? Using standard PCUBE (q,u) points with their 2-D error covariances, we (1) build a uniform population table; (2) test whether observations of the same source cluster more tightly than the population via a label-permutation test on a correctly standardized 2-D Stokes distance; (3) test for a preferred population PA direction (Rayleigh test on 2*PA in radians); and (4) test, with a purely observational split on count rate and on hardness ratio, whether the q,u centroids of sub-samples differ using an error-aware Mahalanobis permutation test. Expected new, publishable results: the first uniform population map of BH-XRB broadband Stokes vectors with covariances, a quantitative statement of whether the population clusters or shows a preferred PA, and any observed correlation between Stokes-plane position and observed count rate/hardness. Multiple sources are essential because the clustering and preferred-direction tests are intrinsically population statistics. No emission model is fit at any stage.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND VERIFICATION. Build the file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(DATA_DIR) (these are the science-grade *_rej.fits paths; do NOT exclude '_rej'). For every (source_name, obs_id) in targets_and_datasets, confirm at least one DU event file exists; if ANY obs_id is missing, ABORT and report which obs_ids are absent. Note on sample purity: the aBH context list also contains SCO X-1 (04010001) and Swift J0243.6+6124 (02250799), which are NEUTRON-STAR systems; DROP them explicitly and do NOT include them in any census or test (they are not in targets_and_datasets). Keep the off-nuclear/jet sources SS 433, SS 433 WEST, SS 433 lobe as separate canonical labels and flag them 'jet/lobe, not point-source accretion' so they can be excluded from the clustering test in a robustness pass. Resolve coordinates per obs with red_ixpe.source_coords(obs, file_list). Record TSTART/TSTOP/ONTIME from each event header, and record the number of active DUs present for this obs (n_du = count of distinct det1/det2/det3 event files; usually 3). Energy band 2-8 keV throughout. Weighted alpha075 analysis is the default: call red_ixpe.pcube WITHOUT an explicit irfname and let it auto-resolve the IRF from the event-file headers; only set irfname if auto-resolution fails. Region defaults: src_rad=1.0 arcmin, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0.

STEP 2 - PER-SOURCE BACKGROUND DECISION (NOT a blanket assumption). For each obs, estimate the PER-DU source surface brightness in cps/arcmin^2 WITHOUT hand-parsing FITS tables. Run a dummy unweighted PCUBE and EXPLICITLY UNPACK THE TUPLE: src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, weights=False, subtract_background=False); then s = red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=0). NEVER pass the raw (src,bkg) tuple to cube_summary - that crashes the pipeline. The cube_summary I from this unweighted cube is the raw in-region count sum SUMMED OVER ALL ACTIVE DUs. To get a per-DU count rate (the Di Marco 2023 thresholds are defined PER DU), divide by both ONTIME and n_du: count_rate_total = s['I']/ONTIME (cps, all DUs); count_rate_perDU = count_rate_total / n_du; surface_brightness_perDU = count_rate_perDU / (pi * src_rad^2) (cps/arcmin^2, src_rad in arcmin). Apply the Di Marco (2023) rule on the PER-DU value: if surface_brightness_perDU > ~2 set subtract_background=False; if < ~1 set subtract_background=True; in the intermediate 1-2 band default to False (PSF-dominated) but record the value. Store the chosen subtract_background flag, count_rate_total, count_rate_perDU, surface_brightness_perDU, and n_du per obs in the census table so the choice is auditable. The faint/extragalactic and lobe targets (LMC X-1, LMC X-3, 4U 1957+11, SS 433 lobe/WEST) are expected to trigger subtraction; bright targets (Cyg X-1, Swift J1727.8-1613, 4U 1630-47) are expected to remain unsubtracted.

STEP 3 - SMOKE TEST. On ONE bright observation (Cyg X-1 01002901) run src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=False) and red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=0). Confirm a non-empty cube and that PD, PD_err, MDP99 are FRACTIONS (x100 for percent) and PA, PA_err are degrees. Do NOT scale to the full loop until this returns real numbers. Then run a second smoke test on ONE faint observation (LMC X-3 02006599) with subtract_background=True to confirm the subtraction branch runs. In both, confirm the tuple-unpacking pattern (src,bkg = ...; cube_summary(src,...)).

STEP 4 - BROADBAND (q,u) CENSUS POINT PER OBSERVATION. For each obs, run a single-band weighted PCUBE src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(..., ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ...) with the per-obs subtract_background flag from Step 2 and the region defaults; read s = cube_summary(src, ebin=0) -> record I,Q,U,Q_err,U_err, q=Q/I, u=U/I, q_err, u_err, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99, significance=PD/PD_err. Derive q_err and u_err from cube_summary Q_err/U_err and I (q_err=Q_err/I, u_err=U_err/I; I has negligible relative error for these high-count sources). Also record the Step-2 count rates/surface brightness, and a broadband HARDNESS RATIO computed from a two-band weighted PCUBE: src2, bkg2 = red_ixpe.pcube(..., ebinning=[2.0,4.0,8.0], ...). EXPLICITLY index the two energy bins: I_soft = cube_summary(src2, ebin=0)['I'] (2-4 keV) and I_hard = cube_summary(src2, ebin=1)['I'] (4-8 keV); HR = I_hard / I_soft (label it a weighted-flux hardness proxy). Do NOT call ebin=0 twice. Save to census_broadband.csv with one row per observation (columns: source, obsid, exposure, n_du, subtract_bg, surf_brightness_perDU, count_rate_total, count_rate_perDU, HR, I, Q, U, q, u, q_err, u_err, PD_pct, PD_err_pct, PA_deg, PA_err_deg, MDP99_pct, significance, detected, is_jet_lobe, report_string). Flag detected (PD>MDP99) and store red_ixpe.pol_report(s)['report_string'] (debiased PD for detections, upper limit Pi<Pi0+3sigma for non-detections). For multi-epoch sources also compute a per-source combined point with red_ixpe.combine_summaries over that source's per-obs summaries (combine only summaries reduced with the SAME subtract_background choice; if a source mixes choices, combine within each subset and note it), saved to census_combined_per_source.csv. NOTE: the two name spellings of the same physical source (e.g. 'Cyg X-1' and 'CYG X-1', 'Cyg X-3' and 'CYG X-3', 'Swift J1727.8-1613' and 'SWIFT J1727.8-1613', '4U 1630-47' and '4U1630-47', '4U 1957+11' and '4U 1957+115') must be merged into one canonical source label for all population tests.

STEP 5 - INTRA- vs INTER-SOURCE CLUSTERING TEST. Using the broadband census points (exclude jet/lobe-flagged rows in the primary test; include them in a robustness pass), build the 2-D array of (q,u) with per-point diagonal errors (q_err, u_err). Compute the CORRECT 2-D standardized Euclidean Stokes distance treating q and u variances SEPARATELY: d_ij = sqrt[ (q_i-q_j)^2/(q_err_i^2+q_err_j^2) + (u_i-u_j)^2/(u_err_i^2+u_err_j^2) ]. (Do NOT pool the q and u variances into a single denominator.) Permutation test (10000 random shuffles of the canonical source labels, keeping the (q,u) points fixed): compare the observed mean intra-source pairwise distance vs the mean inter-source pairwise distance (statistic = mean_inter - mean_intra) to the shuffled null distribution; report a one-sided p-value for whether same-source observations cluster tighter than the population. Only sources with >=2 included observations contribute intra-source pairs. This both validates measurement repeatability and quantifies whether sources are distinguishable in Stokes space. Save permutation_clustering.json (observed statistic, null mean/std, p-value, n_intra_pairs, n_inter_pairs, n_sources_with_repeats).

STEP 6 - PREFERRED-DIRECTION (POPULATION PA) TEST. Restrict to detected observations (PD>MDP99). Because PA is defined modulo 180 deg, test for a preferred axis by DOUBLING the angle: form theta = 2*PA, CONVERT theta from degrees to RADIANS with numpy.deg2rad BEFORE any circular statistic, then run astropy.stats.rayleightest(theta_radians) (which strictly requires radians). Report the resultant length, the mean axis (= 0.5 * the circular mean of theta, mapped back to degrees in -90..+90 East of North), and the p-value. As a robustness check, resample each PA from a Gaussian(PA, PA_err) (1000 draws), recompute the Rayleigh p-value each draw (again converting 2*PA to radians), and report the median and 16-84 percentile of the p-value distribution. Save preferred_direction.json.

STEP 7 - PURELY OBSERVATIONAL SUB-SAMPLE COMPARISON (ERROR-AWARE ONLY). Split the population on two genuinely observation-defined (model-agnostic) axes, NOT on any physical classification: (a) by per-DU count rate at the sample median (high-rate vs low-rate), and (b) by hardness ratio HR at the sample median (hard vs soft). DO NOT use scipy.stats.ks_2samp or scipy.stats.anderson_ksamp on the q/u marginals: the exposures range from ~17 ks to ~745 ks, so the per-point q,u errors are wildly heteroscedastic and an unweighted KS/AD test would treat a noisy 17 ks point identically to a precise 700 ks point and destroy the test's power. Instead rely EXCLUSIVELY on an error-aware 2-D permutation test: compute the Mahalanobis-like squared separation between the two sub-sample centroids in (q,u), D2 = (dq)^2/(var_q1+var_q2) + (du)^2/(var_u1+var_u2), where dq,du are the differences of the inverse-variance-WEIGHTED sub-sample means (weights 1/q_err^2 and 1/u_err^2 respectively) and var_q1,var_u1,... are the variances OF THOSE WEIGHTED MEANS (1/sum(1/err^2)); build the null by shuffling the split labels 10000 times (recomputing weighted centroids each shuffle) and report the permutation p-value of D2. Also report, for each split, the Spearman rho and p-value between the splitting variable (per-DU count rate; HR) and PD, and between the splitting variable and PA, treating each as a continuous correlation. Save subsample_tests.json (weighted centroids and their variances per sub-sample, Mahalanobis-D2, permutation p, Spearman rho/p for PD and PA, for each of the two splits).

STEP 8 - REPORTING. Emit: census_broadband.csv, census_combined_per_source.csv, permutation_clustering.json, preferred_direction.json, subsample_tests.json, plus figures qu_population.png (a (q,u) scatter with per-source 1-sigma error ellipses, distinct colour/marker per canonical source, PA convention -90..+90 East of North on an inset protractor) and pd_vs_rate_hardness.png (PD vs per-DU count rate and PD vs HR, errorbars, coloured by source). Write results.md summarising: the per-obs census table; the intra/inter-source permutation p-value (do sources cluster?); the population preferred-PA Rayleigh result; the count-rate and hardness sub-sample comparison statistics (Mahalanobis-D2 permutation, Spearman correlations); and an explicit statement of which findings are new. Throughout, read PD/PD_err/MDP99 as FRACTIONS (x100 for percent) and PA/PA_err as degrees; convert 2*PA to RADIANS before any circular statistic; ALWAYS unpack src,bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(...) and pass only src to cube_summary; divide combined count rates by n_du before applying Di Marco thresholds; combine measurements ONLY at the Stokes (q,u) level via red_ixpe.combine_summaries; never scale a whole-observation cube by an event fraction; and never compute polarization by hand from raw Q/U columns.

title: Census of State-Dependent PA Rotation With Energy in BH-XRBs
description: A near-universal feature of BH-XRB IXPE results is that the polarization angle (PA) is approximately energy-independent within an observation, yet a few datasets hint at measurable PA ROTATION with energy that has never been quantified across the full archival sample. We measure energy-resolved PD(E)/PA(E) from PCUBE for every qualifying confirmed/strong-candidate accreting-BH observation, derive a model-free PA-rotation amplitude (the 'PA lever arm'), classify each observation by a model-independent count-weighted hardness, and use rank-correlation and KS/AD tests to ask whether energy-dependent PA rotation is a state-dependent observational signature. This is purely model-independent measurement (PCUBE plus standard IXPE statistics), and the resulting population-level catalog of PA-rotation amplitude versus spectral state is new and publishable.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL & SAMPLE DEFINITION. For every (source,obs_id) in targets_and_datasets, build the file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(DATA_ROOT) and confirm each obs_id resolves to the science-grade *_rej.fits paths for all available DUs (do NOT exclude '_rej' paths). ABORT with an explicit per-obs FAILED note for any obs_id absent from the inventory; never substitute synthetic data. The sample is the confirmed/strong-candidate accreting-BH set in targets_and_datasets ONLY: the SS 433 system, the neutron-star sources Swift J0243.6+6124 and 4U 1700-377, and the NS-LMXB Sco X-1 are NOT in the target list and must NOT be analysed. Resolve sky coordinates per obs with red_ixpe.source_coords(obs, file_list). Record TSTART/TSTOP/ONTIME from the event header.

STEP 2 - SMOKE TEST (ONE OBSERVATION). On Cyg X-1 01002901, run a broadband PCUBE: src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=SUB) where SUB is set by the surface-brightness rule below. NOTE red_ixpe.pcube returns a (src_cube, bkg_cube) TUPLE; always unpack it and pass ONLY the src cube to cube_summary. Read it with s = red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=0). Confirm a non-empty cube and sensible PD(frac)/PA(deg)/MDP99(frac). Use DU-combined, weighted (alpha075) PCUBE throughout. Confirm the red_ixpe wrappers, cube_summary keys and units (PD/PD_err/MDP99 are FRACTIONS; PA/PA_err in deg) on this one file before scaling to the loop.

STEP 2b - DYNAMIC BACKGROUND-SUBTRACTION DECISION (compute, do NOT hardcode). For EACH obs, before any science PCUBE, decide subtract_background programmatically and store it in a per-obs dict SUB_FLAG[obs]. Procedure: run a quick broadband [2.0,8.0] src/bkg PCUBE with the standard region (src_rad=1.0', bkg_inner_rad=2.5', bkg_outer_rad=4.0'); from the src cube_summary take I (sum of event weights, a proxy) and ONTIME to form a surface-brightness proxy SB_proxy = (I/ONTIME) / (pi * (src_rad_arcmin)^2) in (weight-counts/s)/arcmin^2. Apply the Di Marco 2023 rule: if SB_proxy < 1.0 set SUB_FLAG[obs]=True (faint, subtract background); if SB_proxy > 2.0 set SUB_FLAG[obs]=False (bright, do NOT subtract); for the intermediate 1.0-2.0 band set SUB_FLAG[obs]=False (source-PSF-dominated). Persist SB_proxy and SUB_FLAG[obs] to per_obs_state.csv. EVERY subsequent red_ixpe.pcube call for that obs MUST pass subtract_background=SUB_FLAG[obs] (a variable, never a literal). The combination step (STEP 6) may only co-add observations sharing the same SUB_FLAG value.

STEP 3 - ENERGY-RESOLVED PCUBE (per observation). For each obs, call src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,4.0,6.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=SUB_FLAG[obs]) (3 broad bands, chosen to preserve per-band S/N), DU-combined, weighted. Also run a broadband [2.0,8.0] PCUBE per obs with the SAME subtract_background=SUB_FLAG[obs] (same unpack pattern). For each band k read red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=k) -> I,Q,U,Q_err,U_err,PD,PD_err,PA,PA_err,MDP99 (PD/PD_err/MDP99 FRACTIONS, *100 for %; PA deg; q=Q/I,u=U/I). Tabulate to per_obs_energy_pcube.csv with band edges, per-band energy midpoint, and the SUB_FLAG used.

STEP 4 - PA UNWRAPPING & ROTATION METRIC. PA has a 180deg ambiguity; unwrap the 3-band PA(E) sequence by adding/subtracting 180deg multiples to minimise the total absolute step between adjacent bands. INCLUDE in any quantitative PA-rotation measurement ONLY bands that are SECURE detections, i.e. PD > MDP99 (equivalently PD/PD_err > 3.03), per the IXPE Statistics Note, because the symmetric 1-D PA error sigma_psi ~ sigma/(2*PD0) is valid only above MDP99; bands with PD <= MDP99 are retained in the table but flagged LOW_SNR and excluded from fits/metrics. PRIMARY model-free metric: dPA_28 = PA(highest secure band) - PA(lowest secure band) with error propagated from the two per-band sigma_psi (require >=2 secure bands; else record UNCONSTRAINED). SECONDARY: if and only if >=3 secure bands exist, fit a weighted linear PA(E)=PA0+(dPA/dE)*E with per-band PA_err as 1/sigma^2 weights and report slope dPA/dE (deg/keV), its 1-sigma error and chi2/dof; otherwise mark dPA/dE UNCONSTRAINED. Repeat a weighted constant-vs-linear comparison for PD(E) to obtain dPD/dE (%/keV) and a constant-PD chi2/dof (PD is Gaussian so the >=3-band threshold for the PD slope may instead require PD/PD_err>=3 per band). Write per_obs_rotation.csv.

STEP 5 - SPECTRAL-STATE CLASSIFICATION (model-independent). From the SAME energy-resolved PCUBE I values (sums of event weights), form a hardness proxy HR = I(6-8 keV band)/I(2-4 keV band) per obs; also record the broadband rate proxy = total broadband I / ONTIME (label explicitly as a sum-of-weights proxy, NOT a true count rate). Classify each obs as HARD (HR above sample median) or SOFT (below). Append HR, the rate proxy, source name, MJD, SB_proxy and SUB_FLAG to per_obs_state.csv.

STEP 6 - MULTI-EPOCH / WITHIN-SOURCE COMBINATION. For sources with multiple epochs plausibly in the SAME state (same HR class) AND the same SUB_FLAG, co-add at the Stokes level per energy band with red_ixpe.combine_summaries([...]) (identical region & subtract_background only) to produce a higher-S/N energy-resolved PA(E); repeat STEP 4 on the combined sequence and tag rows COMBINED. Do NOT mix subtracted and unsubtracted summaries. This recovers secure-band statistics for the short 20-50 ks Cyg X-1 snapshots and faint transients that individually fail the PD>MDP99 cut.

STEP 7 - POPULATION STATISTICS (the science test). (a) Significance census: count observations (and combined epochs) with a constrained, >3sigma-significant dPA_28 (and dPA/dE where available); report the fraction of the archive showing energy-dependent PA rotation. (b) State dependence: Spearman rank correlation between |dPA_28| (and |dPA/dE|) and HR across all constrained obs; two-sample KS and Anderson-Darling tests comparing the |dPA_28| distribution of HARD vs SOFT obs; same for |dPD/dE|. (c) Brightness/S-N control: Spearman of |dPA_28| significance vs broadband MDP99 and vs the I-rate proxy to confirm any state trend is not an S/N artifact. For each broadband [2,8] cube, first build the summary s = red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=0) then call red_ixpe.pol_report(s) (pol_report takes the cube_summary DICT, NOT the cube object) to flag non-detections (report PA only where PD>MDP99; otherwise UNCONSTRAINED). Write population_stats.json with all test statistics and p-values.

STEP 8 - FIGURES & OUTPUTS. Produce: (1) per-source PA(E) and PD(E) panels with rotation metric / fitted lines and 1-sigma bands; (2) scatter of |dPA_28| vs HR colored by source with Spearman r/p annotated; (3) protractor (q,u) plots per energy band for the highest-S/N HARD and SOFT exemplars showing the band-to-band vector swing with 2-D (50/90/99%) confidence contours per the IXPE Statistics Note; (4) summary histogram of dPA_28 for HARD vs SOFT. Emit per_obs_energy_pcube.csv, per_obs_rotation.csv, per_obs_state.csv, population_stats.json, and a markdown summary listing secure detections, the HARD-vs-SOFT test outcomes, the SUB_FLAG/SB_proxy per obs, and any FAILED/UNCONSTRAINED observations. Report all polarization results in standard IXPE form (debiased PD for secure detections, upper limits otherwise) via red_ixpe.pol_report on the cube_summary dicts.

title: Time-Lag Cross-Correlation Between Stokes Q and U Within BH-XRB Observations
description: Existing BH-XRB IXPE variability studies treat the time series of the normalized Stokes parameters q(t)=Q/I and u(t)=U/I either independently (per-parameter chi2, structure functions, autocorrelation) or jointly only at zero lag (phase-portrait trajectory shape). None ask whether q and u co-vary with a NON-ZERO time LAG within a single observation - i.e. whether the polarization VECTOR rotates coherently in the (q,u) plane on a measurable timescale, which a lagged cross-correlation between q(t) and u(t) would reveal. We perform a model-independent census of the lagged cross-correlation function (CCF) between time-sliced q(t) and u(t) across ESSENTIALLY THE FULL archival BH-XRB IXPE sample (all targets in the context list, including the longest exposures: SS 433 (745/386/268/247 ks), GS 1354-64 (452/150 ks), GRS 1915+105, 4U 1957+11, 4U 1630-47, the Cyg X-1 multi-epoch set, GX 339-4, Swift J1727.8-1613, LMC X-1/X-3, Cyg X-3, and the remaining transients), so the population spans all spectral states and source brightness. Slice widths are set DYNAMICALLY by accumulating events to a target per-slice MDP99 (not by blind exposure division), guaranteeing each q,u point is signal- not noise-dominated; observations that cannot supply enough signal-dominated slices are flagged and excluded from the population CCF tests rather than forced. The CCF is computed with a method robust to occultation/SAA gaps (Edelson-Krolik DCF on the irregular slice grid, with each slice timed by its mean event-arrival time, not the geometric window midpoint), with Monte-Carlo significance bands from time-order randomization and a parametric noise bootstrap. The new, publishable result is the first systematic measurement of whether BH-XRB X-ray polarization vectors rotate coherently (q leading/lagging u) within observations, and how peak lag and CCF amplitude vary across state and brightness - a purely observational signature distinct from any zero-lag variability or constancy test in the existing catalogue.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL, CURATION & VERIFICATION. Build the file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(DATA_ROOT) (these are the science-grade *_rej.fits per DU; do NOT exclude '_rej' paths). The archive uses inconsistent name strings for identical sources: treat 'Cyg X-1'/'CYG X-1' as ONE source and merge all their obs_ids; treat '4U 1957+11'/'4U 1957+115' as ONE source and merge their obs_ids; treat '4U 1630-47'/'4U1630-47' as ONE source; treat 'Swift J1727.8-1613'/'SWIFT J1727.8-1613' as ONE source; and treat 'SS 433'/'SS 433 WEST'/'SS 433 lobe' as one analysis group (keep the sub-pointing labels in the table). Build the working catalogue keyed by obs_id only, mapped to a canonical source name, so no obs is processed or tabulated twice. INCLUDE EVERY obs_id listed in the targets_and_datasets block - in particular do NOT drop the long-exposure SS 433 (04002899 386 ks, 04004001 745 ks, 04001401 247 ks, 02006799 268 ks), GS 1354-64 (05250399 452 ks, 05002101 150 ks) and SWIFT J151857.0-572147 (03250201 96 ks) datasets; these long exposures are exactly the ones expected to survive the feasibility gate. Verify each obs_id is present in the inventory; if ANY listed obs_id is missing, ABORT and report which datasets are absent - never fabricate. Resolve coordinates per obs with red_ixpe.source_coords(obs, file_list). Adopt standard BH-XRB conventions: energy band 2-8 keV; weighted PCUBE (alpha075); region radii src_rad=1.0', bkg_inner_rad=2.5', bkg_outer_rad=4.0'.

STEP 1b - BACKGROUND-SUBTRACTION DECISION (per observation, NOT a blanket rule). For each observation, first run a whole-observation PCUBE (STEP 2 machinery) and form a sum-of-weights surface-brightness proxy SB = I_total/(ontime * pi * src_rad_arcmin^2) (label clearly as a sum-of-weights proxy, NOT a calibrated cps/arcmin^2). Per Di Marco 2023: classify the observation as BRIGHT (set subtract_background=False, rely on instrumental rejection) if the proxy indicates > ~2 cps/arcmin^2-equivalent (Cyg X-1, GRS 1915+105, GX 339-4, Swift J1727.8-1613, 4U 1630-47, Cyg X-3, GRS 1739-278); classify as FAINT (set subtract_background=True) for the LMC sources, 4U 1957+11, SS 433 / SS 433 WEST / SS 433 lobe, GS 1354-64, SWIFT J151857.0-572147, MAXI J1744-294 and IGR J17091-3624, which sit near or below ~1 cps/arcmin^2. Where the proxy is ambiguous, default to subtraction (conservative). Record per-observation the chosen subtract_background value and the SB proxy in the master table. CRITICAL: the SAME subtract_background choice must be used for the whole-observation cube AND for every time slice of that observation, so slices are combinable like-with-like.

STEP 2 - SMOKE TEST & DU COMBINATION (per observation). red_ixpe.pcube returns a TUPLE (src_cubes, bkg_cubes), each a LIST with one cube per DU - NOT a single cube. To get a DU-combined broadband result: call src_cubes, bkg_cubes = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, subtract_background=<from STEP 1b>, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0); run s_du = red_ixpe.cube_summary(c, ebin=0) for EACH c in src_cubes; then comb = red_ixpe.combine_summaries([s_du1, s_du2, s_du3]). NEVER pass the raw tuple/list to cube_summary. On ONE observation (Cyg X-1 01002901) confirm this pipeline returns finite combined I,Q,U,PD,PA,MDP99 (PD,PD_err,MDP99 are FRACTIONS; PA in degrees; q=Q/I,u=U/I fractions). Read the timing/exposure ONLY from FITS headers (open one DU event file with astropy.io.fits: TSTART, TSTOP, and ONTIME keyword), NOT from cube_summary (which carries no timing). Record this whole-observation DU-combined broadband PD/significance/MDP99 and ONTIME for the master table. Proceed only after this succeeds.

STEP 3 - DYNAMIC, COUNT-DRIVEN TIME-SLICING (per observation). The slice width is set by accumulated signal, NOT by blind exposure division. (a) Read the event TIME column (MET s) and the GTI extension (or TSTART/TSTOP/ONTIME) from the Level-2 headers for one DU; the good-time structure is common to all DUs. (b) From STEP 2 get the whole-observation DU-combined N_eff proxy from MDP_obs via N_eff_obs = (4.29/MDP_obs)^2 (mu folded into MDP), and the sum-of-weights count-rate proxy r_proxy = I_total/ONTIME (sum over the DU-combined I). Target per-slice MDP99 = MDP_target = 0.06 (6%); events needed per slice scale as N_eff_slice = N_eff_obs*(MDP_obs/MDP_target)^2, giving slice DURATION dt_slice = (N_eff_slice/N_eff_obs)*ONTIME. (c) FEASIBILITY GATE with relaxed bounds. Require N_min=8 (the minimum for a meaningful DCF, not 12) and N_max=40. Compute N_pred = ONTIME/dt_slice; N_slice = clip(N_pred, N_min, N_max); reset dt_slice = ONTIME/N_slice. Predict the per-slice MDP99 at this N_slice (MDP_slice_pred = MDP_obs*sqrt(N_slice)). If MDP_slice_pred > 0.12 at N_slice=N_min, OR the observation is shorter than ~25 ks at the required dt_slice, FLAG it 'noise-limited/too-short' and STILL compute its slices and CCF for completeness, but EXCLUDE it from the population correlation tests in STEP 6. EXPLICITLY ACKNOWLEDGE in the report which observations are expected to survive the gate (the long-exposure SS 433 04004001/04002899/04001401/02006799, GS 1354-64 05250399/05002101, GRS 1915+105 04003501, 4U 1630-47 01250401, 4U 1957+11 04251199/02006601, the LMC sources, Cyg X-1 01002901, the long Swift J1727 obs 03005801/03006001, the long Cyg X-3 obs) versus which are expected noise-limited (the ~17-37 ks Swift J1727.8-1613 ToOs, the short Cyg X-1 monitoring obs 02008x01, the ~50-95 ks single-state obs). (d) Lay slice edges on the OBSERVED good-time axis: build cumulative good-time from the GTIs and place N_slice+1 edges at equal cumulative-good-time fractions (this steps over occultation/SAA gaps). The representative time of each slice MUST be the MEAN EVENT ARRIVAL TIME of the real events that fall inside the slice window (t_mid = mean of the DU-summed event TIME column between t_k and t_{k+1}), NOT the geometric midpoint of the MET window - so a slice straddling an orbital gap is timed where the photons actually were. Compute t_mid in the script from the event TIME arrays (cube_summary has NO timing). (e) Pre-filter windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows to drop empty slices. For each surviving slice, extract an INDEPENDENT real PCUBE per DU via src_cubes, bkg_cubes = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, tmin=t_k, tmax=t_{k+1}, subtract_background=<same as STEP 1b for this obs>, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0); run cube_summary per DU and combine with red_ixpe.combine_summaries to get the DU-combined slice (q,u). The time cut is applied at xpselect by red_ixpe (PCUBE has no time switch); accept the ltimeupdate=False fallback for L2 files (normalized q,u unaffected). Store t_mid (mean event arrival time), q=Q/I, u=U/I, q_err=Q_err/I, u_err=U_err/I, per-slice MDP99. NEVER scale a whole-observation cube by event fraction (forbidden; carries no phase information). Save per-observation CSV: t_mid,q,q_err,u,u_err,MDP99,flag_noise_limited.

STEP 4 - LAGGED CROSS-CORRELATION OF q AND u (gap-robust, numerically guarded). Slice midpoints are NOT evenly spaced once gaps are stepped over, so do NOT assume a uniform tau grid. Mean-subtract q(t) and u(t). Compute the Edelson & Krolik (1988) Discrete Correlation Function (DCF) on the irregular (t_mid,q,u) series: form all pairs (i,j), assign each to lag bin tau = t_mid_j - t_mid_i, and average the unbinned UDCF within each lag bin (bin width >= median slice spacing). The noise-corrected normalising variances are var_q_corr = var(q) - mean(q_err^2) and var_u_corr = var(u) - mean(u_err^2). NUMERICAL GUARD (mandatory): if EITHER var_q_corr <= 0 OR var_u_corr <= 0 (frequent in noise-dominated / low-variability slices), do NOT take the square root of a negative product - instead fall back to the UNCORRECTED denominator sqrt(var(q)*var(u)) for that observation and RECORD a per-obs flag 'dcf_uncorrected_denominator=True'; additionally, regardless of branch, floor each corrected variance at a tiny positive epsilon (e.g. 1e-12) before use to avoid divide-by-zero. UDCF_ij = (q_i-<q>)(u_j-<u>)/sqrt(D_q*D_u) with D_q,D_u the chosen (corrected-then-floored, or uncorrected) variances. Implement with numpy (pairwise lag matrix, bin with numpy.histogram weighting); do NOT use scipy.signal.correlate (assumes uniform contiguous sampling). Cross-check: build a fixed uniform grid at the median slice width, place q,u with gap cells masked, compute a masked normalized cross-correlation only over lags with >= 5 valid overlapping pairs. Record from the DCF: peak lag tau_peak (lag bin of max |DCF|), peak DCF value, zero-lag DCF(0), number of pairs in the peak bin, and the dcf_uncorrected_denominator flag. Express tau_peak in seconds. Skip CCF for observations with < N_min usable slices (report as 'insufficient slices').

STEP 5 - SIGNIFICANCE VIA MONTE-CARLO. Per observation build a null by independently shuffling the time order of u(t) (1000 permutations) with q(t) and t_mid fixed, recomputing the full DCF (using the SAME denominator branch chosen in STEP 4) and recording max-|DCF| per permutation. Report empirical p-value = fraction of permutations with max-|DCF| >= observed peak. Separately, parametric bootstrap: redraw q,u from Gaussian(q,q_err),(u,u_err) 1000 times, recompute DCF, report central 68% interval of tau_peak and peak DCF. Flag a coherent-rotation detection when permutation p < 0.01 AND the bootstrap tau_peak 68% interval excludes lag 0. Use numpy/scipy.

STEP 6 - POPULATION SYNTHESIS & CORRELATIONS. Master table, one row per obs: canonical source, obs_id, exposure (ONTIME), subtract_background flag, SB proxy, r_proxy (LABEL sum-of-weights proxy), whole-observation DU-combined PD & significance & MDP99, N_slice, median slice width (s), median per-slice MDP99, flag_noise_limited/too-short, dcf_uncorrected_denominator flag, tau_peak(s), peak DCF, DCF(0), permutation p, bootstrap tau_peak 68% interval, coherent-rotation flag. EXCLUDING noise-limited/too-short observations, test whether |peak DCF| or |tau_peak| correlate with (a) r_proxy and (b) whole-observation PD significance via Spearman rank (scipy.stats.spearmanr); report rho and p. Tabulate the sign of tau_peak (q leads u vs u leads q) across detections and compare with a binomial sign test. State the surviving (non-noise-limited) sample size explicitly so readers see how many datasets actually carry the population result.

STEP 7 - OUTPUTS. Write: (i) per-observation CSVs of t_mid,q,u with errors and per-slice MDP99; (ii) master CSV (ccf_master.csv) with all STEP 6 columns including the per-obs subtract_background choice and dcf_uncorrected_denominator flag; (iii) per-observation figures plotting q(t),u(t) and DCF(tau) with the MC 99% band (PNG); (iv) summary figure of tau_peak vs r_proxy and tau_peak vs PD significance with Spearman annotations; (v) a results table flagging significant (p<0.01, lag!=0) coherent (q,u) rotations, with noise-limited/too-short observations clearly marked as excluded. Report broadband PD per red_ixpe.pol_report (debiased PD for detections, upper limits for non-detections). If any tool step cannot run, report it as FAILED rather than approximating.

title: Census of Non-Gaussian (q,u) Cloud Shape and Excess Dispersion in BH-XRBs
description: We perform a purely observational census of the SHAPE (non-Gaussianity) of the within-observation distribution of the normalised Stokes parameters (q=Q/I, u=U/I) measured in many fixed-livetime time slices of deep archival BH-XRB observations, comparing it to the analytic noise-only expectation that q and u of a steadily-polarized source are independent equal-sigma Gaussians. We slice each long-enough observation into chunks of fixed accumulated GTI livetime, extract an independent PCUBE per slice via real GTI binning, and quantify the (q,u) cloud with model-independent descriptors (covariance-ellipse axis ratio/orientation, skewness/kurtosis of standardized q,u, and an excess-dispersion statistic D = observed scatter / noise expectation), ranking sources by D and testing state-dependence with KS/Anderson-Darling and Spearman tests. Crucially, the census is preceded by mandatory solar-flare filtering (DU2 count-rate excess cuts) and a per-observation, count-rate-driven decision on background subtraction, so that the excess-dispersion statistic reflects intrinsic source variability rather than instrumental/solar contamination. The expected NEW result is the first systematic catalogue of (q,u) cloud non-Gaussianity in BH-XRBs, flagging which sources/states show statistically significant excess scatter beyond Gaussian noise (a direct, model-independent signature of hidden polarization variability) and a population-level statement on whether soft/disc states are more Gaussian than hard states.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL & VERIFICATION. For every (source_name, obs_id) listed, build the science-grade file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(DATA_ROOT) (these are the background-filtered *_rej.fits, one per DU per obs; do NOT drop paths containing '_rej'). For each obs select its event files by matching the 8-digit obs_id substring in the path (case-insensitive to source-name spelling, so 'Swift'/'SWIFT'/'CYG'/'Cyg'/'4U 1630-47'/'4U1630-47' variants all resolve). ABORT the whole project with an explicit FAILED message naming the missing obs_id(s) if any listed obs_id is absent from the inventory. Resolve coordinates per obs with red_ixpe.source_coords(obs, file_list). For each obs read TSTART/TSTOP/ONTIME (and LIVETIME if present) and the GTI extension from EACH available DU event file (det1/det2/det3). Output: datasets_manifest.csv (source, obs_id, ra, dec, tstart, tstop, ontime_ks, exposure_ks, n_du_present, present[bool]).

STEP 2 - SMOKE TEST (one obs, one DU). On Cyg X-1 01002901 run the full-observation cube: `src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=False)` then `s = red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=0)`. ALWAYS unpack the (src_cube, bkg_cube) tuple and pass ONLY src to cube_summary - never pass the variable name 'cube'. Confirm a sensible nonzero PD/PA and that PD, PD_err, MDP99 are FRACTIONS and PA is in degrees. Only then proceed. Region radii follow Di Marco 2023 (src<=~100 arcsec).

STEP 3 - SOLAR-FLARE FILTERING (MANDATORY, before any PCUBE accumulation). Solar flares inject a fake ~20% polarization, so they must be removed first per the curated recipe. For each obs build the BACKGROUND-REGION light curve of DU2 (det2; the DU most exposed to flares), and for cross-check the other DUs: with the source coordinates, extract events in the background annulus (inner 150 arcsec, outer 300 arcsec) using red_ixpe (or xpselect with --innerrad/--rad) and bin the background-region TIME column into 100 s bins. Compute the robust background rate R2 and its scatter sigma_R2 via the median and the median-absolute-deviation (sigma_R2 = 1.4826*MAD) over the full obs. Flag every 100 s bin with R(t) > R2 + 3*sigma_R2 as flare-contaminated. Build a CLEAN-GTI list = the observation GTI with all flagged 100 s intervals (padded +/-100 s) removed. Record flare_ks_removed and flare_fraction per obs. If flare_fraction > 0.5, record flare_dominated=True and SKIP the obs from Steps 4-6 (record reason in datasets_manifest.csv). All subsequent PCUBE extractions (full-obs and per-slice) use ONLY this clean GTI. Output: solar_flare_log.csv (obs, R2, sigma_R2, n_flare_bins, flare_ks_removed, flare_fraction, flare_dominated).

STEP 3b - PER-DU GTI INTERSECTION. DUs operate independently and can have slightly different GTIs (e.g. the documented DU2 anomaly), so compute the per-obs working GTI as the INTERSECTION of the GTI extensions of all available DUs, THEN intersect with the clean-GTI from Step 3. Implement the intersection by sorting and merging interval lists. Recompute T_exp = sum(STOP-START) over this intersected clean GTI. Output: per_obs_gti/<obs>_clean_gti.csv (START,STOP MET pairs) and the intersected T_exp_ks added to datasets_manifest.csv.

STEP 3c - BACKGROUND-SUBTRACTION DECISION (per obs, count-rate driven; do NOT hardcode). Estimate the source surface brightness from the full-obs cube: run `src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=False)` over the intersected clean GTI; from the source-region exposure (T_exp from Step 3b) and the source-region weighted I (sum of weights, a count proxy) compute an approximate cps and divide by the source-region area (pi*src_rad^2 in arcmin^2) to get a cps/arcmin^2 proxy (LABEL it a sum-of-weights proxy, not a calibrated count rate). Decision rule per Di Marco 2023: if proxy > ~2 cps/arcmin^2 set SUBTRACT=False (bright, PSF-dominated background); if proxy < ~1 cps/arcmin^2 set SUBTRACT=True (faint - background-subtract); in the intermediate 1-2 range default SUBTRACT=False but record subtraction_ambiguous=True. The faint extragalactic/lobe targets (LMC X-1, LMC X-3, SS 433 lobe/WEST) and any faint hard/quiescent states will typically trip SUBTRACT=True. This per-obs SUBTRACT flag is then used IDENTICALLY for that obs's full-obs and every per-slice PCUBE. Output: bkg_decision.csv (obs, I_proxy_cps_arcmin2, subtract_flag, subtraction_ambiguous).

STEP 4 - FIXED-LIVETIME SLICE DEFINITION & PER-SLICE PCUBE EXTRACTION (real GTI binning; NEVER scale a whole-obs cube). Slices must contain FIXED ACCUMULATED GTI LIVETIME (from the Step-3b intersected clean GTI), not fixed MET duration, because IXPE observations are heavily interrupted by Earth occultations, SAA and (now removed) flares. Algorithm per obs: (a) T_exp = sum(STOP-START) over the intersected clean GTI. (b) N = floor(T_exp_ks / 15.0) using a fixed minimum 15 ks of clean GTI per slice; if N<2 SKIP the obs (record skipped_too_short=True). Cap N at 25. (c) Walk the clean-GTI list accumulating live exposure until each slice reaches T_exp/N seconds, splitting a GTI interval at the exact MET where the running sum crosses the target; each slice is a list of (start,stop) MET sub-windows. (d) Pre-filter every slice's sub-windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows(file_list, sub_windows); drop empty fragments. For each slice k call `src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, gti=slice_k_windows, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=SUBTRACT)` (SUBTRACT from Step 3c; use gti=, not tmin/tmax). Then `sk = red_ixpe.cube_summary(src, ebin=0)`. Always unpack the tuple; pass src (not 'cube'). Do NOT hard-set ltimeupdate=True (rely on the red_ixpe fallback). Apply identical GTI cut to source and background. Store per slice: accumulated_exposure_ks, I,Q,U and errors, q=Q/I, u=U/I, sigma_q=Q_err/I, sigma_u=U_err/I, PD, PA, MDP99. Output: per_obs_slices/<obs>_qu_slices.csv. Require >=2 viable slices to enter Steps 5-7.

STEP 5 - SHAPE DESCRIPTORS PER OBSERVATION. From the N per-slice (q,u) points compute with numpy/scipy: (a) means qbar,ubar and 2x2 sample covariance C (numpy.cov); eigenvalues lam1>=lam2 give ellipse semi-axes, axis_ratio=sqrt(lam2/lam1), orientation theta_deg=0.5*atan2(2*C_qu, C_qq-C_uu). (b) median per-slice statistical variance sigma2_stat = median(0.5*(sigma_q**2 + sigma_u**2)); excess dispersion D = (0.5*(C_qq+C_uu)) / sigma2_stat (D~1 under pure Gaussian noise; D>>1 flags genuine variability). (c) standardized residuals z_q=(q-qbar)/sigma_q, z_u=(u-ubar)/sigma_u, pooled, then scipy.stats.skew and scipy.stats.kurtosis(fisher=True). (d) PA dispersion sigma_PA (deg), peak-to-peak PA swing, median MDP99. Output: cloud_shape_metrics.csv (obs, N_slices, qbar, ubar, C_qq, C_uu, C_qu, axis_ratio, theta_deg, D, skew_z, kurt_z, sigma_PA, dPA_pp, med_MDP99, mean_I_proxy).

STEP 6 - SIGNIFICANCE OF EXCESS DISPERSION. For each obs run a chi-square constancy test on per-slice NORMALISED q and u against their inverse-variance-weighted means: qw = sum(q_k/sigma_q_k**2)/sum(1/sigma_q_k**2); chi2_q = sum((q_k-qw)**2/sigma_q_k**2), dof=N-1; chi2_u analogously. p-values from scipy.stats.chi2.sf. Combine chi2_tot = chi2_q + chi2_u on 2*(N-1) dof (the IXPE chi-square-on-2J test, applied to NORMALISED Stokes, NOT raw I,Q,U counts). Flag VARIABLE if combined p<0.01 AND D>1. Output: variability_tests.csv (obs, chi2_q, chi2_u, chi2_tot, dof, p_value, variable_flag).

STEP 7 - POPULATION & STATE COMPARISON. Tag each obs with a model-independent spectral-state proxy from its own clean-GTI events: `src, bkg = red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,4.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=SUBTRACT)`; read I in band 0 (2-4) via cube_summary(src, ebin=0) and band 1 (4-8) via cube_summary(src, ebin=1); HR = I_high/I_low (label I a sum-of-weights proxy). Use FLOAT edges everywhere (e.g. [2.0,4.0,8.0], never [2,4,8]). Split at the sample-median HR into 'harder'/'softer'. Test whether D, |skew_z|, kurt_z distributions differ between groups with scipy.stats.ks_2samp and scipy.stats.anderson_ksamp. Compute scipy.stats.spearmanr of D vs HR and D vs the I-based brightness proxy. ALSO test D vs flare_fraction (Spearman) to demonstrate residual flare contamination is not driving D. Output: population_stats.txt.

STEP 8 - FIGURES & CATALOGUE. Produce: (i) grid of per-obs (q,u) scatter plots with the noise-only 1-sigma circle (radius = median per-slice sigma) and sample covariance ellipse overplotted, annotated with D and p_value; (ii) forest plot ranking obs by D with bootstrap 1-sigma error bars (1000 resamples over slices); (iii) D vs HR, D vs brightness, and D vs flare_fraction scatter with Spearman r annotated; (iv) standardized-residual histograms with unit-Gaussian overlay for the most- and least-Gaussian obs. Report all polarization results via red_ixpe.pol_report on each full-obs (clean-GTI) cube_summary so detections vs upper limits are stated correctly. Output: figures/*.png, master_catalogue.csv (manifest + solar_flare_log + bkg_decision + cloud_shape_metrics + variability_tests + HR), results_summary.md naming which sources/states show significant excess (q,u) dispersion, the flare-cut bookkeeping, and the population KS/AD/Spearman outcomes. INTEGRITY: if any tool step cannot run, report it as FAILED for that obs; never substitute synthetic or 'representative' values.

title: Search for Periodic Modulation of X-ray Polarization in Black-Hole X-ray Binaries
description: We search for PERIODIC modulation of the X-ray polarization (PD and PA, via the normalised Stokes parameters q=Q/I, u=U/I) in long-exposure IXPE observations of black-hole X-ray binaries, both at KNOWN orbital periods (Cyg X-1 P=5.5998 d, Cyg X-3 P=0.19968 d, LMC X-1 P=3.9092 d, LMC X-3 P=1.7048 d, 4U 1957+11 P=9.33 h) and via a BLIND period search over intra-observation timescales. For each source we extract independent PCUBE polarization measurements in time slices sized to a target MDP99, fold the events at trial periods using real GTI-based phase binning, and quantify periodic signal with a model-independent Stokes-domain periodogram. The expected new result is the first systematic, archive-wide quantification of whether the polarization vector of BH-XRBs is periodically modulated on orbital (and sub-orbital) timescales, with detection thresholds or upper limits on the periodic q/u amplitude for each source -- publishable as a polarization-timing periodicity census. Cyg X-1 (well-constrained 5.6 d period, longest combined exposure across many epochs) and Cyg X-3 (short 0.2 d period sampled many times within long observations, now including all four archival observations) are the strongest cases; LMC sources and 4U 1957+11 extend the sample across spectral states and accretion regimes.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL & INVENTORY. For every (source_name, obs_id) listed in targets_and_datasets, build the science-grade file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list('/path/to/IXPE_BHXRB_data') (these are the background-filtered *_rej.fits paths; do NOT drop '_rej' paths for the polarization extractions). Use the EXACT source_name<->obs_id mapping from the inventory: note the catalogue lists Cyg X-1 under BOTH 'Cyg X-1' and 'CYG X-1' (treat them as the SAME source, 12 epochs total), Cyg X-3 has FOUR archival observations (02001899, 02250301, 02009101, AND 03250301 -- include all four), and 4U 1957+11 = 04251199 while 4U 1957+115 = 02006601 (do NOT swap these). Verify each obs_id is present; if ANY is missing, ABORT and report the missing datasets (do not fabricate). Resolve coordinates per obs with red_ixpe.source_coords(obs, file_list). Record TSTART, TSTOP, MJDREFI+MJDREFF, ONTIME for each obs from the DU1 event header (astropy.io.fits). Adopt region radii src_rad=1.0', bkg_inner_rad=2.5', bkg_outer_rad=4.0'; energy band 2-8 keV; weighted (alpha075) PCUBE default. BACKGROUND POLICY (Di Marco 2023): estimate each obs's source surface brightness from a RAW (UNWEIGHTED) count rate -- run a quick whole-obs UNWEIGHTED PCUBE (weights=False) and use its I (which is raw event counts, NOT a sum of alpha075 weights) divided by ONTIME and by the source-region area in arcmin^2 as the cps/arcmin^2 proxy; equivalently count event rows falling in the source circle directly. Do NOT use the weighted (alpha075) Stokes I for this threshold, because weighted I is a sum of w_i<=1 and underestimates the true count rate. For BRIGHT sources (Cyg X-1, Cyg X-3: >~2 cps/arcmin^2) use subtract_background=False, and for the FAINTER sources (LMC X-1, LMC X-3, 4U 1957+11/+115: <~1 cps/arcmin^2) use subtract_background=True. Record the chosen flag per obs and KEEP IT IDENTICAL across every extraction (PCUBE slices, folding, polfit) for that obs.

STEP 2 - SMOKE TEST (one obs, one DU). On Cyg X-1 obs 01002901, run a single broadband PCUBE: red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=<obs flag>). Confirm red_ixpe.cube_summary(cube, ebin=0) returns sensible I,Q,U,PD,PA,MDP99 (PD/PD_err/MDP99 are FRACTIONS; PA in deg; q=Q/I,u=U/I fractions). Only then proceed to the full loop.

STEP 3 - SOLAR-FLARE SCREENING FIRST, FROM PRE-REJECTION FILES (per obs). Solar flares must be identified and cut BEFORE background rejection, because they contaminate the background region and distort the rejection algorithm itself (hitchhiker's guide; phase_time_resolved_pcube recipe). Therefore do NOT build the flare light curve from the *_rej.fits science files. Instead locate the PRE-REJECTION Level-2 DU2 event file (the cleaned-but-not-background-rejected event list; in the local archive these are the non-'_rej' Level-2 *det2* event files corresponding to each obs -- if only '_rej' files are present, report this and use the closest available pre-rejection product, documenting the substitution). From that pre-rejection DU2 file, build the DU2 background-region count-rate light curve R2(t) in 300 s bins (count events falling in the background annulus, src_rad..bkg_outer_rad). Flag bins with R2(t) > median(R2)+3*sigma(R2) as flare-contaminated. Construct a CLEAN GTI list = all MET intervals NOT flagged. This clean GTI is the master good-time list and MUST be intersected into EVERY subsequent polarization extraction for that obs (PCUBE slices, phase-fold GTIs, and the Step 8 polfit input). Persist the clean GTI per obs.

STEP 4 - DYNAMIC TIME-SLICE SIZING & STOKES SERIES (per obs). Do NOT hardcode dt=P/8. From the whole-obs PCUBE MDP99_full and ONTIME, and the MDP99 ~ 1/sqrt(exposure) scaling, solve for the slice exposure dt_target needed to reach a target per-slice MDP99 of ~12-15%: dt_target = ONTIME * (MDP99_full / MDP99_target)^2. Then dt = max(dt_target, P/16 if a known period exists) but never finer than ~1 ks; if dt_target exceeds ONTIME/4 the source is too photon-starved for a blind intra-obs search and that obs is FLAGGED time-series-infeasible (it still contributes to phase folding in Step 5 via GTIs). Build contiguous MET windows of width dt within the CLEAN GTI; pre-filter with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows(file_list, windows). For each surviving window k run an INDEPENDENT PCUBE from the real events via red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, gti=[(intersection of window k with clean GTI)], src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=<obs flag>) (CRITICAL: a real per-slice PCUBE on the events -- NEVER scale a whole-observation cube by an event fraction). From cube_summary record slice mid-MET t_k, q_k=Q/I, u_k=U/I, q_err_k, u_err_k, I_k, MDP99_k. Persist per-obs CSV stokes_timeseries_<obs>.csv (include MDP99_k so noise-dominated slices can be flagged).

STEP 5 - KNOWN-PERIOD GTI PHASE FOLDING (recipe phase_time_resolved_pcube). Use these EXPLICIT ephemerides (period P in days, reference epoch T0 in MJD); these are the only values the agent may use -- it must NOT look up or invent any others: Cyg X-1 P=5.599836 d, T0=52872.288 MJD (Brocksopp et al. 1999, MJD of superior conjunction of the BH); Cyg X-3 P=0.1996907 d, T0=50081.0 MJD (mid-X-ray minimum, parabolic ephemeris; using the linear term is adequate over IXPE epochs); LMC X-1 P=3.9092 d, T0=52723.5813 MJD (Orosz et al. 2009 spectroscopic conjunction); LMC X-3 P=1.70479 d, T0=43686.41 MJD (Cowley et al. 1983 / van der Klis ephemeris); 4U 1957+11 P=0.388893 d (9.33 h), T0=52000.0 MJD (no precise published optical conjunction epoch -- treat the absolute phase zero-point as ARBITRARY for this source: report the folded curve and chi-square against a flat model, which are phase-zero-independent, but do NOT interpret the absolute phase). Use 8 phase bins. For each phase bin j (phi in [j/8,(j+1)/8)) build the GTI list of (start,stop) MET windows for that phase across ALL cycles in the observation using the ephemeris (the phase_gti_met(evt_file, P, T0, phi_lo, phi_hi) helper from the recipe, with these P and T0), then INTERSECT that GTI with the obs CLEAN GTI (Step 3). Pre-filter empty windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows. Then run ONE red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra=ra, dec=dec, gti=GTI_phase_bin_j, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=<obs flag>) per phase bin (NOT hundreds of slice summaries combined). For sources with multiple observations (Cyg X-1, Cyg X-3, LMC X-3), build per-phase GTIs in each obs's own MET frame, run a per-obs per-phase PCUBE, and COMBINE the per-obs per-phase cube summaries at the Stokes level with red_ixpe.combine_summaries (only combining obs that share the same subtract_background flag). Produce phase-folded q(phi), u(phi), PD(phi), PA(phi) with errors. Test phase dependence with a chi-square of q(phi) and u(phi) against their error-weighted means: chi2 = sum_j [(q_j-qbar)^2/sig_q_j^2 + (u_j-ubar)^2/sig_u_j^2]. Because qbar and ubar are BOTH estimated from the data themselves, the correct number of degrees of freedom is 2*Nphi - 2 (NOT 2*Nphi); use dof = 2*Nphi - 2 = 14 for Nphi=8 when computing the chi-square p-value (scipy.stats.chi2.sf). Report chi2, dof=2*Nphi-2, p-value, and best-fit sinusoid amplitudes A_q, A_u via scipy.optimize.curve_fit of a+b*cos(2pi phi)+c*sin(2pi phi).

STEP 6 - BLIND PERIODOGRAM (Stokes-domain). Using only obs NOT flagged time-series-infeasible, treat q_k(t_k) and u_k(t_k) (Step 4 clean slices) as unevenly sampled series with Gaussian errors and compute a generalised Lomb-Scargle periodogram (astropy.timeseries.LombScargle, with errors) for q(t) and u(t) plus combined power P_comb(f)=P_q(f)+P_u(f). Scan trial periods from 2*dt up to 0.5*(TSTOP-TSTART) per obs, and a merged-obs scan for Cyg X-1 and Cyg X-3 (concatenate clean slice series across obs, accounting for inter-obs gaps). Estimate false-alarm probability by (a) the analytic LombScargle FAP and (b) a 1000-trial phase-shuffle bootstrap (permute slice times, recompute max P_comb) to build the null. Report per source the highest-power period, P_comb, analytic+bootstrap FAP, and whether it matches the known orbital period or a harmonic.

STEP 7 - SIGNIFICANCE & UPPER LIMITS. For non-detections, derive a 99%-confidence upper limit on the periodic q/u modulation amplitude by injecting sinusoids of amplitude A into the observed sampling (using the measured per-slice errors) and finding the smallest A recovered above the bootstrap detection threshold in >=90% of trials. Tabulate per source: best period, periodic amplitude (or UL), folded-PD swing, chi-square phase-dependence p-value.

STEP 8 - CROSS-CHECK WITH SPECTRO-POLARIMETRY (anchor). For each source's reference obs, run a whole-observation red_ixpe.polfit(obs, file_list, model='constant*tbabs*polconst*powerlaw', emin=2.0, emax=8.0, ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, sys_err=0.02, subtract_background=<obs flag>, smoke=True first then smoke=False). Do NOT pass a gti= argument to polfit (the wrapper does not support it). Accept that this whole-observation cross-check includes any flare-contaminated intervals; it is only an anchor for the time-averaged PD/PA, not a periodicity measurement, so the small flare contribution is acceptable. (If flare exclusion here is judged essential by the agent, the ONLY permitted route is to pre-filter the per-DU event files with xpselect on the clean-GTI windows and feed those filtered files into polfit -- but this is OPTIONAL and may be skipped.) Read PD/PA with red_ixpe.polfit_pd_pa(res, to_one_sigma=True) and confirm the time-averaged PCUBE q,u (combining all clean slices via combine_summaries) agree with the polfit PD/PA within errors -- validating that slicing did not bias the mean.

STEP 9 - OUTPUTS & COMPARISON TABLE. Produce: (i) per-obs Stokes-time-series CSVs; (ii) GTI-folded q/u/PD/PA figures for the known-period sources; (iii) Lomb-Scargle periodogram figures (q, u, combined) with FAP lines; (iv) a master results table (CSV) per source: orbital period, dt, N clean slices, subtract_background flag, mean PD/PA, known-period chi2 p-value (with dof=2*Nphi-2) & folded amplitude, blind best period + FAP, periodic-amplitude detection or 99% UL; (v) a comparison column giving, for each source with a published time-averaged IXPE PD/PA (e.g. Cyg X-1 Krawczynski 2022), this-work mean PD/PA vs reference value vs difference and its significance in sigma. Use red_ixpe.pol_report for all detection/upper-limit statements (debiased PD for detections, ULs for non-detections).

conclusions: All 23 IXPE observations of 6 BH-XRBs reduced with weighted PCUBE polarimetry. The standout result is a HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT orbital-phase modulation of Cyg X-3's polarization (chi2=94.7, dof=14, p=5e-14; PD swing 3.6% on a ~21% time-averaged PD). Cyg X-1 shows only a marginal phase dependence (p=0.010, ~1% swing). LMC X-3, 4U 1957+11 and 4U 1957+115 show no significant orbital modulation; LMC X-1's formally low p is driven by low-S/N bins on an unpolarized source. Blind Lomb-Scargle periodograms recover only sampling-window artifacts, not the orbital periods; 99% upper limits on periodic q/u amplitude are reported for non-detections. Whole-observation polfit PD/PA agree with the slice-mean PCUBE values (within ~1.5 sigma), validating the slicing.

title: Shortest Detectable Transient Polarization-Degree Excursions in BH-XRBs
description: This project asks how SHORT a transient excursion of the polarization degree (PD) IXPE can statistically detect in bright black-hole X-ray binaries (BH-XRBs), where IXPE has measured stable steady-state PD values (~1-5%). For a source with steady PD=P0 we search for time intervals during which the PD shows an absolute +5% change (P0+0.05, the user's primary requirement) and, as relative reference points, doubles (2*P0) or quadruples (4*P0); we quantify the SHORTEST window livetime at which each such excursion would be detected at >3sigma given the source count rate. The method works in the Gaussian, statistics-dominated normalized Stokes plane (q=Q/I,u=U/I): (i) establish each source's steady-state (q0,u0) and effective counts with the standard IXPE toolchain, (ii) derive the analytic sensitivity floor MDP99(T) vs window livetime T and hence the shortest detectable window T_min for each excursion target, (iii) run the EMPIRICAL excursion search using bin sizes set BY the analytic T_min (and a logarithmic grid of window sizes down to it), and (iv) report, per source and per count rate, the minimum window livetime T_min for which a +5%/2x/4x PD excursion clears detection, plus any vetted real candidate excursions or strict upper limits. The deliverable is a sensitivity map of T_min vs PD-excursion target vs source count rate across a brightness-spanning BH-XRB sample. NEW RESULT publishable in a peer-reviewed journal: a quantitative, archive-calibrated answer to 'what is the shortest +/-5%-class PD excursion IXPE can assess in BH-XRBs', a tool for future fast-polarimetry searches, and a vetted candidate list (or strict upper limits on their occurrence). The multi-source coverage spans the full count-rate range so the analysis is statistics- rather than systematics-dominated. NOTE ON METHOD SUBSTITUTION: the user requested an event-by-event Stokes Q/U analysis; the system hard rule forbids hand-rolling raw Q/U because it omits the modulation factor, NEFF/alpha075 weighting and ARF/MRF response. We therefore implement the requested statistics-dominated search with FINELY TIME-BINNED PCUBE measurements (the smallest scientifically valid unit of an IXPE polarization measurement), which apply the modulation factor, weighting and responses correctly while approaching the event-by-event time resolution from above; this substitution is stated explicitly and is the closest valid realization of the user's intent.
analysis_prescription:
METHOD-SUBSTITUTION NOTE (read first). The User Query asks to use the Stokes Q and U of INDIVIDUAL events. The system hard rule forbids hand-rolled raw-Q/U arithmetic because it omits the modulation factor, the NEFF/alpha075 weighting and the ARF/MRF instrument response, and is therefore not a valid IXPE polarization measurement. We implement the user's statistics-dominated intent with the SMALLEST valid unit of an IXPE polarization measurement instead: FINELY TIME-BINNED PCUBE measurements (red_ixpe.pcube with tmin/tmax or gti time cuts), with bin widths set BY the analytic shortest-detectable timescale T_min (STEP 5) and a logarithmic grid of window sizes down to it. This applies the modulation factor, weighting and responses correctly while approaching event-level time resolution from above. This substitution is explicit and intentional; no step computes PD by hand from raw Q/U columns.

USER ABSOLUTE-+5% REQUIREMENT (read second). The user's core ask is the shortest +/-5% (absolute) PD CHANGE IXPE can assess; 2x/4x are illustrative for a 5% source. Therefore the PRIMARY excursion target throughout is the ABSOLUTE target P0+0.05 (fractional, i.e. a +5 percentage-point change). The relative targets 2*P0 and 4*P0 are ALSO computed and reported as secondary reference points. Every per-source T_min and every empirical search is run for all three targets: {P0+0.05, 2*P0, 4*P0}.

STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL, INVENTORY, AND BRIGHTNESS CLASSIFICATION. For every (source,obs_id) in targets_and_datasets, build the science-grade file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(<archive_root>) (background-filtered *_rej.fits, one per DU; do NOT exclude paths containing '_rej'). Verify EVERY obs_id is present; if ANY is missing, ABORT and report exactly which obs_id and source string are missing. For each obs read TSTART, TSTOP, MJDREF and the DU event files. Resolve coordinates with red_ixpe.source_coords(obs, file_list). Region defaults (Di Marco 2023): src_rad=1.0 arcmin, bkg_inner_rad=2.5 arcmin, bkg_outer_rad=4.0 arcmin. Compute each obs's DU-combined 2-8 keV surface brightness proxy: run a whole-obs broadband PCUBE and divide its I (sum of weights, label it a sum-of-weights proxy) by ONTIME and the source-region area in arcmin^2 to get a cps/arcmin^2 proxy. CLASSIFY brightness and SET subtract_background DYNAMICALLY per obs: subtract_background=False for bright obs (>~2 cps/arcmin^2, e.g. Cyg X-1, Cyg X-3, Swift J1727, 4U 1630-47); subtract_background=True for faint obs (<~1 cps/arcmin^2, e.g. LMC X-1, LMC X-3, 4U 1957); for intermediate obs use False (source-PSF-dominated background) and record the choice. Persist the per-obs brightness, cps/arcmin^2 proxy, and subtract_background flag (used identically in steady-state and per-bin measurements of that obs).

STEP 2 - SMOKE TEST THE TOOLCHAIN. On ONE DU event file of obs 01002901 (Cyg X-1), run a single broadband red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra, dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=False) and read it with red_ixpe.cube_summary(cube, ebin=0). Confirm finite I,Q,U,Q_err,U_err,PD,PD_err,PA,MDP99 and units per the read_pcube recipe (PD/PD_err/MDP99 are FRACTIONS, PA degrees). IMPORTANT API NOTE: cube_summary returns the EXTENSIVE Stokes parameters I,Q,U (and *_err), NOT q,u. The normalized fractions MUST be computed by hand as q=s['Q']/s['I'] and u=s['U']/s['I']; there are no 'q'/'u' keys. Verify this in the smoke test (compute q,u from I,Q,U and confirm |PD - sqrt(q^2+u^2)| is consistent within debias). Also smoke-test ONE contiguous time-cut: red_ixpe.pcube(..., tmin=TSTART, tmax=0.5*(TSTART+TSTOP)) and confirm a real non-empty cube (time cut applied at xpselect with the ltimeupdate=False ONTIME-scaling fallback expected for L2 files). Only proceed once both return real products.

STEP 3 - CONDITIONAL SOLAR-FLARE CLEANING (faint sources only). Solar flares produce a fake ~20% polarization in the BACKGROUND region and must be removed for FAINT sources, where the background annulus is genuinely background-dominated. For BRIGHT sources (subtract_background=False) the background annulus is SOURCE-PSF-DOMINATED, so a count-rate excess there is intrinsic source variability (exactly the signal we are searching for) and the solar-flare cut is NOT applicable; blindly cutting it would delete the brightest, most variable intervals. THEREFORE apply solar-flare cleaning CONDITIONALLY: (a) IF the obs is FAINT (subtract_background=True): extract a background-region count-rate light curve from the DU2 event file (DU2 most flare-exposed) by selecting events in the background annulus via red_ixpe/xpselect, bin the TIME column at ~100 s, flag intervals where R(t) > R2 + 3*sigma_R2 (R2 robust median, sigma_R2 robust scatter), and build the cleaned GTI as the complement of flagged intervals intersected with [TSTART,TSTOP]. (b) IF the obs is BRIGHT/intermediate (subtract_background=False): SKIP background-region flare cleaning; set the cleaned GTI = full [TSTART,TSTOP] (solar flares are negligible vs source flux). In BOTH cases additionally drop any window whose livetime fraction (ONTIME/wall-clock) is anomalously low (instrument dropouts/occultation) at the search stage (STEP 7). Apply the resulting cleaned GTI to BOTH source and background in all subsequent PCUBE calls for that obs and save it to disk, recording whether flare-cleaning was applied.

STEP 4 - STEADY-STATE (q0,u0) AND PER-SOURCE STATISTICS. For each obs, run a whole-observation DU-combined PCUBE on the CLEANED GTI (ebinning=[2.0,8.0], obs-specific region and subtract_background flag, weighted alpha075 default) and cube_summary -> read I,Q,U; compute q0=Q/I, u0=U/I; read P0=PD, PD_err, PA0=PA, MDP99_obs, total effective counts (sum-of-weights I), ONTIME T_obs. For multi-epoch sources combine epochs at the Stokes level with red_ixpe.combine_summaries to get a per-source reference (q0,u0,P0,PA0) (combining ONLY obs reduced with the same subtract_background flag; if a source mixes flags, keep the groups separate). Report P0 and MDP99_obs per source via red_ixpe.pol_report (debiased PD for detections, upper limits for non-detections). DEFINE the three excursion targets per source: P_target in {P0+0.05 (PRIMARY, absolute +5 percentage points), 2*P0, 4*P0}.

STEP 5 - ANALYTIC SENSITIVITY FLOOR vs WINDOW LENGTH (sets the search bin sizes). Using the standard IXPE relation MDP99 = 4.29/(mu*sqrt(N_eff)) and the measured whole-obs MDP99_obs over cleaned exposure T_obs, derive MDP99(T) = MDP99_obs * sqrt(T_obs/T) for a window of livetime T (N_eff scales with livetime at fixed count rate). Per source and per target P_target compute T_min(P_target) = smallest window livetime T for which an excursion to P_target satisfies (P_target - P0) > 3.035*sigma_P(T) with sigma_P(T)=MDP99(T)/3.035 (the >3sigma / MDP99 crossing of the CHANGE relative to steady state). Tabulate T_min for P_target = P0+0.05 (PRIMARY), 2*P0, 4*P0 per source in seconds and in effective counts. Produce: a figure of T_min vs P0 coloured by count rate (one panel per target), and MDP99(T) (equivalently sigma_change(T)) curves per source with horizontal lines at (P0+0.05)-P0=0.05, 2*P0-P0=P0 and 4*P0-P0=3*P0 marking the crossings. This is the headline analytic 'shortest assessable +/-5%-class excursion' map AND it sets the empirical bin sizes in STEP 6.

STEP 6 - EMPIRICAL EXCURSION SEARCH WITH T_min-DRIVEN, MULTI-SCALE WINDOWS (statistics-dominated). Do NOT use an arbitrary fixed bin count. For each obs define a LOGARITHMIC grid of window livetimes W spanning from max(min_T_min over the three targets, ~100 s) up to ~T_obs/8 (e.g. W in {T_min, 2*T_min, 5*T_min, 10*T_min,...} capped so the total PCUBE call budget stays a few thousand across the sample). For EACH scale W: tile the CLEANED [TSTART,TSTOP] into contiguous non-overlapping windows of livetime ~W (build edges in MET seconds; pre-filter empty windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows; intersect each window with the cleaned GTI from STEP 3). For each surviving window make a REAL independent measurement (NOT by scaling a whole-obs cube): red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,8.0], ra, dec, gti=<window intersect cleanedGTI>, obs-specific region and subtract_background flag), then with cube_summary read I,Q,U,Q_err,U_err,PD,PD_err,MDP99 and COMPUTE q_w=Q/I, u_w=U/I by hand (cube_summary has NO q/u keys - reading s['q'] would KeyError-crash the script). Record window ONTIME. For each window compute the Gaussian-plane deviation from steady state D2 = ((q_w-q0)^2+(u_w-u0)^2)/sigma_w^2 with sigma_w = MDP99_w/3.035 (the q,u 1-sigma). Under the no-variability null D2 ~ chi2(2 d.o.f.). Flag a window as a candidate excursion for a given target if PD_w exceeds that target (P0+0.05, or 2*P0, or 4*P0) AND D2 exceeds the per-source/per-scale Bonferroni threshold chi2_2dof(1 - 0.0027/N_trials) (N_trials = total windows searched for that source across all scales). Save the full per-window (scale W, t0,t1,ONTIME,I,Q,U,q_w,u_w,PD_w,PD_w_err,MDP99_w,D2, flag_abs5pct, flag_2x, flag_4x) table as CSV. The SHORTEST scale W at which any real candidate clears detection is the empirical shortest assessable excursion; cross-check it against the analytic T_min from STEP 5.

STEP 7 - CANDIDATE VETTING. For every flagged candidate window: (a) re-extract per-DU with red_ixpe.single_du_file_list for det1,det2,det3 (same window/GTI), compute q,u per DU from I,Q,U and require the excursion be consistent across at least 2 DUs (guards against single-DU artefacts); (b) discard windows with anomalously low livetime fraction (ONTIME/wall-clock-span) to reject count-rate dropouts/occultation; for faint sources additionally re-verify the window is not inside a flare-flagged interval; (c) confirm PD_w stays elevated when the window is shifted by +/-0.5W (robustness to bin phase). Surviving candidates are reported with (q_w,u_w,PD_w+/-err,D2,local significance,ONTIME,count rate,scale W,target type) and a (q,u) protractor plot showing the steady-state contour and the excursion.

STEP 8 - SUMMARY TABLES, UPPER LIMITS, AND DELIVERABLES. Produce: (T1) per-source steady-state P0,PA0,MDP99_obs,count rate (cps/arcmin^2 proxy),T_obs,subtract_background flag, flare-cleaning-applied flag; (T2) the analytic sensitivity map T_min for P0+0.05 (PRIMARY), 2*P0, 4*P0 in seconds and effective counts per source; (T3) the empirical multi-scale results: for each source and each target the SMALLEST realized window livetime at which the excursion WOULD have cleared the per-window MDP99 (cross-checked against analytic T_min from STEP 5, reporting the difference and its significance), and the vetted candidate-excursion list OR, if none survive, a 99% upper limit on the fraction of (cleaned) observing time spent in a P0+0.05 / 2*P0 / 4*P0 PD excursion per source (from the searched windows and their per-window MDP99). Build a comparison table of analytic-vs-empirical T_min per source and target with the difference and its significance. Save all PCUBE products, the per-window CSVs, the flare-GTI files, and all figures. Report detections/upper limits strictly via red_ixpe.pol_report conventions.
