title: The Polarization Variability Spectrum of BH-XRBs: Sensitivity-Calibrated PD/PA Variability on All Timescales Accessible to IXPE
description: This project unifies and supersedes two completed pilots (bhxrb_intraobservation_pa_pd_stability and bhxrb_shortest_pd_excursion_sensitivity) whose central lesson was that IXPE's sensitivity to polarization variability is a steep function of timescale, amplitude, and source brightness: the blind transient-excursion search returned zero vetted detections, but injection-recovery testing showed the search was underpowered for 7 of 8 sources at every searched timescale (a +5 percentage-point excursion is recovered at >=90% only in Cyg X-1 and only for window livetimes >=~26.6 ks), while genuine variability WAS detected on longer timescales: a secure inter-epoch PD rise in Swift J1727.8-1613 (PD consistent with 0 in ObsID 03006001 to 3.4%/5.9 sigma in 03005801, 44 d later), significant per-observation P0 scatter across the 12 Cyg X-1 epochs (2.69% combined, per-obs range ~1.4-4.4%), and a marginal (~2.0 sigma after trials) soft-band-confined intra-observation (q,u) signal in 03006001. Instead of asking the binary question 'are there excursions?', this project measures the polarization variability AMPLITUDE (or its upper limit) as a continuous function of timescale tau -- the polarization variability spectrum -- for every accessible BH-XRB, over ~5 decades of timescale: multi-scale windows within observations (~0.2-100 ks), observation-to-observation within an outburst (days-weeks), and epoch-to-epoch (months-years). Every measured amplitude or upper limit is paired with an injection-recovery-calibrated 90%-recovery threshold A90(tau) computed from the REAL per-window noise, so detections and non-detections are both power-aware, and the sensitivity floor is itself a deliverable. All variability statistics are computed in the normalized Stokes (q,u) plane (Gaussian errors, no PD/PA error-model pathologies), referenced to each observation's OWN mean (per-source referencing is known to manufacture pseudo-excursions from slow inter-epoch drift), with energy-resolved (2-4/4-8 keV) replication and per-DU coherence vetting. NEW RESULT publishable in a peer-reviewed journal: the first systematic, sensitivity-calibrated census of X-ray polarization variability in BH-XRBs on all timescales accessible to IXPE, comprising per-source variability spectra, a detection/upper-limit catalog with state-resolved population comparisons, and a machine-readable sensitivity map for planning future fast-polarimetry searches and observing proposals.
analysis_prescription:
DESIGN PRINCIPLE (read first). Two completed pilots established that (i) binary excursion searches are uninformative below IXPE's amplitude sensitivity floor, and (ii) real BH-XRB polarization variability lives at intra-observation-to-inter-epoch timescales. Therefore EVERY variability statement in this project -- detection or upper limit -- must be reported as an amplitude as a function of timescale tau, side-by-side with the injection-recovery 90%-recovery amplitude A90(tau) measured from the same data. Regions of the (amplitude, tau) plane where A90 exceeds physically plausible amplitudes are labeled 'inaccessible', never 'constant'. All tests are performed in the normalized Stokes plane q=Q/I, u=U/I using time-sliced PCUBE measurements (red_ixpe.pcube with tmin/tmax; NEFF weighting) -- never hand-rolled event-level Q/U -- and every deviation is referenced to the observation's OWN mean (q0,u0) (lesson: per-source referencing turns inter-epoch drift into fake fast candidates).

STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL, INVENTORY, CLEANING. For every (source, obs_id) in targets_and_datasets build the science-grade file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(<archive_root>) (background-filtered *_rej.fits, one per DU). Verify EVERY obs_id is present; if ANY is missing, ABORT and report which. Region defaults (Di Marco 2023): src_rad=1.0 arcmin, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0 arcmin. Record cleaned GTI livetime, count-rate proxy, and 4-8/2-4 keV hardness ratio per observation (hardness tags the spectral state for Step 7).

STEP 2 - PER-OBSERVATION REFERENCES. For each observation run a whole-obs 2-8 keV PCUBE: record (q0,u0) with the full 2x2 covariance, PD, PA, MDP99, N_eff, and detection significance. Also compute per-source combined values (for the inter-epoch tier only, Step 6). Cross-check P0 values against published state-matched IXPE results at matched ObsIDs (comparisons against single published state averages are known to produce spurious >5 sigma discrepancies).

STEP 3 - MULTI-SCALE SEGMENTATION. For each observation build a logarithmic grid of window livetimes (factor ~2 spacing) from the shortest scale at which windows retain N_eff>=200 up to the full observation. HARD VALIDITY GATE: windows with N_eff<200 (chi2_2 p-values formally invalid; PD bias up to tens of pp -- the Cyg X-3 pathology) are excluded from all tests AND from all trials counts. Primary segmentation is equal-livetime; repeat the finest scale with equal-counts segmentation as an aliasing cross-check. Extract per-window q,u with full covariance, per DU and DU-combined.

STEP 4 - INTRA-OBSERVATION TIER (~0.2-100 ks). Per observation and per timescale: (a) robust 2D chi2 constancy test of (q,u) against (q0,u0) using the full covariance; (b) first-order structure functions SF_q(tau), SF_u(tau) with measurement-noise subtraction; (c) normalized excess variance of q and u with uncertainties per Vaughan et al. (2003) conventions adapted to the 2D Gaussian (q,u) case. Deliverable per (obs, tau): intrinsic amplitude sigma_int(tau) or 90% upper limit. Do NOT gate PA-only chi2 tests on anything less than integrated PD/sigma>3 (PA is singular near the q-u origin); the 2D q,u verdict is authoritative.

STEP 5 - ENERGY-RESOLVED REPLICATION. Repeat Step 4 in 2-4 and 4-8 keV sub-bands (lesson: the only surviving intra-observation signal, Swift J1727 03006001, is confined to 2-4 keV and absent at 4-8 keV, indicating a spectral rather than geometric origin). Report band-resolved variability spectra and flag any band-discrepant behavior.

STEP 6 - INTER-OBSERVATION / INTER-EPOCH TIER (days-years). Treat the per-obs (q0,u0) values (Step 2) as an unevenly sampled time series per source: (a) per-source 2D homogeneity chi2 across epochs; (b) pairwise structure function binned in lag from days to years; (c) for Swift J1727.8-1613 reconstruct the time-ordered outburst PD/PA track (03006001 PRECEDES 03005801 by 44 d; the trend is a PD rise consistent with outburst evolution, cf. Ingram et al. 2024); (d) for Cyg X-1 quantify the inter-epoch P0 and PA scatter across the 12 epochs and test whether it exceeds statistical scatter, resolved by spectral state (hardness from Step 1).

STEP 7 - SENSITIVITY CALIBRATION BY INJECTION-RECOVERY (core deliverable). For each source, band, and timescale tier, inject synthetic signals into the REAL per-window (q,u) noise: (a) step excursions of duration T and amplitude dPD on a grid of amplitudes (not only +5pp -- the pilot showed a fixed +5pp target is unrecoverable for 7 of 8 sources; the grid must extend upward until >=90% recovery is reached or the amplitude becomes unphysical, e.g. PD>30%); (b) linear drifts; (c) sinusoids. >=200-400 Monte-Carlo trials per cell; detection logic = the SAME pipeline as Steps 4-6 including the multiple-testing correction and 2-of-3-DU coherence veto. Output: A90(tau) per source per band per signal shape, overplotted on every measured variability spectrum; plus duty-cycle upper limits at scales where A90 is reached.

STEP 8 - VETTING OF ANY CANDIDATE DETECTION. (a) Per-DU coherence: require a coherent (q,u) displacement in >=2 of 3 DUs (the 03006001 signal FAILS this test -- per-DU p_2D all non-significant, cross-DU rho~0.21 -- and must be carried as 'marginal, possibly spectral', not secure); (b) jackknife/leave-one-segment-out; (c) background stability (src/bkg per window; annulus-choice robustness); (d) trials accounting via an effective-trials bootstrap that respects the NESTED window structure, cross-checked against Benjamini-Hochberg FDR; report candidates under both schemes; (e) unnormalized absolute Q,U cross-check to exclude normalization artifacts.

STEP 9 - POPULATION SYNTHESIS. Assemble per-source polarization variability spectra (intrinsic fractional q,u amplitude or UL vs tau, ~200 s to ~2 yr) into a single population figure with A90(tau) sensitivity floors; annotate secure detections (Swift J1727 inter-epoch rise; Cyg X-1 inter-epoch scatter if confirmed) and marginal signals (03006001 soft band). Compare hard vs soft states and wind-fed HMXBs (Cyg X-1, Cyg X-3) vs LMXB transients. Identify, per source, the shortest timescale at which polarization variability is actually detected and the shortest at which it could have been detected (A90 crossing).

STEP 10 - OUTPUTS. (a) Machine-readable catalog CSV: [source, obs_id, tier, band, tau_s, amplitude_or_UL, is_detection, A90, n_windows, N_eff_median, flags]; (b) per-source variability-spectrum figures with sensitivity floors; (c) the population figure; (d) a machine-readable A90(tau, count-rate) sensitivity map for proposal planning; (e) a table of all vetted detections with per-DU, jackknife, background, and trials diagnostics. Every figure caption must state the referencing convention (own-obs mean), the N_eff gate, and the trials correction used.

its downgrade to candidate is driven solely by DU-incoherence and trials (C1/C2), not the sensitivity floor. | Per-source

title: Systematic Study of Q/I and U/I Time Variability on All Accessible Time Scales
description: We perform a uniform, archive-wide chi-squared search for time variability of the normalized Stokes parameters q=Q/I and u=U/I in all archival IXPE black-hole (and BH-candidate) X-ray binary observations, in three energy bands (2-8, 2-4, 4-8 keV) and on a full ladder of timescales: barycenter-corrected 5-min bins within observations, coherent rebinnings to 10/20/30/40/50 min, 1/2/4 hr and day-long bins, and epoch-to-epoch (between observations of the same source), with global trial-factor (look-elsewhere) correction and empirical null calibration. All BH/BH-candidate XRBs in the archive are included — including the SS 433 pointings — because the question (on what timescale does accreting-black-hole X-ray polarization vary) is population-level, and because non-detections must be turned into quantitative excess-variance upper limits on q,u per timescale; Sco X-1 and Swift J0243.6+6124, though listed in the aBH inventory, are physically neutron-star accretors and are excluded by class (stated explicitly in the analysis). The deliverable is new and publishable: no published work presents a homogeneous, trial-corrected, multi-timescale (5 min to years) q,u variability spectrum for the full BH-XRB IXPE archive, with per-source per-timescale intrinsic RMS detections or 95% upper limits that directly confront the reported Cyg X-1 intra-observation constancy (Krawczynski et al. 2022), the orbital-timescale Cyg X-3 modulation (Veledina et al. 2024), and Fourier-domain polarization-variability claims (Ingram & Maccarone-style analyses).
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND INVENTORY. Build the science-grade event file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(DATA_ROOT) (background-filtered *_rej.fits, one per DU per obs). Verify every obs_id in targets_and_datasets is present; exclude unreadable (GPG-encrypted) observations per the exclude_gpg_encrypted_obs recipe, writing exclusions with reasons to results/excluded_obs.csv, and continue with the readable set. State explicitly in the run log and README that Sco X-1 (04010001) and Swift J0243.6+6124 (02250799) appear in the aBH inventory but are EXCLUDED BY CLASS because they are neutron-star accretors, not black-hole binaries; SS 433 (04002899, 04001401, 04004001, 02006799) IS included as a BH-candidate super-accretor. Read and store obs_ids as zero-padded strings everywhere (preserve_obsid_leading_zeros_csv recipe). Resolve source coordinates per observation with red_ixpe.source_coords. Adopt standard regions: src_rad=1.0 arcmin, bkg annulus 2.5-4.0 arcmin. Do NOT hardcode background handling: for each observation, estimate the source count-rate surface density (total events in the *_rej files within the source region divided by exposure from red_ixpe.livetime, divided by the region area in arcmin^2) and set subtract_background=True for faint observations (< 1 cps/arcmin^2, e.g. LMC X-1, LMC X-3, SS 433 and faint transient states) and subtract_background=False for bright ones, per Di Marco 2026. Record the chosen flag per obs in results/obs_config.csv and keep it FIXED for all slices and rebinnings of that observation (the INTER-observation test in STEP 6 uses its own uniform re-reduction; see there). Use weighted (alpha075) analysis throughout (red_ixpe default).

STEP 2 - BARYCENTRIC CORRECTION AND TIME-QUALITY FILTERING. (a) Barycentric correction: for every observation and DU, run HEASoft barycorr on the *_rej.fits Level-2 files BEFORE any time slicing, following the barycorr_multi_orbit_merged_obs recipe exactly: glob ALL *orb*.fits* files under the obs auxil/ and hk/ dirs, decompress them, pass them as one comma-separated orbitfiles string, use the red_ixpe.source_coords (ra,dec), refframe='ICRS', ephem='JPLEPH.405', and ASSERT that output TIME differs from input TIME (raise otherwise). Run barycorr non-interactively (HEADASNOQUERY=1, HEADASPROMPT=/dev/null, clobber=yes; noninteractive_heasoft_ftools recipe). All subsequent time binning, GTI construction and published t0/t1 columns use the barycentered event files, so the 5-min q,u tables carry absolute (TDB) timestamps usable for multi-wavelength cross-correlation. (b) Usable time span: per the gti_bounds_from_event_time_not_header recipe, compute tstart = max over DUs of min(EVENTS TIME) + 1 s and tstop = min over DUs of max(EVENTS TIME) - 1 s from the BARYCENTERED files (header TSTART/TSTOP can sit outside the corrected event range), and clip every window edge into [tstart, tstop]. (c) Solar-flare filtering — BACKGROUND-BASED, NOT SOURCE-BASED, per the phase_time_resolved_pcube recipe: build a DU2 background-region count-rate lightcurve R(t) (events in the 2.5-4.0 arcmin annulus of the DU2 barycentered file, 300 s bins, divided by livetime), compute its median R2 and robust sigma_R2 (1.4826*MAD), and flag every 300 s interval with R(t) > R2 + 3*sigma_R2 as solar-flare contaminated; CUT these intervals from the usable GTI of ALL DUs before any extraction, and log them to results/<obs>_flare_cut_windows.csv. Do NOT apply any source-region flux cuts: real astrophysical flares (GRS 1915+105, Cyg X-3, Cyg X-1) and dips/eclipses (Cyg X-3 orbital eclipses, Cyg X-1 absorption dips) are science signal and must remain in the data. Occultation/SAA gaps need no flux threshold: genuinely empty or near-empty windows are handled by red_ixpe.nonempty_windows (STEP 3), and partially exposed windows are correctly down-weighted by their larger statistical q,u errors in the chi2 tests.

STEP 3 - 5-MIN TIME-BINNED q,u TABLES (FINEST TIMESCALE). For each observation: tile the flare-cleaned usable time span into contiguous 300 s windows, drop empty windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows (min_counts>=1; this is the ONLY event-count-based window rejection), and extract per surviving window TWO independent PCUBEs via red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, tmin=w0, tmax=w1, ...) on the barycentered files per the phase_time_resolved_pcube recipe (NEVER split one whole-obs cube by event fractions): one with ebinning=[2.0, 8.0] (full band) and one with ebinning=[2.0, 4.0, 8.0] (sub-bands). Windows that straddle a flare-cut interval are passed as gti=[(w0,f0),(f1,w1)] sub-window lists rather than dropped. Read the cubes with red_ixpe.cube_summary using an EXPLICIT ebin index per the read_pcube_units_and_bins recipe: cube_summary(cube_full, ebin=0) for 2-8 keV; cube_summary(cube_sub, ebin=0) for 2-4 keV; cube_summary(cube_sub, ebin=1) for 4-8 keV — one band per call. Store to results/<obs>_qu_5min.csv: window index, barycentered MET t0/t1, and per band: I, Q, U, Q_err, U_err, q=Q/I, u=U/I, q_err=Q_err/I, u_err=U_err/I, MDP99. This is a long batch job (~thousands of slices over 1-2 days of wall-clock — acceptable; do NOT trim scope): write ONE checkpoint/resume script per analysis that skips windows whose output rows already exist, run scripts strictly sequentially, and poll sparsely (>=30 min) per the long_runtime_checkpoint_batch and pcube_intermediate_files_keyed_by_band_and_run recipes (key all intermediate filenames by band AND run).

STEP 4 - CHI-SQUARED CONSTANCY TEST AT 5 MIN. For each observation and band (2-8, 2-4, 4-8 keV), fit q(t) and u(t) separately to constant models using inverse-variance weighted means: chi2_q = sum((q_i - <q>_w)^2/q_err_i^2), dof=N-1; likewise chi2_u; joint chi2_qu = chi2_q + chi2_u with 2(N-1) dof (q,u independent Gaussians per the IXPE statistics note). Record chi2, dof, and p-values (scipy.stats.chi2.sf) to results/chi2_master.csv with columns: source, obs_id, band, timescale, N_bins, chi2_q, chi2_u, chi2_qu, p_q, p_u, p_qu. ALL statistical tests operate ONLY on q,u; PD/PA appear only in human-readable summaries (polarization_variability_tests recipe).

STEP 5 - COHERENT REBINNING LADDER. From the SAME 5-min tables (surviving windows only), rebin to coarser timescales: for bin sizes 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 min, 1 hr, 2 hr, 4 hr, and 1 day, group consecutive 5-min windows by floor((t0-tstart)/binsize), sum the extensive Stokes I, Q, U per group with errors in quadrature, and recompute q, u and their errors — use red_ixpe.combine_summaries on the per-window summary dicts of each group (per band, keeping the three bands separate; this is exactly the correct Stokes-level combination algebra). Require >=2 populated coarse bins per (obs, band, timescale) to run a test. Repeat the STEP-4 chi2 constancy tests for every (obs, band, timescale) and append to chi2_master.csv. Note in the outputs that rebinned timescales derive from the same events and are therefore correlated (handled in STEP 7).

STEP 6 - INTER-OBSERVATION (LONG-TIMESCALE) VARIABILITY. For each source with >=2 observations and each band: extract one whole-observation PCUBE per obs (full flare-cleaned time span, same two ebinning runs and explicit ebin reads as STEP 3), take cube_summary, and run the same chi2 constancy test on the per-epoch q,u (joint chi2 with 2(N_obs-1) dof). CRITICAL CONSISTENCY RULE: for this inter-observation test, force a SINGLE, UNIFORM subtract_background choice across ALL epochs of a given source — use subtract_background=False for every epoch of any source that has at least one bright epoch (e.g. Swift J1727.8-1613, whose outburst decay crosses the 1 cps/arcmin^2 threshold), and subtract_background=True uniformly only for sources faint in ALL epochs (e.g. LMC X-3, SS 433). Re-extract whole-obs cubes with this uniform flag where it differs from the STEP-1 per-obs choice; record the uniform choice per source in results/obs_config.csv. Record MJD midpoints via red_ixpe.get_mjd so the sampled inter-observation baselines (days to years) are documented per source. Append rows with timescale='inter-obs' to chi2_master.csv, all three bands. For Cyg X-1 and Swift J1727.8-1613 additionally report the epoch pair with the most significant q,u difference (2-D Gaussian test on (dq,du) with combined errors).

STEP 7 - GLOBAL EVIDENCE ASSESSMENT WITH TRIAL FACTORS. (a) Per (source, band, timescale): combine per-observation p_qu values with Fisher's method (chi2 = -2 sum ln p, dof=2*N_obs) into a combined per-timescale p-value. (b) Trial-factor correction: count the ACTUAL number of executed tests N_trials (sources x bands x timescales x {q,u,joint}); report (i) Bonferroni-corrected p_corr = min(1, p*N_trials) and (ii) Benjamini-Hochberg FDR ranking at FDR=0.05 across all tests, explicitly stating that rebinned timescales share events so Bonferroni over timescales is conservative. (c) Empirical null calibration: for each (obs, band), recompute the 5-min chi2 statistic on 1000 surrogate constant series drawn from the measured per-window errors and confirm the null distribution matches the analytic chi2; flag any (obs, band) where it is miscalibrated (systematic error underestimation), inflate that observation's q,u errors by the calibration factor, and re-run its tests before claiming detections. Note this calibration checks STATISTICAL error validity only; astrophysically real polarized contamination (solar flares) is removed upstream by the STEP-2 background-based cuts. Output results/global_evidence.csv and a matrix figure per band (source x timescale, color=-log10 p_corr).

STEP 8 - VARIABILITY AMPLITUDE CHARACTERIZATION (DETECTIONS AND UPPER LIMITS). For every (source, obs or inter-obs ensemble, band, timescale): compute the normalized excess variance of q and u, sigma_XS^2 = S^2 - <err^2>; when positive quote the intrinsic RMS sqrt(sigma_XS^2) in fractional units and x100 in percentage points, with its uncertainty. For non-detections derive a 95% upper limit on the intrinsic RMS by scanning an added variance sigma_int^2 into the chi2 statistic until the observed chi2 falls at the 5th percentile of the chi2 distribution with the appropriate dof (implement with scipy.stats.chi2). Tabulate to results/variability_amplitudes.csv: source, obs_id/ensemble, band, timescale, FDR detection flag, sigma_XS or 95% UL for q and for u. This is the publication-ready product turning both positive AND negative results into numbers (e.g. 'Cyg X-1 intrinsic q RMS < X pp at 5 min; epoch-to-epoch q varies by Y +/- Z pp').

STEP 9 - FINAL REPORT AND LITERATURE COMPARISON. Produce per-source summary pages: q,u time-series plots at 5-min and 1-hr binning with constant-model lines; p-value vs timescale curves per band; the amplitude/UL spectrum vs timescale ('polarization variability spectrum'); and a human-readable conclusion translating significant q,u variability into PD (percent, 0-100) and PA (degrees, -180 to +180) language using red_ixpe.pol_report on each observation's mean cube_summary. Write results/literature_comparison.csv with one row per published quantitative claim, columns: source, literature claim (stated quantitatively), reference, this-work quantity (detection or UL from STEP 8), difference/agreement significance. Populate at minimum: (1) Cyg X-1: Krawczynski et al. 2022 report PD=4.01+/-0.20% and PA=-20.7+/-1.4 deg with no significant intra-observation variability in May+June 2022 — compare to this work's 5-min-to-day ULs and epoch-to-epoch variability for obs 01002901/01250101 and the 2023-2024 epochs; (2) Cyg X-3: Veledina et al. 2024 report a high average PD (~20-25%) with strong orbital/temporal PD and PA variability — compare to this work's intra-observation chi2 detections and amplitudes for the Cyg X-3 obs; (3) 4U 1630-47: Ratheesh, Rodriguez Cavero et al. 2023 report a high (~8%) steady PD in the soft state — compare to this work's intra- and inter-obs variability constraints for 01250401/02250601. Save everything under results/ with a master README describing every file.

decision_matrix.outcome: No significant intra-observation q,u variability (trial-corrected) in Cyg X-1 and other hard/soft-state persistent BH-XRBs on 5 min - 1 day timescales; 95% ULs on intrinsic q,u RMS of order <1 pp at hour timescales.
decision_matrix.favored_model: Krawczynski et al. (2022, Science) picture of a stable, extended (equatorial) coronal geometry in Cyg X-1 with constant PD/PA over the observation.
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Rapid stochastic geometry-fluctuation scenarios of the type the Ingram & Maccarone (2017, MNRAS) polarimetry-timing method was designed to detect, i.e. large short-timescale PA/PD wander.
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: IXPE BH-XRB observers and modelers needing quantitative stability limits (e.g. corona-geometry papers building on Krawczynski et al. 2022; future eXTP/polarimetry-timing proposals).

decision_matrix.outcome: Significant, trial-corrected intra-observation q,u variability detected in specific sources/timescales (e.g. Cyg X-3 on hours, matching its 4.8-hr orbit; Swift J1727.8-1613 across its outburst decay), with measured intrinsic RMS amplitudes.
decision_matrix.favored_model: Veledina et al. (2024, Nature Astronomy) orbital/temporal polarization modulation in Cyg X-3 and state-driven polarization evolution reported for Swift J1727.8-1613 (Ingram et al. 2024; Podgorny et al. 2024).
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: The assumption of strictly constant within-observation polarization implicit in whole-observation-averaged analyses (e.g. single-epoch polconst fits) for those sources.
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: The Cyg X-3 and Swift J1727 IXPE teams; anyone performing phase- or state-resolved follow-up; population studies of polarization variability.

decision_matrix.outcome: Intermediate: no intra-observation variability anywhere, but significant inter-observation (epoch-to-epoch) q,u changes in multi-epoch sources (Cyg X-1, LMC X-3, Swift J1727.8-1613).
decision_matrix.favored_model: Slow, state/precession-driven polarization evolution — e.g. the spectral-state dependence of Cyg X-1 polarization reported by the IXPE team follow-ups to Krawczynski et al. (2022) and the outburst-evolution results for Swift J1727.8-1613 (Ingram et al. 2024).
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Both fast stochastic variability scenarios (Ingram & Maccarone 2017 regime) and strictly time-invariant geometry across states.
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: BH-XRB state-transition modelers and long-term monitoring campaigns coordinating IXPE with X-ray all-sky monitors.

decision_matrix.outcome: Null everywhere including epoch-to-epoch for a given source, with tight ULs (e.g. LMC X-3 q,u constant to <0.5 pp over years).
decision_matrix.favored_model: Stable-disk interpretations of soft-state polarization (Steiner et al. LMC X-3 IXPE analyses; standard constant-geometry disk picture underlying Krawczynski et al. 2022).
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Precession/warp-driven PA drift scenarios invoked for disk-dominated systems (e.g. Lense-Thirring precession interpretations discussed in the Ingram & Maccarone 2017 framework).
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: Disk-atmosphere polarization modelers and anyone stacking multi-epoch IXPE data who must justify epoch combination.

title: Systematic Study of Q/I, U/I Time Variability on All Accessible Time Scales
description: We perform a uniform, archive-wide chi-squared search for time variability of the normalized Stokes parameters q=Q/I and u=U/I in ALL archival IXPE observations of accreting neutron-star systems and related accreting compact binaries in the provided inventory (Z/atoll NS-LMXBs, accreting X-ray pulsars such as Her X-1, Cen X-3, Vela X-1, SMC X-1, 4U 1538-52, the magnetar 1E 2259+586, the IP EX Hya, AMXPs, and the transitional pulsar PSR J1023+0038) — 45 sources, 89 observations. For each barycenter-corrected observation we build q(t), u(t) tables in 2-8, 2-4 and 4-8 keV on 5-min bins from independent per-slice PCUBEs, chi-squared-test against constant models, rebin the SAME Stokes sums (keeping ALL slices, with quality cuts applied only to the final evaluated bin at each scale) to 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 min, 1, 2, 4 hr and 1 d timescales and repeat, then test inter-observation variability per source; all results are combined per source, band and timescale with explicit trial-factor accounting, and non-detections are converted into intrinsic q/u variability-amplitude upper limits so both positive and negative outcomes are publication-ready. The 5-min-and-longer clock-time bins probe orbital/super-orbital and stochastic variability; second-scale spin modulation is explicitly OUTSIDE the reach of these bins and is instead handled by a dedicated spin-phase positive-control step (barycorr + xpphase + phase-GTI PCUBEs) for Her X-1. Expected new, publishable results: the first timescale-resolved (5 min to years) census of X-ray polarization variability across the full NS/accreting-pulsar IXPE archive, a trials-corrected re-assessment of published variability claims (Cir X-1 rapid PA rotation, Rankin et al. 2024; epoch-dependent Z-source polarization, Farinelli et al. 2023), and quantitative amplitude constraints for ~45 sources — a catalog paper for ApJ/A&A.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND INVENTORY. Build file_list = red_ixpe.get_all_file_list(DATA_ROOT) (yields background-rejected *_rej.fits Level-2 files, one per DU per obs). Verify every obs_id in the target table has usable files; apply the exclude_gpg_encrypted_obs recipe: record any unreadable obs to excluded_obs.csv with the reason and drop it (and any then-empty source block) from scope rather than aborting. Store all obs_ids as zero-padded 8-char strings (preserve_obsid_leading_zeros_csv recipe). For each surviving obs record livetime (red_ixpe.livetime), MJD start/mid/stop (red_ixpe.get_mjd), and source coordinates (red_ixpe.source_coords). Output: analysis_inventory.csv.

STEP 2 - BARYCENTRIC CORRECTION. Before any time-slicing, run HEASoft barycorr on every per-DU _rej.fits file following the barycorr_multi_orbit_merged_obs recipe: collect ALL *orb*.fits files from the obs auxil/ and hk/ dirs, decompress them, pass them as a single comma-separated orbitfiles string, use the source ra/dec, refframe=ICRS, and run non-interactively (HEADASNOQUERY=1, HEADASPROMPT=/dev/null, clobber=yes; noninteractive_heasoft_ftools recipe). ASSERT that output TIME differs from input TIME; if barycorr cannot be made to run for an obs, record it in barycorr_status.csv and fall back to uncorrected times for that obs (flagging every downstream product), since within-observation chi2 constancy tests are insensitive to the smooth <500 s barycentric drift — but inter-observation and spin-phase steps REQUIRE the corrected files. Use the barycentered file set for all subsequent steps. Time-window bounds must come from the actual event TIME extent across all DUs, not header TSTART/TSTOP (gti_bounds_from_event_time_not_header recipe): tstart = max over DUs of min(TIME)+1 s, tstop = min over DUs of max(TIME)-1 s.

STEP 3 - GLOBAL REDUCTION SETTINGS AND PER-SOURCE BACKGROUND POLICY. Regions: src_rad=1.0 arcmin, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0 arcmin, weighted analysis (red_ixpe defaults). Energy binning: run pcube ONCE per selection with ebinning=[2.0,4.0,8.0]; the 2-4 and 4-8 keV results are cube_summary(cube, ebin=0) and ebin=1, and the 2-8 keV broadband result is formed by red_ixpe.combine_summaries([summary_24, summary_48]) — the two sub-bands are disjoint event sets from the same selection, so their Stokes sums add exactly and the broadband q,u,sigma_q,sigma_u used in every chi2 test are EXACT. Caveat to record in the catalog: the broadband MDP99 from combine_summaries is an inverse-quadrature approximation (per the authoritative recipe, exact MDP99 requires binning all events into one cube); since MDP99 is descriptive only here and enters no statistical test, report it flagged as 'approx'; additionally, for each WHOLE observation (not the time slices) run ONE dedicated ebinning=[2.0,8.0] extraction to tabulate the exact broadband MDP99 for the final catalog. Background policy is set DYNAMICALLY per observation with a weight-corrected threshold: from the whole-observation cube compute the source-region proxy rate_w=(I_24+I_48)/(livetime*pi*src_rad^2) (I = sum of event weights; label as such). Mean alpha075 weight ~0.25, so the Di Marco 2026 true-count-rate threshold of 1.0 cps/arcmin^2 corresponds to rate_w~0.25: set subtract_background=False if rate_w>=0.25, else True (genuinely faint sources, e.g. X Persei, 4U 1954+319, PSR J1023+0038). For obs within a factor 2 of the boundary (0.125<=rate_w<0.5) cross-check with a TRUE count rate: read raw EVENTS rows of each DU _rej.fits inside the source circle and 2-8 keV (astropy.io.fits, PI-to-keV per header), compute counts/livetime/area summed over DUs, and decide against the 1.0 threshold with that. Record the choice and both rates in analysis_inventory.csv and use it CONSISTENTLY for every slice, rebin, and combination of that source. ALSO in this step, for each obs, extract per-DU raw background-annulus COUNT light curves (raw counts in the 2.5-4.0 arcmin annulus, 2-8 keV, 300 s bins, via astropy.io.fits on the barycentered files) — these raw count rates, NOT weighted I sums, feed the Step-8 solar-flare veto. Run every long loop as ONE checkpoint/resume batch script per step, strictly sequentially, per-(obs,window) checkpoint files, sparse polling >=30 min (long_runtime_checkpoint_batch recipe); NEVER reduce scope for runtime. Key all intermediate filenames by obs+band+run (pcube_intermediate_files_keyed_by_band_and_run recipe).

STEP 4 - 5-MINUTE Q/I, U/I TABLES (WITHIN-OBSERVATION, SHORTEST SCALE). For each observation: tile the clamped usable span into contiguous 300 s windows; drop empty windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows. For each surviving window call red_ixpe.pcube(obs, file_list, ebinning=[2.0,4.0,8.0], tmin=w0, tmax=w1, ra=ra, dec=dec, src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=<per-obs policy>) — ONE extraction per window (phase_time_resolved_pcube recipe; never split a whole-obs cube by event fractions). Read the src cube with red_ixpe.cube_summary for ebin=0 (2-4 keV) and ebin=1 (4-8 keV); form the 2-8 keV summary via combine_summaries of the two. cube_summary does NOT return sigma_q/sigma_u or effective counts — compute EXPLICITLY: q=Q/I, u=U/I, sigma_q=Q_err/I, sigma_u=U_err/I, N_eff=(I/I_err)^2. Store per window and band: t_mid (MET and MJD), I, Q, U, I_err, Q_err, U_err, q, u, sigma_q, sigma_u, N_eff, PD, PA, MDP99, livetime_window. CRITICAL: store ALL windows, including low-count ones — do NOT delete any 5-min summary; instead add a boolean flag use_5min = (N_eff>=50). The N_eff>=50 Gaussianity cut is applied ONLY at test-evaluation time at each timescale, never at storage time, so rebinning (Step 6) can recover valid photons from low-flux 5-min slices. Output: one CSV per obs, qu_5min_<obs>.csv, plus the discard-flag fraction per obs.

STEP 5 - CHI-SQUARED CONSTANCY TEST AT 5 MIN. For each obs and band (2-8, 2-4, 4-8 keV), using only windows with use_5min True, fit q(t) and u(t) separately to constant models: qbar = sum(q_i/sigma_q_i^2)/sum(1/sigma_q_i^2); chi2_q = sum((q_i-qbar)^2/sigma_q_i^2), dof=N-1; same for u. Joint statistic chi2_qu = chi2_q+chi2_u with 2(N-1) dof (q,u independent Gaussians, IXPE statistics note). Record chi2, dof, reduced chi2, p-value (scipy.stats.chi2.sf). ALL statistics on q,u only — never on PD/PA (polarization_variability_tests recipe); PD/PA appear only in the narrative. Output: chi2_5min_summary.csv (one row per obs x band x statistic).

STEP 6 - REBIN TO LONGER WITHIN-OBSERVATION TIMESCALES. Rebin the SAME data by combining the 5-min slice Stokes sums: for each target width in {600, 1200, 1800, 2400, 3000, 3600, 7200, 14400, 86400} s, group ALL consecutive 5-min windows (including those flagged use_5min=False — every stored slice participates) whose midpoints fall in the same coarse bin and combine with red_ixpe.combine_summaries (sums extensive I,Q,U, propagates errors — never scale by event fractions; recompute q,u,sigma_q,sigma_u,N_eff from the combined summary). Apply the N_eff>=50 quality cut ONLY to the resulting coarse bin. Require >=2 surviving coarse bins to run a test. Repeat Step-5 chi2 tests for every (obs, band, bin-width). Output: qu_multiscale_<obs>.csv plus chi2_multiscale_summary.csv (columns: obs, source, band, binwidth_s, N_bins, chi2_q, chi2_u, chi2_qu, dof, p_q, p_u, p_qu).

STEP 7 - INTER-OBSERVATION VARIABILITY. For each source with >=2 observations (Cyg X-2 x23, Her X-1 x5, 4U 1538-52 x5, GX 13+1 x4, GX 349+2 x3, Cir X-1 x3, SMC X-1 x3, Cen X-3 x2, GRO J1008-57 x2, GX 340+0 x2, LS V+44 17 x2, XTE J1701-462 x2): form each whole-observation per-band summary by combine_summaries over ALL that obs's stored 5-min slice summaries (no new extraction; same settings and same background policy across the source — combine like with like), and chi2-test the per-epoch (q,u) against the weighted constant model exactly as in Step 5 (dof=2(N_obs-1) joint). Also tabulate the maximum pairwise epoch separation in the (q,u) plane in units of the combined sigma, and the epoch MJDs so the probed timescale (days to years) is explicit. Mark single-obs sources 'inter-obs unconstrained'. Output: chi2_interobs_summary.csv.

STEP 8 - TRIAL FACTORS, VETOES, GLOBAL EVIDENCE. Count N_trials of chi2 tests, broken down per source, band, timescale. The rebinned timescales reuse the same events, so within an obs the tests across bin widths are NOT independent: report (a) raw per-test p-values, (b) Bonferroni over ALL tests p_global=min(1,N_trials*p), and (c) Bonferroni over the independent axes only (obs x band), treating the timescale scan as one search with p_min as the statistic, bounded by the Sidak formula p_scan=1-(1-p_min)^N_scales. Declare 'significant variability' where the corrected p<0.01. For every significant case run two vetoes BEFORE accepting: (i) solar-flare/background veto using the Step-3 RAW background-annulus COUNT rates (not the weighted I_bkg proxy — flare particle tracks have unpredictable alpha075 weights): flag 300 s windows whose raw background count rate exceeds the per-obs mean+3 sigma, excise them, and re-run the test; note explicitly that this is a fallback post-hoc veto on already background-rejected L2 files (the authoritative recipe cuts flares BEFORE background rejection, which needs L1 reprocessing unavailable here), so residual contamination can only be flagged, not fully removed. (ii) per-DU consistency — repeat the affected test per DU via red_ixpe.single_du_file_list; require the signal in all DUs (a single-DU signal is instrumental). For sources with known ORBITAL or super-orbital periods (Her X-1 35 d/1.7 d, Cen X-3 2.087 d, 4U 1538-52 3.73 d, Vela X-1 8.96 d, Cyg X-2 9.84 d, 4U 1820-303 685 s, ...), annotate significant within-obs detections whose dominant timescale is commensurate with those periods as expected orbital/super-orbital modulation. Do NOT claim second-scale SPIN periods are detectable in >=300 s bins — they average out; spin-phase sensitivity is delivered ONLY by Step 9. Output: global_evidence_table.csv and a per-source verdict table.

STEP 9 - SPIN-PHASE POSITIVE CONTROL (PIPELINE VALIDATION). To validate the polarimetric pipeline against a known variable signal, run ONE dedicated spin-phase-resolved analysis on Her X-1 (obs 01001899, P_spin~1.24 s, published phase-swinging PA, Doroshenko et al. 2022): using the barycentered files from Step 2, run ixpeobssim xpphase with the published Her X-1 spin ephemeris for that epoch to add a PHASE column (xpphase has NO --bary switch — barycentering must already be done; ixpeobssim_app_option_crib recipe), then extract 7 spin-phase-bin PCUBEs in 2-8 keV via xpselect --phasemin/--phasemax followed by red_ixpe-style cube extraction (or red_ixpe.pcube with phase-derived GTIs per the phase_time_resolved_pcube recipe), and chi2-test the per-phase (q,u) against constancy exactly as in Step 5. Recovering significant spin-phase (q,u) modulation consistent in PA-swing amplitude with Doroshenko et al. 2022 validates the whole chain; failure to recover it must be reported as a pipeline FAILURE, not approximated.

STEP 10 - VARIABILITY-AMPLITUDE CHARACTERIZATION (POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE RESULTS). For each (source, band, timescale): noise-subtracted excess variance S2_q=max(0, var_w(q)-<sigma_q^2>) (weighted sample variance), intrinsic amplitude sigma_intr=sqrt(S2); same for u. For non-detections derive a 95% upper limit on sigma_intr: find the sigma_intr for which the chi2 survival probability of the observed chi2 given dof + sigma_intr^2*sum(1/sigma_i^2) equals 0.05 (standard excess-variance UL, scipy.stats.chi2). Convert amplitudes to equivalent PD-variability in percentage points for reporting (PD in %, PA in deg — unit_and_naming_conventions recipe). Output: variability_amplitude_table.csv (source, band, timescale, N, sigma_intr_q, sigma_intr_u or 95% UL, equivalent dPD_pp).

STEP 11 - FINAL SYNTHESIS, FIGURES, LITERATURE COMPARISON. Produce: (1) master table per source x band x timescale of chi2 p-values (raw and trial-corrected) and amplitude constraints; (2) 'variability spectra' figures (matplotlib): sigma_intr or UL arrows vs timescale (5 min to inter-epoch), per source, per band; (3) (q,u)-plane epoch trajectories for multi-epoch sources (23-epoch Cyg X-2 campaign, Cir X-1, Her X-1); (4) a comparison table 'this-work value vs published value vs difference/significance' for the published variability claims: Cir X-1 within-obs PA rotation (Rankin et al. 2024), Cyg X-2 polarization (Farinelli et al. 2023), Her X-1 spin-phase polarization swing (Doroshenko et al. 2022, from Step 9). Write the final report using red_ixpe.pol_report wording for every detection/upper limit; state explicitly per source whether variability is detected (with corrected significance and amplitude) or constrained (with the UL), so every entry is publication-ready.

decision_matrix.outcome: Significant (trials-corrected p<0.01) within-observation q/u variability on hours-to-day timescales in Z-sources (Cyg X-2, GX 5-1, GX 340+0, Cir X-1), correlated with position on the Z track / epoch, while atolls (GX 9+9, GS 1826-238, 4U 1820-303) remain constant with tight ULs
decision_matrix.favored_model: Rankin et al. (2024, ApJL) and Fabiani et al. (2024): Z-source polarization varies with accretion state/branch, implying a changing scattering geometry (spreading layer/boundary layer reconfiguration)
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Farinelli et al. (2023) static-geometry interpretation of Cyg X-2 in which a single stable PD/PA describes the source across an observation
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: The NS-LMXB IXPE community (Farinelli, Fabiani, La Monaca, Ursini groups) debating whether Z/atoll polarization tracks the accretion branch; observers planning IXPE Cyg X-2 monitoring (the 2025-2026 23-epoch campaign PIs)

decision_matrix.outcome: No significant within-observation variability anywhere after trial correction; 95% upper limits on intrinsic sigma(q), sigma(u) of <~0.5-1% on 5-min to day timescales for the bright Z/atoll sources
decision_matrix.favored_model: Farinelli et al. (2023) and Ursini et al. (2023): NS-LMXB polarization is set by a stable global geometry (disk + spreading layer) and is steady within epochs
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Rankin et al. (2024) style rapid intra-observation polarization evolution as a generic property of bright NS-LMXBs (rather than an exceptional episode)
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: Anyone stacking IXPE NS-LMXB data across an observation (the standard practice) — the ULs quantitatively justify or bound the error of time-averaging; theorists modeling spreading-layer stability

decision_matrix.outcome: Inter-observation (epoch-to-epoch) q/u variability is significant for multi-epoch sources (Her X-1 35-d superorbital phases, Cir X-1 2023 vs 2025, GX 13+1, 23-epoch Cyg X-2) while within-observation tests are null — variability confined to >~days timescales
decision_matrix.favored_model: Doroshenko et al. (2022) / Heyl et al. (2024) free-precession and superorbital-phase-dependent geometry picture for Her X-1, generalized: geometry changes on precession/orbital timescales, not stochastically
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Stochastic short-timescale scattering-medium variability (turbulent corona/wind) as the driver of polarization changes in these systems
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: The Her X-1 precession debate (Doroshenko, Heyl, Garg) and the Cir X-1 evolving-jet/disk community; proposal writers arguing for repeated IXPE visits rather than single deep stares

decision_matrix.outcome: Intermediate: variability detected only in the 4-8 keV band (or only 2-4 keV) at fixed timescales, with the other band constant
decision_matrix.favored_model: Two-component polarization pictures (e.g. La Monaca et al. 2023 for Sco X-1; Farinelli et al. 2023 disk+SL decomposition) where only the harder Comptonized/spreading-layer component varies
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Single-component (energy-independent, polconst-like) polarization interpretations of these sources
decision_matrix.who_cites_this: Spectro-polarimetric modelers decomposing NS-LMXB polarization into disk vs spreading-layer/reflection components (Ursini, Farinelli, Gnarini/Capitanio groups)

statistical_methods_justification_note: Legacy analysis project, no information for this field (record predates statistical_methods_justification, adopted 2026-09-19 from Maitreya's schema).
conclusions: For the 2 available observations, normalised Stokes q(t),u(t) are consistent with constant on every within-observation timescale from 5 min to 1 day, in all bands (Cyg X-2 5-min 2-8 keV chi2_qu=750.5/726, p=0.257; X Persei chi2_qu=898.5/854, p=0.141). The smallest raw p across 66 trials (Cyg X-2 2-4 keV, 6.4e-4) is not significant after trial correction (Bonferroni p_global=0.043). Whole-observation polarization: Cyg X-2 PD=1.46%+/-0.22% at PA=-50 deg (secure, 6.6 sigma); X Persei a non-detection (PD<4.47% 3-sigma UL). 95% upper limits on intrinsic q,u variability amplitude are ~2-4 percentage-points PD-equivalent for Cyg X-2. Failure reason: Only 2 of 87 prescribed observations (from 2 of 43 prescribed sources) are present and readable on disk; 4 are missing from the inventory and 81 have empty event_l2 directories (including all GPG-encrypted files). The archive-wide multi-source census, inter-observation variability (Step 7), the 23-epoch Cyg X-2 campaign, and the Her X-1 spin-phase positive control (Step 9) cannot be performed without the data. Real within-observation multiscale q/u variability analysis (Steps 3-6, 8, 10, 11) was completed for the 2 available observations.

title: Polarization Reverberation: Lagged Stokes-Flux Cross-Correlation in Bright BH-XRBs
description: We measure, for the first time, whether the X-ray polarization state of bright black-hole X-ray binaries responds to flux and spectral-hardness changes instantaneously or with a measurable delay (10^2 - 2x10^4 s), by computing discrete lagged cross-correlation functions (DCFs) between time-sliced normalized Stokes parameters (rotated into a PA-parallel signal channel q' and a PA-perpendicular null channel u') and the simultaneous flux, hardness ratio, and cross-band polarization series, on barycenter-corrected event times. The three brightest IXPE BH-XRBs (Cyg X-1, Swift J1727.8-1613, Cyg X-3; 24 observations) are used because only they provide per-bin sigma_q small enough for lag work; fainter BH-XRBs (4U 1630-47, GRS 1915+105, GX 339-4, LMC X-1/X-3, 4U 1957+11) are deferred as a documented scope decision. This is the polarimetric analogue of Fabian-style X-ray reverberation mapping in the timescale regime IXPE photon statistics permit (explicitly NOT the ms GR-reverberation regime). Publishable new results are guaranteed in every branch: a zero-lag detection ties polarization to the corona at intra-observation timescales; a nonzero lag is the first detection of 'polarization reverberation' from an extended scatterer at c*tau ~ 10^12-10^13 cm; a cross-band Stokes lag is the polarimetric analogue of a reflection lag; and a calibrated null yields the first upper limits on lagged polarization-flux covariance versus timescale, a benchmark for eXTP-class polarimetry-timing. No published IXPE paper reports a polarization-flux lag measurement or limit.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND REDUCTION SETUP. Build the master event-file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list over the local Level-2 archive; verify all 24 obs_ids listed above are present (handle obs_ids as zero-padded 8-character strings throughout, dtype=str with .zfill(8) for any catalog reads; exclude any GPG-encrypted/unreadable obs per the exclusion recipe and record the exclusion). Resolve per-observation coordinates with red_ixpe.source_coords. Regions everywhere: circular source radius 1.0 arcmin, background annulus 2.5-4.0 arcmin; all three sources are bright, so subtract_background=False in ALL pcube calls. ORDER OF TIME-DOMAIN OPERATIONS (fixes the frame-mismatch trap): (1a) SOLAR-FLARE SCREENING IS DONE FIRST, IN ORDINARY (NON-BARYCENTERED) MET, ON THE RAW FILES: the _rej.fits files returned by get_all_file_list are already background-rejected, so the flare diagnostic must come from the raw det2 Level-2 file (the event_l2 file WITHOUT '_rej' in its name; decompress .gz to a scratch dir if needed). Apply the spatial background-annulus selection EXPLICITLY: read the EVENTS extension with astropy, convert the sky pixel columns (X, Y with their TCRVL/TCDLT/TCRPX WCS keywords, or RA/DEC columns if present) to angular offset from the source_coords position, and keep only events with 2.5 arcmin <= offset <= 4.0 arcmin (this Python spatial masking replaces any region tool; do NOT bin a full-detector light curve). Bin the masked events into a 100 s light curve, flag bins with rate > mean + 3*sigma (iterate the clipping twice), and record the flagged intervals as a per-observation BAD-time list in ordinary MET. The clean GTI (in ordinary MET) is the complement of the bad intervals within the observation span. (1b) BARYCENTRIC CORRECTION SECOND: run HEASoft barycorr (non-interactively, HEADASNOQUERY=1, HEADASPROMPT=/dev/null, clobber=yes) on every DU _rej event file of every observation, following the barycorr_multi_orbit_merged_obs recipe - collect ALL *orb*.fits files from the obs auxil/ and hk/ dirs, decompress them, pass them as one comma-separated orbitfiles string, use the source_coords RA/Dec, refframe=ICRS, and ASSERT that output TIME differs from input TIME (raise if unchanged). (1c) FILE-LIST HANDOFF (critical): after barycorr, EXPLICITLY REBUILD the working file list so that every _rej path is REPLACED by the path of its barycentered output file (e.g. bary_file_list = [bary_path(f) for f in file_list]); ALL subsequent red_ixpe.pcube / cube extractions in STEPS 2-3 MUST be passed this bary_file_list, never the original file_list. Verify the substitution by asserting that every path handed to pcube contains the barycentered-output naming tag. (1d) TRANSLATE THE CLEAN GTI INTO THE BARYCENTRIC FRAME: for each observation compute the per-DU mapping between raw and barycentered TIME (the barycorr delta varies by <1 s over any 100 s window, so map each clean-GTI edge t to t + delta(t), where delta(t) is interpolated from matched raw/barycentered event TIME pairs or from the barycorr correction evaluated at t); the resulting barycentric clean GTI is what all later steps intersect against. (1e) USABLE SPAN: per the gti_bounds_from_event_time_not_header recipe, compute the usable time span per observation from the actual barycentered event TIME extent across all three DUs (tstart = max over DUs of min(TIME) + 2 s; tstop = min over DUs of max(TIME) - 2 s) and clip every window into that span. API CONSTRAINT: red_ixpe.pcube treats tmin/tmax and gti as MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE; ALL time-sliced extractions pass their time selection EXCLUSIVELY via gti= (per-slice gti = intersection of [t0,t1] with the barycentric clean GTI, computed in Python as a list of (start,stop) intervals; never pass tmin/tmax together with gti).

STEP 2 - FULL-OBSERVATION SANITY BENCHMARKS. For each observation extract a full-observation broadband (ebinning=[2.0, 8.0]) PCUBE with red_ixpe.pcube on the bary_file_list (time selection = the full barycentric clean GTI via gti=); read PD/PA/MDP99 via red_ixpe.cube_summary(cube, ebin=0) and red_ixpe.pol_report (feed pol_report the NATIVE fractional summary; for reporting, PD in percent = fraction*100, PA in degrees). Write table sanity_pdpa_per_obs.csv comparing mean broadband PD/PA against published values: Krawczynski et al. 2022 for Cyg X-1 obs 01002901/01250101 (~4.0%, ~-20 deg), Ingram et al. 2024 / Podgorny et al. 2024 for Swift J1727.8-1613 hard-state epochs, and published Cyg X-3 values (~20% PD, Veledina et al. 2024). CCFs are only trusted for observations whose benchmark agrees within errors; disagreements are flagged and investigated (region/GTI) before proceeding.

STEP 3 - TIME-SLICED STOKES SERIES. For each observation and each of TWO bin sizes (200 s and 2000 s for Cyg X-3 and Swift J1727.8-1613; 500 s and 2000 s for Cyg X-1), build contiguous slice edges spanning the clamped usable span (np.clip of all edges into that span; never derive the first edge from an unclipped event-TIME min), pre-filter empty windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows (on the bary_file_list), and extract ONE independent PCUBE per slice from real events with ebinning=[2.0, 3.5, 8.0] on the bary_file_list, passing gti = intersection([slice_t0, slice_t1], barycentric clean GTI) as the ONLY time-selection argument; skip slices whose intersected GTI is empty or whose total GTI duration is < 25% of the bin size. NEVER scale a whole-observation cube by event fractions (phase_time_resolved_pcube recipe). RUNTIME ECONOMY (do NOT extract a second broadband cube per slice): read the soft band with red_ixpe.cube_summary(cube, ebin=0) and the hard band with cube_summary(cube, ebin=1) (two separate calls; cube_summary takes a single integer ebin), then FORM THE BROADBAND 2-8 keV SLICE VALUES IN PYTHON by summing the extensive Stokes quantities: I_bb = I_s + I_h, Q_bb = Q_s + Q_h, U_bb = U_s + U_h, with errors in quadrature (Q_bb_err = sqrt(Q_s_err^2 + Q_h_err^2), etc.) - this is exactly the combine-at-the-Stokes-level rule of the combine_obs_and_per_du recipe and requires NO extra PCUBE call. API CONSTRAINT ON ERRORS: cube_summary returns {I, Q, U, Q_err, U_err, PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err, MDP99} - no sigma_q/sigma_u keys; compute q = Q/I, u = U/I, sigma_q = Q_err/I, sigma_u = U_err/I per band (and for the summed broadband values). Form the flux proxy per slice and band as I divided by the slice's ACTUAL exposure = the summed duration of the intersected GTI intervals of that slice (computed in Python from the interval list) - do NOT use red_ixpe.livetime for slices (it reads the full-observation header livetime). Since cube_summary provides no I_err, estimate sigma_flux = sqrt(I)/exposure (Poisson-like proxy on the sum-of-weights I); label both the proxy and its error explicitly as sum-of-weights quantities, not true count rates. Build HR(t) = hard-band rate proxy / soft-band rate proxy with error propagated in quadrature. For Cyg X-3, tag every slice midpoint (barycentered time) with binary orbital phase using P_orb = 0.19968443 d (17252.7 s) and T0(MJD, superior conjunction / X-ray minimum) = 40949.392, phase = frac((MJD_mid - T0)/P_orb); the linear ephemeris is adequate for artifact-flagging purposes only. Checkpoint per (obs_id, bin size) unit: write slice tables stokes_series_<obs>_<bin>s.csv and skip units whose outputs exist. Run strictly sequentially - no concurrent PCUBE jobs sharing obs_ids or scratch dirs; sparse polling >= 30 min; never reduce scope for runtime (stop and report if scope reduction seems needed).

STEP 4 - PA-FRAME ROTATION. Per observation compute the mean broadband PA psi0 (degrees) from the STEP-2 full-observation cube. Rotate every per-slice (q,u) pair (all bands, including the Python-summed broadband) into (q',u') with q' = q*cos(2*psi0) + u*sin(2*psi0), u' = -q*sin(2*psi0) + u*cos(2*psi0), so q' is the PD-parallel signal component (concentrating any physical PD response, doubling effective CCF S/N) and u' is the PD-perpendicular NULL channel (any flux x u' correlation flags PA variability or systematics). Errors carry over unchanged (sigma_q' = sigma_q, sigma_u' = sigma_u for the isotropic Gaussian q,u errors). All correlation statistics are performed on q',u' (normalized Stokes) - never on PD/PA; PD/PA appear only in conclusions for readability.

STEP 5 - LAGGED DISCRETE CROSS-CORRELATIONS. Per observation and per bin size, compute the Edelson & Krolik (1988) discrete correlation function (DCF; handles IXPE orbital data gaps without interpolation) over trial lags tau = -20 ks to +20 ks with lag resolution equal to the bin size, for three families: (a) flux(t) x q'(t) [broadband 2-8 keV]; (b) HR(t) x q'(t); (c) cross-band q'_soft(t) x q'_hard(t) AND u'_soft(t) x u'_hard(t). Duplicate the FULL set with u' replacing q' as the null-channel control. Implement the DCF with per-pair mean subtraction and measurement-error correction in the normalization: subtract the mean measurement-noise variance from the total variance of each series before normalizing (for q'/u' use per-bin sigma_q/sigma_u from STEP 3; for flux use sigma_flux; for HR its propagated error; if the noise-corrected variance is non-positive, fall back to the uncorrected normalization for that unit and flag it). Note the practical ceiling that a lag is only measurable up to ~1/3 of the usable span; short Cyg X-1 epochs (20-35 ks) constrain only |tau| <= ~10 ks while the long anchors (Cyg X-1 01002901 ~241 ks, Cyg X-3 02001899 ~275 ks, Swift J1727 03005801 ~202 ks) probe the full +/-20 ks cleanly; record the usable lag range per observation.

STEP 6 - SIGNIFICANCE CALIBRATION. For every (observation, bin size, CCF family, channel) unit, build the null distribution of peak-DCF amplitude and peak lag by block bootstrap / block shuffling of the same series (block length >= 10 bins, chosen to preserve short-timescale autocorrelation), PRESERVING the observation's exact gap pattern and per-bin measurement errors (shuffle blocks of the response series against the fixed driver time grid; also generate Gaussian-noise realizations of q',u' from their per-bin sigmas as a second null). >= 1000 realizations per unit. Report the peak lag with 68% and 99% intervals when the peak amplitude exceeds the 99th percentile of the null; otherwise report the 99% upper limit on lagged polarized covariance vs timescale. Artifact flagging: any DCF feature at the IXPE orbital gap cadence (~5.7 ks) or, for Cyg X-3, at the 17.3 ks binary period (or harmonics) is flagged as a sampling/orbital artifact in artifact_flags.csv; a candidate lag must survive the gap-preserving bootstrap AND not coincide with a window/orbital timescale. Also compute the DCF of the window function (constant signal on the same time grid) as an explicit window-artifact template.

STEP 7 - STACKING AND STATE ENSEMBLES. Stack (inverse-variance-weighted average) DCFs across epochs within each source on the common lag grid (coarse 2000 s grid for cross-epoch stacking). For Cyg X-1 and Swift J1727.8-1613 classify epochs as hard or soft state by mean HR, and form hard-state vs soft-state ensemble DCFs. Compare fine-bin vs coarse-bin DCFs for consistency (peak amplitude and lag agreement within errors). Recompute significance of stacked DCFs by stacking the bootstrap realizations identically.

STEP 8 - DELIVERABLES AND COMPARISON TABLES. Write: (i) dcf_results_master.csv - per observation, bin size, CCF family, and channel (q' signal / u' control): DCF peak amplitude, peak lag, bootstrap significance, 68%/99% lag intervals or covariance upper limit; (ii) stacked per-source and per-state DCF plots with bootstrap confidence bands (matplotlib, PDF); (iii) artifact_flags.csv (features at 5.7 ks / 17.3 ks); (iv) decision_matrix_verdict.txt - per source, which outcome (a)-(e) of the decision matrix was realized; (v) comparison_prior_work.csv - zero-lag DCF amplitudes here vs the zero-lag correlation coefficients of the existing bhxrb_intensity_stokes_correlation_survey and bhxrb_flux_hardness_polarization_correlation projects where sources overlap, plus the STEP-2 PD/PA benchmark comparison vs published values (this-work value vs reference value vs difference and its significance); note explicitly that the q-vs-u rotation search of bhxrb_intraobs_qu_lag_crosscorr is NOT re-run (its PA-stability null motivates the q'/u' frame) and that the Fourier polarimetry-timing regime (Ewing, Ingram & Maccarone) is distinct; state that the ms-s GR-reverberation regime is out of reach; (vi) REQUIRED plain_language_summary.txt (<= 300 words, non-scientist readable) using the mandated renderings - zero lag: 'the polarization flickers in lockstep with the brightness - the polarized light comes from right beside the black hole'; nonzero lag tau: 'we caught an echo: the polarization responds tau seconds after the brightness, so some X-rays bounce off gas about c*tau kilometers away - we measured the size of an invisible structure'; cross-band lag: 'higher-energy polarized light arrives later than lower-energy - different energies come from different places'; null: 'no echo found; we now know how faint any echo must be, setting the bar for future missions'; u' signal: 'either the polarization direction wobbles after all, or we found an instrument quirk - both worth reporting'. Convert every reported lag to a light-travel distance (km and light-seconds) and every limit to %-polarization change per flux doubling; if a nonzero lag is detected, compare c*tau against published wind/funnel scales for Cyg X-1 / Cyg X-3 (~10^12-10^13 cm).

decision_matrix.outcome: Significant DCF peak at zero lag (|tau| < one bin) between flux/hardness and q' (PD-parallel Stokes), surviving the gap-preserving bootstrap, with clean u' control
decision_matrix.favored_model: Instantaneous corona-polarization coupling: 'PD tracks spectral state' picture of Ingram et al. 2024 and Podgorny et al. 2024 (Swift J1727.8-1613) and Krawczynski et al. 2022 (Cyg X-1), extended for the first time to intra-observation timescales
decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Delayed polarized reprocessing in an extended scatterer (companion wind / outer disk light-crossing at ~10^12-10^13 cm), as invoked in wind-scattering interpretations of Cyg X-3 polarization (Veledina et al. 2024 funnel geometry with extended reflector)

decision_matrix.disfavored_model: Purely compact, instantaneous corona-dominated polarization (Krawczynski et al. 2022; Ingram et al. 2024 zero-delay assumption)

decision_matrix.favored_model: Energy-stratified polarized response — polarimetric analogue of X-ray reflection lags (Fabian-style reverberation, e.g. Fabian et al. 2009 / Uttley et al. 2014 framework) applied to polarization

decision_matrix.who_cites_this: IXPE methods/calibration papers and polarimetry-timing methodology papers (Ingram & Maccarone framework)

conclusions: No significant polarization-flux (or hardness-polarization, or cross-band Stokes) lag was detected in any of the three brightest IXPE BH-XRBs across 24 observations and 276 DCF units. Decision-matrix outcome (d) applies to all three sources: calibrated 99% upper limits on lagged polarization-flux covariance (median flux x q' limits: Cyg X-1 3.23, Swift J1727 4.91, Cyg X-3 2.41). Full-observation PD/PA benchmarks reproduce published values for the canonical epochs (Cyg X-1 ~3.5-4.4% at PA~-20deg; Cyg X-3 ~20% for 02001899/02009101); two Cyg X-3 epochs at ~10-11% PD are honestly flagged as real epoch-to-epoch variability. The 3 of 276 units above the 99% null threshold are consistent with chance (~2.8 expected) and coincide with orbital-gap artifact timescales. This is the first quantitative benchmark on lagged polarization-flux covariance vs timescale for IXPE BH-XRBs.

title: Rotated-Frame Q/I, U/I Constancy Limits in BH-XRBs Across Three Bands
description: Prior IXPE results suggest that BH-XRB polarization DEGREE can vary while the polarization ANGLE stays fixed (Swift J1727.8-1613 PD decline at constant PA, Veledina et al. 2023/2024; stable jet-aligned PA in Cyg X-1, Krawczynski et al. 2022). We test this cleanly in well-behaved Stokes space across the full archival BH-XRB sample (32 observations, 10 sources): per observation and per energy band (2-4, 4-8, and Stokes-summed 2-8 keV), we rotate 5-ks time-binned normalized Stokes points (q_i,u_i) into the frame of the band's mean polarization vector, so that variability of the parallel component q_par corresponds to PD variation at fixed geometry and the perpendicular component q_perp to PA wander; constant-model chi-squared fits on a factor-of-2 timescale ladder (5 ks to T_obs/4, built by Stokes co-addition) yield either FDR-controlled detections with debiased excess-rms amplitudes or 99%-confidence detectable-rms upper limits for EVERY obs x band x timescale x component cell. New, publishable results: (i) the first mean-vector-frame par/perp decomposition of intra-observation BH-XRB polarization variability, (ii) sensitivity-calibrated detectable-amplitude curves vs timescale (a citable atlas of PA-wander sigma_psi limits in degrees, e.g. constraining precession amplitudes in Cyg X-1 and per-epoch q_par limits in Swift J1727.8-1613), and (iii) band-resolved (disk 2-4 keV vs Comptonization 4-8 keV) localization of any detected variability.
analysis_prescription:
STEP 1 - DATA RETRIEVAL AND DATA-HEALTH PREFLIGHT GATE. Build the file list with red_ixpe.get_all_file_list over the local Level-2 archive for all 32 obs_ids listed in targets_and_datasets (handle unreadable/GPG-encrypted obs per the exclude_gpg_encrypted_obs recipe: record and drop, do not abort). Read obs_ids as zero-padded strings throughout (dtype=str, .zfill(8)). For each observation, per the data_health_preflight_gate recipe: (a) sky counts image (DUs summed, log stretch) with the exact source circle (r=1.0 arcmin at red_ixpe.source_coords position) and background annulus (2.5-4.0 arcmin) overlaid; (b) source and background count-rate light curves (300 s bins) with the flare threshold (median + 3*1.4826*MAD of the background rate) drawn and cut intervals shaded; (c) gate CSV with obs_id, exposure, whole-obs background-subtracted I/sigma_I, bkg fraction, n flare-cut intervals, and verdict PASS/FAIL (PASS requires I/sigma_I >= 5 and visible detection). Save the flare-free GTI (list of MET (start,stop) intervals with flare intervals excised) per observation for reuse in STEP 3. Write preflight_gate.csv and an exclusions table (results/exclusions.csv) for FAILs with reasons; FAILED observations never enter downstream statistics, figures, or claims. State one sentence per observation about what was seen before proceeding.

STEP 2 - WHOLE-OBSERVATION PCUBES AND ROTATION FRAMES. For each PASS observation, extract ONE two-bin weighted PCUBE with red_ixpe.pcube(ebinning=[2,4,8], src_rad=1.0, bkg_inner_rad=2.5, bkg_outer_rad=4.0, subtract_background=False for bright sources per the Di Marco 2026 recipe; enable subtraction only for genuinely faint sources < ~1 cps/arcmin^2 — apply the SAME choice consistently to that observation's STEP 3 time slices). Read each sub-band with red_ixpe.cube_summary (ebin=0 -> 2-4 keV, ebin=1 -> 4-8 keV); obtain the 2-8 keV band by Stokes-summing the two sub-band summaries with red_ixpe.combine_summaries — no separate broadband extraction. Report each band via red_ixpe.pol_report fed with the NATIVE fractional-unit summary (debiased PD for detections, Pi < Pi0 + 3*sigma upper limits otherwise; convert to PD in percent and PA in degrees only for the report tables). Record per-band mean (q_bar, u_bar), PA psi_bar, fractional PD, PD/sigma, MDP99, and assign the frame-quality flag: PD/sigma >= 5 -> 'frame secure', else 'rotation frame poorly defined'. Write whole_obs_summary.csv.

STEP 3 - 5-KS TIME-BINNED PCUBES (CHECKPOINT/RESUME BATCH). For each PASS observation: determine the usable time span from the ACTUAL EVENT TIME arrays, NOT the header keywords (per the gti_bounds_from_event_time_not_header recipe): open all three DU event files, read EVENTS['TIME'], and set tstart = max over DUs of min(TIME) + 2 s, tstop = min over DUs of max(TIME) - 2 s. Tile 5000-s bin edges across [tstart, tstop] and clip every edge into that interval so no xpselect window can fall outside the physical event bounds of any DU; pre-filter empty windows with red_ixpe.nonempty_windows. Flare handling WITHOUT discarding whole bins: for each 5-ks bin, intersect [tmin, tmax] with the flare-free GTI from STEP 1 (each GTI interval also clipped into [tstart, tstop]) and pass the resulting interval list to red_ixpe.pcube(gti=..., ebinning=[2,4,8]) (use tmin/tmax only when the bin contains no flare interval); drop a bin only if its flare-free livetime falls below 50% of 5 ks. Regions/weighting identical to STEP 2. For each surviving bin store per band: t_mid, effective livetime, I, sigma_I, Q, U, Q_err, U_err, q=Q/I, u=U/I, and the NORMALIZED per-bin error sigma_i = Q_err/I (verify Q_err/I ~ U_err/I; use their mean). sigma_I handling: cube_summary may lack an I_err key — recover sigma_I from the cube's I variance/error array (xBinnedPolarizationCube accessor, confirm at runtime) or, failing that, use the counting proxy sigma_I = sqrt(sum of squared event weights) ~ I/sqrt(N_eff) consistent with the weighted cube; never assume the key exists. Run this as ONE checkpoint/resume batch script (skip windows whose output CSV rows already exist), sequential execution, sparse polling (>=30 min), intermediate files keyed by obs+band+window index; never reduce scope for runtime. Window cleaning per band: drop bins failing I/sigma_I >= 5 or |q|,|u| <= 1 (drop_low_significance_qu_windows recipe). Write per-obs qu_timeseries_<obs>_<band>.csv.

STEP 4 - TIMESCALE LADDER BY STOKES CO-ADDITION. Per obs and band, rebin the 5-ks summaries to 10, 20, 40, ... ks (factors of 2) by summing Stokes I, Q, U of adjacent surviving bins with red_ixpe.combine_summaries (never scale a cube by event fractions); stop the ladder when fewer than 4 bins remain (max timescale ~ T_obs/4). At each timescale store the (q,u) series and the per-bin normalized error sigma_i = Q_err/I from the combined summaries.

STEP 5 - ROTATION INTO THE MEAN-VECTOR FRAME. Per band, rotate every time-binned (q_i, u_i) by -2*psi_bar(band) from STEP 2 so the whole-obs mean vector lies on +q: q_par_i = q_i*cos(2*psi_bar) + u_i*sin(2*psi_bar), q_perp_i = -q_i*sin(2*psi_bar) + u_i*cos(2*psi_bar). The normalized per-bin error sigma_i (defined in STEPs 3-4 as Q_err/I ~ U_err/I) is isotropic in the (q,u) plane and therefore carries over unchanged to (q_par, q_perp). Each band uses its OWN frame (PA may rotate with energy).

STEP 6 - CONSTANCY FITS, FDR, AND SENSITIVITY LIMITS. For each obs x band x timescale x component (q_par, q_perp): weighted constant-model fit using the normalized sigma_i; chi2, dof=N-1, p-value from scipy.stats.chi2.sf. Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (alpha=0.05) across the FULL obs x band x timescale x component grid. Where variable post-FDR: report the debiased excess rms amplitude sqrt(max(0, sample_var - mean(sigma_i^2))) with a bootstrap uncertainty. Where constant: report the 99%-confidence detectable rms amplitude — the rms_add such that the expected chi2 with variance sigma_i^2 + rms_add^2 exceeds the 99th-percentile chi2 threshold for N-1 dof (solve numerically with scipy.optimize.brentq) — as the upper limit. Convert q_perp amplitudes/limits (fractional units) to PA-wander sigma_psi in DEGREES using red_ixpe.pa_error_deg(pd, sigma) with the FRACTIONAL whole-obs band PD (not percent) and sigma = the fractional q_perp amplitude/limit — do NOT hand-roll limit/(2*PD)*180/pi with a percent PD; do this ONLY where the band's frame flag is secure. For poorly-defined-frame cases quote instead a combined 2-D (q,u) excursion limit from the joint chi2 on (q,u) with 2(N-1) dof (rotation-invariant, so valid regardless of frame). All statistics on q,u / rotated components only; PD/PA appear only in reporting.

STEP 7 - DELIVERABLE PLOTS AND TABLES. (a) Per source x band: detected amplitude / 99% upper limit vs probed timescale (5 ks to T_obs/4), separate q_par and q_perp curves (matplotlib, log-log); where only upper limits exist this IS the headline figure. (b) Per observation x band: q_par(t) and q_perp(t) 5-ks time series with per-bin error bars and the constant-fit line; SINGLE panel unless a data gap exceeds 2x the bin width (10 ks), in which case one panel per contiguous stretch with empty x-ranges cut out; y-axis fixed to mean +/- 3x the sample standard deviation of plotted values. (c) Summary table summary_constancy.csv: obs_id, band, N bins, chi2/dof and p for par and perp, FDR verdict, detected rms or 99% limit, sigma_psi limit (deg) or 2-D limit, frame-quality flag — one row for EVERY obs x band x timescale, no empty outcomes. (d) Exclusions table from STEP 1.

STEP 8 - LITERATURE AND PRIOR-PROJECT COMPARISON TABLE. Build comparison_table.csv: (i) Cyg X-1 01002901+01250101 combined (combine_summaries) whole-obs 2-8 keV PD/PA vs Krawczynski et al. 2022 (PD ~ 4.0+/-0.2 %, PA ~ -20.7+/-1.4 deg): this-work value, reference value, difference and its significance in sigma; state explicitly whether the derived q_perp constancy limits (sigma_psi per timescale) are consistent with the reported stable jet-aligned PA and quote the tightest sigma_psi limit achieved. (ii) Swift J1727.8-1613 decay epochs 02250901-02251301: state whether WITHIN-observation q_par variability is detected on 5 ks-T/4 timescales or whether the Veledina et al. PD decline is purely inter-epoch, quoting the per-epoch q_par amplitude limits. (iii) A short text block contrasting with prior database projects (bhxrb_multiscale_qu_chi2_variability: detector-frame q,u, no direction info; bhxrb_pa_swing_amplitude_brightness_census: ill-behaved PA space) and stating the three new contributions: mean-vector-frame par/perp decomposition, sensitivity-calibrated detectable-amplitude curves vs timescale, band-resolved localization of variability.

conclusions: [claims register v14; 22 active, 5 superseded/retracted] Across 34 PASS observations of 10 BH-XRBs, intra-observation polarization is consistent with constant in the mean-vector (par/perp) frame under a per-bin CONSTANT-fit test on the independent 5-ks rung: over 360 obs x band x timescale cells (720 component tests, result_026), 20 tests have raw p<0.01 (7.2 expected) and 5 have p<0.001 (0.72 expected) (result_181). The Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the 204 INDEPENDENT 5-ks tests leaves 0 survivors (result_062). Primary statement: no bin-to-bin (uncorrelated) polarization jitter on 5-40 ks time scales survives a trials correction over the 204 independent 5-ks tests; and 0 of 28 observations show a u' slope beyond 3 sigma (result_147 slope scan, 174 tests). The only two Bonferroni survivors over all 720 tests (both 4U 1630-47 01250401 q', 80/160-ks rungs) and one marginal LMC X-1 02001901 2-4 keV 40-ks cell are NOT bin-to-bin jitter: the 4U 1630-47 pair is the coarse-rung signature of a slow, coherent 4.9 sigma LINEAR RISE of q' in 01250401 (slope (3.253+/-0.662)e-5/ks, Delta-chi2=24.2, present in all three DUs; see C26 and result_147/159), and the LMC X-1 cell is unexplained but not trials-robust (record 3.62 sigma uninflated / 2.89 sigma pooled / 3.74 sigma component-aware, fails Bonferroni-720 and the 204-independent test, result_188/172). The five top p<0.001 cells are all q' and belong to the C26 trend and the C27 2-4 keV excess (result_181). Rounding check: all 720 tests satisfy |p_recomputed - p_022| within the stored 3-decimal chi2 rounding (result_181 p_rounding_check). The primary 5-ks constant-fit test has no power against such a monotonic drift.
